verdict.title: Global 500ms damage lockout hard-caps ALL incoming damage at 2 hits/sec — simultaneous strikes collapse to one, and a 1-dmg poke swallows a 60-dmg boss slam
verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED (mechanism + player impact real; stated magnitude INFLATED ~4x)
verdict.reason: MECHANISM REPRODUCED with my own vitest probe against the REAL useGameStore (not the claim's): 5x damagePlayer(10) => hp 90 (one hit landed); 10 hits @100ms => trace 90,90,90,90,90,80,80,80,80,80 — character-for-character identical to the claimed output. Not fabricated. LINE IS REAL: useGameStore.jsx:747 is verbatim `if (now - state.lastDamageTime < 500) return;` (grepped on HEAD). Cited test soft-death-protections.spec.js:41 exists and calls it "the cooldown" — the guard IS deliberate. NOT FIXED: `git log -- frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx` last touch = 114e5a6, 2026-06-28; today's fixes (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) touched different files. NEW EVIDENCE THE CLAIM MISSED: (a) P3 probe — damagePlayer(1,'weak-zombie') then damagePlayer(60,'BOSS SLAM') => hp 99: the big hit is eaten ENTIRELY; there is no damage-overflow carve-out. (b) EnemyProjectileSystem.jsx:42 `for (let i=0;i<hits;i++) damagePlayer(15,'projectile')` — a 3-arrow volley on one frame deals 15, not 45; the loop is a no-op past iteration 0. (c) BossEntity.jsx:420 Burning Lava ticks 6 dmg on its OWN 500ms timer, phase-colliding with the global lock, so it can swallow the Shadow Dragon's Bite (BossEntity.jsx:262) / Shockwave (:308). WHERE THE CLAIM IS INFLATED: its "a horde of 20 is exactly as dangerous as 1 mob" is refuted by the worker's own constants — ai.worker.js:130 ATTACK_COOLDOWN=1500 plus WINDUP_MS=380 (line ~277) = a 1880ms per-mob cycle = 0.53 hits/sec, against a 2 hits/sec cap. A staggered pack therefore lands ~3.8x a solo mob, not 1x. "N mobs = 1 mob" holds ONLY for a same-tick synchronized volley (which does occur — AIWorkerSystem.jsx:35 drains all attacks from one 15Hz tick, and zustand `set` is synchronous so call 2..N see the updated lastDamageTime and early-return).
verdict.real_player_impact: REAL, and reachable in normal play through three live damage paths. Honest magnitude (correcting the claim's 4x overstatement): incoming damage is hard-capped at 2 hits/sec, i.e. roughly 3.8 melee mobs' worth of DPS — so every attacker beyond ~4 concurrent contributes EXACTLY ZERO. A 20-mob siege is ~4x a lone zombie, not 20x; ~80% of a horde's swings are deleted (and the mob still burns its own 1500ms cooldown on the swallowed swing, so the damage is gone, not deferred). Worse in practice than the pure rate cap: because the lockout is armed by whichever hit arrives FIRST regardless of size, chip damage shadows burst damage — a 1-dmg zombie poke fully absorbs a 60-dmg boss slam, and boss Burning Lava (6 dmg on its own 500ms cadence) can swallow the Shadow Dragon's heavy attacks during the game's climax fight. Multi-arrow skeleton volleys likewise collapse to a single 15-dmg hit. Net: crowd control, positioning and kiting have sharply reduced mechanical value, and boss burst is unreliable — consistent with open task #19 ("enemies must feel dangerous"). NOT dead code, NOT theoretical. Severity: HIGH on mechanism is defensible but slightly generous; MEDIUM-HIGH is the honest grade, since the guard is an intentional Minecraft-style i-frame and the true ceiling is ~4 mobs rather than 1. The actionable defect is that the i-frame is GLOBAL across all sources with NO damage-overflow carve-out (a larger hit arriving during the window should deal the difference, or the window should be per-source), not that the i-frame exists at all.

verdict.title: Camera shake decays PER FRAME, not per second — identical crit shake lasts 1067ms @30fps vs 267ms @120fps
verdict.reason:
Independently reproduced with my own vitest probe (not the claimant's) replaying the real Components.jsx:1221-1239 block against the real useGameStore + real shakeOffset from src/game/trauma.js. Result: a crit (trauma=1.6) always takes exactly 32 frames to decay below the 0.01 cutoff, regardless of dt — 30fps=1066.7ms, 60fps=533.3ms, 120fps=266.7ms. The unused decayTrauma(rate=1.5) gives 666.7ms at all three framerates.

file:line is real and verbatim. `git show HEAD:frontend/src/Components.jsx | sed -n '1236p'` => `store.triggerCameraShake(trauma * 0.85); // Decay`. It sits inside `useFrame((state, delta) => {` opened at Components.jsx:515, and `delta` IS in scope — it is used 4 lines later at line 1240 (`const kick = stepKick(kickRef.current, delta);`). So delta was available and simply not used.

NOT already fixed: `git log -3` = 1386b5e / 45778e7 / a8c7b71, all docs-only commits. `git status --short frontend/src/Components.jsx` returns empty (working tree == HEAD). No commit in `git log -8 -- frontend/src/Components.jsx frontend/src/game/trauma.js` touches the shake decay.

Supporting context independently verified (not fabricated): cameraKick.js:48 really is delta-correct (`const f = Math.exp(-decay * Math.max(0, delta));`); AIWorkerSystem.jsx:155 really does contain the "120Hz ProMotion iPads no longer pay double" comment; `grep -rn "decayTrauma\|addTrauma" src/` shows consumers ONLY in src/game/trauma.test.js — the correct function is genuinely dead code.

Reachability verified: the only early-returns in useFrame above line 1236 are isCaptureMode (521), void-fall (818), world-not-built (825), spawn-retry (845/856) — all bypassed in normal play. No fps cap on the game canvas (`frameloop` only appears in TitleDiorama.jsx:63, and is 'always' outside capture mode).
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, a player experiences this on every hit. src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx:60 calls triggerCameraShake(isCrit ? 1.6 : 1.0, hitDir[0], hitDir[2]) on every player melee hit; EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:136, HurlSystem.jsx:62 and BossEntity.jsx:296/385 also drive it. The shake therefore lasts ~1067ms on a 30fps laptop and ~267ms on a 120Hz ProMotion iPad — a 4x swing in the duration of the single most-felt piece of combat juice, on a device the project explicitly targets. It also means shake duration silently stretches whenever framerate dips mid-fight.

ONE CORRECTION to the claim's framing: it says the shake is "4x weaker" on 120Hz. That is FALSE, and the claim's own evidence contradicts it (its table shows peak offset 0.956 identical at all three framerates; my probe agrees — amplitude is set by trauma^2 and the per-frame trauma sequence is identical at every fps). The defect is 4x SHORTER duration, not 4x weaker amplitude. "Nauseating" is rhetoric.

SEVERITY: the claim says HIGH; honest tier is MEDIUM-HIGH. The bug is real, reachable, and player-felt, but it is game-feel/polish — not a crash, data-loss, or correctness defect. It does not block play.

FIX NOTE: wiring the dead decayTrauma() naively would change the feel curve (it is LINEAR, the shipped decay is EXPONENTIAL; and triggerCameraShake SETS rather than adds, so crits pass 1.6, outside decayTrauma's implicit 0..1 domain). The tuning-preserving fix is `trauma * Math.pow(0.85, delta * 60)`, which is exactly today's curve at 60fps but framerate-independent.

verdicts_joined.title: EnemyProjectileSystem's multi-arrow damage loop is dead code -- 3 arrows deal 15 damage, not 45
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/systems/EnemyProjectileSystem.jsx:42 (`if (damagePlayer) for (let i = 0; i < hits; i++) damagePlayer(15, 'projectile');`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The author wrote an explicit loop over `hits` -- the intent is unambiguous: N arrows landing in one frame should deal N x 15. Every iteration after the first is a guaranteed no-op, because damagePlayer's 500ms lockout (useGameStore.jsx:747) rejects it. The loop is either a silent bug or dead code; either way the source reads as if volley damage works and it does not. Nothing tests this: stepEnemyProjectiles has a behavioral test, but the damagePlayer call site it feeds has NONE.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Probe P2 (vitest, REAL useGameStore):
  3 x damagePlayer(15) => playerHealth = 85   (would be 55 if all land)
Only the first of the three iterations mutated health.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: An archer volley (multiple Bonepickers) is no more threatening than a single arrow. Ranged enemies cannot ever be a real threat by massing, which is the only threat model archers have.
verdicts_joined.domain: Combat: melee, damage, telegraphs, hitstop, dodge, i-frames

verdict.title: EnemyProjectileSystem's multi-arrow damage loop is dead code -- 3 arrows deal 15 damage, not 45
verdict.reason:
Mechanism REPRODUCED (claim did not fabricate): vitest probe vs REAL useGameStore -> 3x damagePlayer(15,'projectile') = playerHealth 85, with only ONE [hit] log for three calls. Cited file:line is real and still on HEAD (EnemyProjectileSystem.jsx:42, untouched since 780bb15; NOT fixed). stepEnemyProjectiles can genuinely return hits=3. So iterations 2..N are dead.

But the claim misattributes the cause, and the player-impact gate fails on two executed probes:

(1) EQUIVALENCE probe, N=1..5: loop-of-N and a SINGLE damagePlayer(15) produce byte-identical player state every time (hp 85, alive true, for all N). Deleting the loop changes NOTHING observable. There is no behavioral delta for a player to experience.

(2) CADENCE probe: the 500ms gate (useGameStore.jsx:747) also rejects arrows arriving in SEPARATE frames <500ms apart; two arrows >500ms apart deal FULL damage (hp 70). The lockout is a cadence, not a mute.

The 500ms gate is global damage infrastructure, not a projectile quirk: all 7 damagePlayer call sites route through it (BossEntity.jsx:262/308/381/423 boss bite/shockwave/fireball/lava, AIWorkerSystem.jsx:54 melee, useGameStore.jsx:816 starvation, EnemyProjectileSystem.jsx:42); BossEntity.jsx:420 re-implements its own parallel 500ms guard; and the dodge i-frame system (dodge.js:46, Components.jsx:906) is built on it. No other damage source loops -- the loop is the outlier, not the lockout.

Granted sub-claim: enemyProjectiles.test.js covers the stepper, and the damagePlayer call site has no test. But an untested no-op is still a no-op.
verdict.real_player_impact:
NONE. Removing the loop entirely yields identical player-observable state (proven for N=1..5), so no player can perceive any difference between current code and the "fixed" code.

The claim's stated impact -- "an archer volley is no more threatening than a single arrow; ranged enemies cannot ever be a real threat by massing" -- is caused by the INTENDED global 500ms i-frame that governs every damage source in the game, NOT by the dead loop. Making the loop deal 45 would burst damage straight through the invulnerability window that every other system (boss, melee, lava, dodge) honors: that is a balance change against a deliberate design invariant, not a bug fix. Massed archers still apply real sustained pressure at the 500ms cadence (two arrows >500ms apart = 30 damage, verified).

Severity MEDIUM is INFLATED. Correct classification: cosmetic dead-code/redundancy nit -- the loop misleads a reader into thinking volley damage stacks. Honest fix is to DELETE the loop (or comment that the global i-frame caps hits at one per 500ms). The claim's own hedge ("either a silent bug or dead code") concedes this, then prices it as if it were the former.

verdicts_joined.title: The hitstop weight hierarchy collapses to 'crit' for any geared player -- the exact gap the feature was built to close
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx:39 (`const weight = damage >= 40 ? 'crit' : damage >= 30 ? 'heavy' : 'light';`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The tiering was added specifically because "a flat 28ms collapsed the light/heavy/crit hierarchy -- the audit's #1 game-feel gap" (comment at CombatSystem.jsx:35). But the thresholds are ABSOLUTE damage numbers (30/40) that never scale with weapon or level, while melee damage is `baseWeaponDmg + strength*1.5`. Equip an Iron Sword and every non-crit already crosses 30; equip a Diamond Sword and every single swing crosses 40. The same `damage >= 40` value is also the `isCrit` proxy driving camera-shake magnitude (1.6 vs 1.0) and spark count -- so all three feedback channels saturate together.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Probe P16 (vitest, REAL solveMeleeDamage + REAL getWeaponBaseDamage + REAL HITSTOP table, CombatSystem:39 tier fn verbatim):
  weapon=Wooden Sword  base=5  | str10: nonCrit=20(light/45ms) crit=40(crit/130ms)
  weapon=Iron Sword    base=20 | str10: nonCrit=35(heavy/90ms) crit=70(crit/130ms) | str20: nonCrit=50(crit/130ms)
  weapon=Diamond Sword base=35 | str10: nonCrit=50(crit/130ms) crit=100(crit/130ms) | str40: nonCrit=95(crit/130ms)
With a Diamond Sword, EVERY hit at EVERY strength is tier 'crit'.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: By mid-game every swing punches identically -- max hitstop, max shake, max sparks. A lucky crit feels exactly like a routine poke, and progression makes combat feedback WORSE (mushier, less legible), not better. The light/heavy/crit hierarchy exists only for a level-1 player holding a wooden sword.
verdicts_joined.domain: Combat: melee, damage, telegraphs, hitstop, dodge, i-frames

verdict.title: Hitstop/shake/spark weight tiers collapse to 'crit' as soon as the player equips iron — the exact hierarchy the feature was built to create
verdict.reason: Tried to refute; could not. (1) REPRODUCED end-to-end, not by re-typing the tier line: mounted the real CombatSystem (jsdom + @testing-library/react), spawned a real ECS mob, drove the real Components.jsx:248-256 pipeline (getWeaponBaseDamage -> solveMeleeDamage -> resolveFormMelee) and called the REAL GameMethods.damageMob, then read the resulting useGameStore hitstopUntil. Measured (baseStr=10, non-crit forced via Math.random stub): unarmed 20dmg -> light/45ms; Stone Sword 33 -> heavy/90ms; Iron Sword 47 -> crit/130ms; Diamond Sword 73 -> crit/130ms. Iron/Diamond non-crit == crit (both 130ms), i.e. collapsed. (2) The claim's OWN numbers are wrong in the bug's favor: it reported Iron Sword str10 nonCrit=35/heavy because it ignored that weapons grant strength (useGameStore.jsx:21 'Iron Sword': {strength: 8}), which getEffectiveAttributes -> effectiveWith -> computeEffective (progression.js:23) folds in. Real effStr=18, real dmg=47 -> collapse begins at the FIRST iron sword at DEFAULT strength, not mid-game. (3) NOT fixed on HEAD: `git show HEAD:frontend/src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx` still has line 39 verbatim, `git status` on the file is empty; last commit touching it is 1b2a243 (de-monolith refactor), the 3 latest commits are docs-only — unrelated to the R1/R4 fixes. (4) Cited file:line is real and accurate: CombatSystem.jsx:39 `const weight = damage >= 40 ? 'crit' : damage >= 30 ? 'heavy' : 'light';` against HITSTOP={light:45,heavy:90,crit:130,boss:160} (trauma.js:10). Same >=40 threshold also drives camera shake (isCrit?1.6:1.0) and sparks (mobHitFx.js:36 count = isCrit?60:25, plus a different color) — all three channels saturate together, as claimed.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and easily reached, not theoretical. Iron Sword has a live recipe (recipes.js:15-22, iron or Iron Nugget + wood) and starting strength is 10 (useGameStore.jsx:145), so the moment a player crafts and equips their first iron sword, EVERY swing deals >=40 and therefore always fires max hitstop (130ms), max camera shake (1.6), and the 60-particle gold crit spark. A lucky crit becomes physically indistinguishable from a routine poke across all three feedback channels, and the 'light' tier becomes unreachable forever. Progression makes combat feedback WORSE (mushier, less legible) rather than better; the intended light/heavy/crit hierarchy only exists for a level-1 unarmed player. Severity MEDIUM is honest — no crash, no data loss, no save corruption, purely game-feel — but it entirely defeats the feature its own comment (CombatSystem.jsx:35-37) calls 'the audit's #1 game-feel gap'. Fix direction: tier on a normalized quantity (fraction of the player's own expected hit) or thread the real isCrit roll from Components.jsx:250 into damageMob, which the comment at CombatSystem.jsx:56-59 already anticipates.

verdict.title: Starvation damage is silently swallowed by the combat damage lockout
verdict.reason:
Cited lines are REAL and accurate on HEAD (1386b5e): useGameStore.jsx:816 `state.damagePlayer(1, 'starvation')` and :747 `if (now - state.lastDamageTime < 500) return;`. Not touched by 926751e/15fcc96. I wrote my own vitest probe against the REAL useGameStore (the claimant's __probe_dmg.test.js no longer exists on disk, so nothing was taken on faith).

MECHANISM CONFIRMED (probe B): damagePlayer(10,'melee') then consumeHunger in the same tick -> hp 90 -> 90, starvation swallowed.

BUT the impact premise is REFUTED by measurement:
(1) Claim says "any player who is being hit at all has their starvation tick rejected." FALSE. Enemy melee cadence is ATTACK_COOLDOWN=1500ms (src/workers/ai.worker.js:130); hunger ticks every 5000ms (src/GameSystems.jsx:102, setInterval(...,5000)). The 500ms lockout shadows only 1/3 of the timeline. Simulated 10 min vs a live attacker: 80 starvation ticks LANDED, 40 swallowed = 67% land. Only a cap-saturating swarm (hit every 500ms) swallows 100%.
(2) Magnitude is nil: hunger drains 0.1 per 5s from 100 -> 83 MINUTES of not eating to reach hunger 0. Starving = 1 dmg/5s = 0.2 HP/s vs enemy ~10 HP/s = 2.0% of incoming damage. Losing a third of 2% is imperceptible.
(3) Probe F — the claim has the sign BACKWARDS: starvation routes through damagePlayer, which SETS lastDamageTime, granting the player 500ms of i-frames against combat. Verified: starvation lands (100->99), then a 15-dmg melee swing inside that window is BLOCKED (99->99). The shared lockout trades 1 HP of starvation to absorb 15 HP of melee — a net BENEFIT to the player.

Probe file removed after the run (frontend/src/__refute_starve.test.js).
verdict.real_player_impact: None a player can perceive. To be exposed at all a player must go 83 minutes without eating to reach hunger 0. Then starvation is worth 0.2 HP/s against ~10 HP/s of incoming enemy damage (2% of the fight's damage), and 67% of its ticks land anyway against a normal single melee attacker — total loss ~0.7% of incoming damage. Meanwhile the same shared lockout gives the player MORE than it takes: each starvation tick buys a 500ms i-frame that can eat a 15-damage melee hit (measured). The naive fix implied by this finding — exempting starvation from the lockout — would strip that shield and make the game strictly harder for no design gain. Severity is inflated even at LOW; this is a non-issue, and acting on it would be a net negative for the player.

verdicts_joined.title: HYPOTHESIS (not executed): mid-air hitstop banks gravity and drops you faster on release
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/Components.jsx:1063 (gravity integrates velocityY) vs :1125 (`velocityY.current * delta * hitstopScale`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: applyGravity mutates velocityY every frame unconditionally, but the DISPLACEMENT it produces is multiplied by hitstopScale (0 during hitstop). So a hitstop taken while airborne freezes the fall visually while velocityY keeps accumulating; when the freeze releases, the player carries ~130ms of banked gravity (~3.4 u/s extra at a typical g). Grounded hits are unaffected (velocityY is clamped to GLUE_VELOCITY at :1060), which is the common case.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: NONE -- I could not execute this. Reaching it requires the Rapier KCC + the real R3F useFrame, which I did not drive. This is a code-reading hypothesis, stated as such. The two lines are confirmed by grep (`grep -n "velocityY.current" src/Components.jsx` -> :1063 integrate, :1125 scaled displacement); the consequence is inferred, not observed.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Unverified. If real: a mid-air crit (jump-attack) causes a small unnatural drop-snap on release. Low impact either way.
verdicts_joined.domain: Combat: melee, damage, telegraphs, hitstop, dodge, i-frames

verdict.title: Mid-air hitstop banks gravity: velocityY integrates while displacement is zeroed, truncating jumps and snapping falls
verdict.reason: Tried to refute; failed. (1) REPRODUCED with my own probe (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kz-Code/c7297111-afb7-46c9-83b3-6edc09ed7f41/scratchpad/probe_hitstop_gravity.mjs) importing the REAL applyGravity from /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/locomotion.js and the REAL HITSTOP table from src/game/trauma.js, replaying the exact per-frame vertical logic. Output: vy at freeze start 4.533 -> at freeze end 0.267 over 8 frames (133ms) = -4.27 u/s banked, matching predicted -g*T (GRAVITY=-32, HITSTOP.crit=130ms -> -4.16). Probe is faithful: during hitstop displacement is exactly (0,0,0) so the Rapier sweep is a trivial no-op, and the velocityY integration is pure JS with zero Rapier involvement — the load-bearing math is fully executed. (2) NOT already fixed: `git diff HEAD` on Components.jsx/CombatSystem.jsx/locomotion.js/trauma.js is EMPTY (working tree == HEAD); last 3 commits (1386b5e, 45778e7, a8c7b71) are docs-only and touch none of these files. (3) Cited lines REAL and accurate: src/Components.jsx:1063 `velocityY.current = applyGravity(...)` in the airborne else-branch; :1120 `hitstopScale = performance.now() < hitstopUntil ? 0 : 1`; :1125 `velocityY.current * delta * hitstopScale`. I read the block after `computedMovement()` — there is NO post-KCC velocity reconciliation, so nothing corrects the banked velocity. (4) REACHABLE: triggerMeleeAttack (Components.jsx:227) has no grounded gate (cooldown only); CombatSystem.jsx:41 sets hitstopUntil for any source==='player' hit with no grounded check; melee cone (range 4.5 3D, vertical cutoff |dy|>2.2 in src/combat/cone.js) still connects at jump apex (~2.15u); juiceIntensity defaults to 1 (useGameStore.jsx:298) and CombatSystem is mounted (SimplifiedNPCSystem.jsx:115). isGrounded comes from Rapier computedGrounded() (:975), which stays false mid-air under a zero-displacement sweep, so the gravity branch keeps running through the freeze.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, and BROADER than the claim stated. The claim framed it as crit-only and as a fall-side "drop-snap." Executed evidence shows: (a) EVERY hitstop tier banks gravity, not just crits — light 45ms -> 1.44 u/s, heavy 90ms -> 2.88, crit 130ms -> 4.16, boss 160ms -> 5.12; (b) the larger effect is on the RISE, not the fall — a mid-air hit during ascent eats the player's upward velocity (4.533 -> 0.267 u/s), truncating the jump: apex falls from 2.151 to 1.796, i.e. ~17% of jump height lost, enough to whiff a platform gap while jump-attacking; (c) on the descending half, the player does resume falling ~4.27 u/s faster than they entered the freeze, exactly the claimed drop-snap. Player action required is ordinary: jump and attack a mob (no grounded gate, cone reaches). Severity LOW is HONEST and arguably conservative — it is a systematic game-feel deviation on every mid-air hit, not a correctness/progression/crash bug. Note the claimant underestimated their own finding: they guessed ~3.4 u/s at a "typical g"; real GRAVITY is -32.0, giving 4.27 u/s. The claim was correctly labeled as an unexecuted hypothesis and it holds up under execution.

verdicts_joined.title: Spatial audio is DEAD until the first hostile mob spawns — footsteps, jump, swing and hit are SILENT at game start
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/SoundManager.jsx:558 (`audioContext: audioContext.current` in the context `value`) + src/render/SpatialAudioController.jsx:75 (`if (!camera || !audioContext) return;`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: SoundProvider publishes `audioContext: audioContext.current` — a REF read during RENDER — but the ctx is created in a useEffect that sets no state. React runs child effects BEFORE parent effects, so on mount SpatialAudioController sees `audioContext === null`, early-returns, and NEVER calls `useGameStore.setState({ playSpatialSound })`. `App()` (App.jsx:54-60) has zero state and zero store subscriptions, so SoundProvider re-renders ONLY on its own subs: activeHostilesCount / bossActive / sfxVolume / masterMuted / soundEnabled / musicEnabled / volume. None change at startup — and MinimapSyncSystem writing `activeHostilesCount: 0` over 0 every 250ms does NOT re-render (zustand Object.is). So the ctx stays null until the first HOSTILE actually spawns. Every DIRECT `store.playSpatialSound?.(...)` call site has NO fallback and becomes a silent no-op: footstep (Components.jsx:1204,1209), jump (:1052), swing (:911,:1033), hit (:295, CombatSystem.jsx:65), attack/aggroGrowl (AIWorkerSystem.jsx:58,82), roar/grab/hurl/slam/bind + all 4 Aspect motifs (Components.jsx:581-754), anvilHit (HurlSystem.jsx:96), element-zone SFX (ElementZoneSystem.jsx:52,56). Block place/break survive only because useGameSounds has an `else playSound(...)` flat fallback. THE DEEPER PROBLEM: spatial audio is alive ONLY by accident of SoundProvider's `activeHostilesCount` subscription — which exists to drive the arpeggiator BPM, and the arpeggiator is DEAD CODE (PROC_MUSIC_GAIN=0, finding #3). Delete that now-pointless subscription — an obviously correct-looking cleanup — and ALL spatial audio dies permanently and silently, with every gate still green.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Mounted the REAL SoundProvider in jsdom with an instrumented fake AudioContext, plus a child replicating SpatialAudioController's exact gate. Printed:
  t=0   playSpatialSound: undefined | regs: 0
  after 20 minimap ticks (hostiles still 0):
     playSpatialSound: undefined | regs: 0
     footstep/jump/swing/hit fired -> 0 sounds actually played  <-- 0 means SILENT
  after first HOSTILE spawns:
     playSpatialSound: function | regs: 1
     footstep fired -> 1 sounds played (cumulative)  <-- now it works
And separately: `[MOUNT] api.audioContext = NULL` / `[MOUNT] store.playSpatialSound = undefined`, then `[HOSTILE] api.audioContext = ctx` / `= function`. Contrast: the storm bed reads the SAME ctx via `getAudioBridge()` LAZILY at call time (WeatherSystem.jsx:74) and is therefore correct — proving the bug is the render-captured ref, not the ctx itself.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: From world-load until the first hostile spawns, the player walks, jumps and swings in SILENCE, and there is no 3D positioning, no distance falloff, no cavern reverb, no raycast occlusion and no underground muffle. Mining still makes noise (flat/mono), so it reads as "the game's audio is half-broken for the first few seconds, then suddenly snaps on." DAY_HOSTILE_CHANCE=0.7 and the spawner drops 20 mobs once the spawn chunk loads, so the window normally closes within a second or two of chunk-load — but it is genuinely reachable, because the player can pointer-lock and start moving while chunks are still streaming. Severity is HIGH primarily for the latent fragility: one innocuous refactor silently kills all spatial audio forever.
verdicts_joined.domain: Audio (synth voices, master bus, music, spatial, biome beds)

verdict.title: Spatial audio registers only on the first SoundProvider re-render — dead for the first few hundred ms of player control (severity inflated)
verdict.reason: MECHANISM REPRODUCED (my own probe, not the claim's). Mounted the REAL SoundProvider (src/SoundManager.jsx) in vitest/jsdom with a fake AudioContext plus a child replicating SpatialAudioController's verbatim gate. Output: at mount `child-effect-ran audioContext:NULL` and `store.playSpatialSound: undefined`; after 20 `setState({activeHostilesCount:0})` minimap ticks still `undefined` and footstep/jump/swing/hit -> "0 sounds actually played"; after `setState({activeHostilesCount:1})` the effect re-ran with `audioContext:"ctx"` and REGISTERED, and footstep then played. CITED LINES REAL + HEAD-CURRENT: SoundManager.jsx:558 `audioContext: audioContext.current` (render-captured ref), ctx created at :440 in a `useEffect(...,[])` that sets no state; SpatialAudioController.jsx:75 `if (!camera || !audioContext) return;` with `audioContext` in deps, and it is the ONLY `playSpatialSound:` registration site (:131). `git status --short` clean on both files; git log -5 shows only docs commits -> NOT already fixed (unrelated to 926751e/15fcc96). Corroborated: App() (App.jsx:54-60) is stateless; nothing outside SoundManager calls setVolume/setSoundEnabled/setMusicEnabled; `activeHostilesCount` is written only by MinimapSyncSystem.jsx:28; PROC_MUSIC_GAIN=0 (SoundManager.jsx:14) so the keep-alive subscription does serve muted code; footstep (Components.jsx:1204,1209) and jump (:1052) use `?.()` with no fallback. A live Playwright probe of the real game showed playSpatialSound `undefined` for the entire 105s while the world streamed (spawn chunk never finished under swiftshader), consistent with the mechanism.
verdict.real_player_impact: REAL but SMALL, and severity HIGH is inflated. I sized the actual window: SpawnerSystem.jsx:88 bursts 20 mobs on a 500ms poll once isSpawnChunkLoaded, and App.jsx:148-155 auto-pointer-locks the player 100ms after that same flag. So the player-controllable silent window is ~100ms to ~750ms after chunk-load (a lost footstep or two / a silent jump), plus a longer window if the player clicks "Start Adventure" while chunks are still streaming. It then self-heals permanently: p(zero hostiles among 20 at DAY_HOSTILE_CHANCE=0.7) is about 3.5e-11, so registration is effectively guaranteed within one spawner tick + one 250ms minimap tick. The claim's own "closes within a second or two" concession is the honest part; the title ("Spatial audio is DEAD", HIGH) oversells a sub-second startup gap. The claim's fragility argument is also slightly overstated: deleting the now-pointless activeHostilesCount subscription would NOT kill spatial audio "forever" — the sfxVolume/masterMuted subscriptions would still re-render SoundProvider and revive it the moment a player touches the audio slider (though most players never would). Honest severity: LOW-to-MEDIUM acute player impact, with a genuine MEDIUM latent-fragility concern worth fixing (publish the ctx via state, or read it lazily like WeatherSystem.jsx:74 does via getAudioBridge()).

verdicts_joined.title: The domain's ONLY live probe is vacuous — `playSpatialSound?.()` cannot fail, so it reports playable=true even when spatial audio does not exist
verdicts_joined.file_line: scripts/visual/esc-pause-probe.mjs:42
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The probe is: `try { w.useGameStore.getState().playSpatialSound?.('hit', w.__threeCamera.position, 1, 20); return true; } catch (e) { return 'throw:' + e.message; }`. The optional chaining is the whole bug: when `playSpatialSound` is `undefined` (exactly the state in finding #1) the expression short-circuits to `undefined`, nothing throws, and the probe returns `true` -> logs `[esc-probe] spatial-sfx playable=true`. It literally cannot distinguish "spatial audio works" from "spatial audio was never registered." It is doubly blind: it also runs after `waitForFunction(isSpawnChunkLoaded)` + `delay(5000)` + up to 8 pointer-lock retries, by which point hostiles have spawned and finding #1 has already self-healed. The companion gate (tests/gates/spatial-sfx-bus-gates.test.js) is 100% readFileSync+regex and asserts `filter.connect(busInput)` EXISTS IN THE SOURCE — which it does, inside an effect that never runs on mount. Green gate, green probe, dead feature: this is the project's stated failure mode, reproduced exactly, on the one bug in this domain.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: Read the probe source (esc-pause-probe.mjs:37-46) and confirmed the `?.` short-circuit. Confirmed by my own probe that `useGameStore.getState().playSpatialSound` is `undefined` at mount and that calling `st.playSpatialSound?.('footstep', ...)` produced `0 sounds actually played` while throwing nothing — i.e. the exact input on which this probe returns `true`. Also verified `grep -rln 'audio|Sound|music' tests/e2e/` -> NONE (0 of 11 e2e specs touch audio) and that all 15 tests/gates/*audio* files call readFileSync.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: None directly — this is the reason finding #1 shipped and would survive any future regression. Fix: assert `typeof playSpatialSound === 'function'` BEFORE calling, and drop the `?.`.
verdicts_joined.domain: Audio (synth voices, master bus, music, spatial, biome beds)

verdict.title: esc-pause-probe.mjs:42 `playSpatialSound?.()` optional-chain makes the audio probe vacuous (reports playable=true when spatial audio doesn't exist)
verdict.reason: File:line is real and verbatim as quoted (/Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/scripts/visual/esc-pause-probe.mjs:42), and the JS semantics point is true in isolation (node check: `o.playSpatialSound?.('hit', arg())` -> `result=undefined argEvaluated=false`, so args aren't even evaluated). But the operative claim — "it reports playable=true even when spatial audio does not exist" — does NOT reproduce at the probe's actual execution point. I ran an instrumented clone of the probe (identical flow/args, plus an AudioBufferSourceNode.prototype.start counter): AT-MOUNT {"playSpatialSound":"undefined","threeCamera":true}; AT-PROBE-POINT {probeVerdict:true, typeofPlaySpatialSound:"function", hasThreeCamera:true, sfxStartsBefore:3, sfxStartsAfter:4}. So at line 42 the function IS registered (SpatialAudioController.jsx:130 setState, effect deps [camera,scene,audioContext,sounds,...] fire once the AudioContext exists) and the call actually started a real audio source — `playable=true` was a TRUE positive, not a vacuous one. The claim itself concedes the mount-time undefined state "has already self-healed" by probe time, i.e. the probe reported the state correctly. Additionally the probe is NOT a gate: grep shows esc-pause-probe.mjs is a one-shot dev script from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-17-crafty-W1-purge-fix.md, referenced by no package.json script and by no .github/workflows/ci.yml step — so it cannot "let a future regression ship". Also inexact: tests/audio/biomeAmbience.test.js is a behavioral (non-readFileSync) audio test, contradicting "all audio tests are regex". Residual true-but-minor: the `?.` does leave the probe unable to distinguish an unregistered function — dev-script hygiene, LOW at most, not HIGH. Not already fixed (nothing to fix on HEAD, 1386b5e); simply not the defect claimed.
verdict.real_player_impact: None. The claim itself states "player_impact: None directly". The artifact is a dev-only puppeteer script under scripts/visual/ — never bundled, never run in CI, never touched by a player. And empirically the state it would supposedly mask (playSpatialSound undefined) is not present when the probe runs: the call fired a live PositionalAudio buffer source. Zero player-facing consequence; severity HIGH is inflated (meta/test-quality at LOW).

verdicts_joined.title: Arpeggiator burns ~28 WebAudio nodes/sec during ALL combat while producing ZERO sound (PROC_MUSIC_GAIN = 0)
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/SoundManager.jsx:14 (PROC_MUSIC_GAIN = 0), :311 (gain ramp target), :318-381 (25ms scheduler interval)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: PROC_MUSIC_GAIN is 0 (the procedural music was deliberately muted in favour of the ElevenLabs tracks), so the arpeggiator's masterGain ramps to `0.75 * volume * 0 = 0`. But the effect at :388-427 still STARTS the arpeggiator whenever `activeHostilesCount > 0 || bossActive`, and it keeps running its 25ms setInterval for the entire duration of combat, allocating an oscillator + biquad + gain per 16th note and a setTimeout per note — all routed into a gain node pinned at 0. It is a pure-waste allocator running in the most frame-critical moments of the game. The same is true of the synth pad (:126-236), which also multiplies through PROC_MUSIC_GAIN=0 (its wind-bed sibling, which is NOT gated by PROC_MUSIC_GAIN, is the only audible part). This is also what makes finding #1 so fragile: the only reason spatial audio ever comes alive is SoundProvider's `activeHostilesCount` subscription, which exists purely to feed this dead arpeggiator.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Drove the real SoundProvider with an ADVANCING-clock fake AudioContext and set `activeHostilesCount: 3` for 1.0s of wall time:
  nodes created in 1.0s of combat: {"gain":10,"osc":9,"biquad":9}
  => osc/sec: 9  total WebAudio nodes/sec: 28
  gain linear ramps (target values): [ 0 ]     <-- masterGain target is 0 => INAUDIBLE
So: 28 WebAudio nodes + ~9 setTimeouts per second of combat, all silent.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Nothing is heard (correct — the music is intentionally muted), but the player pays GC churn and a 25ms timer for it, continuously, for as long as any hostile is alive. Deleting the arpeggiator + synth-pad code paths costs zero audio and removes the allocation. It must be done together with a fix for finding #1, because removing the `activeHostilesCount` subscription is precisely what would permanently kill spatial audio.
verdicts_joined.domain: Audio (synth voices, master bus, music, spatial, biome beds)

verdict.title: Arpeggiator burns ~28 WebAudio nodes/sec during ALL combat while producing ZERO sound (PROC_MUSIC_GAIN = 0)
verdict.reason: Every MECHANICAL sub-claim reproduces; the player impact does not. (1) Citations accurate: SoundManager.jsx:14 `const PROC_MUSIC_GAIN = 0;` (grep shows this is the sole definition, 5 read-only use-sites, no dev toggle/override); :311 `0.75 * volume * PROC_MUSIC_GAIN` ramp; :318-381 the 25ms setInterval; :388-427 the `activeHostiles > 0 || bossActive` start effect. (2) Reachable in real play: SoundProvider wraps the app (App.jsx:56) and MinimapSyncSystem.jsx:28 writes activeHostilesCount from the live ECS mob query every 250ms — so the arp does start whenever a hostile lives. (3) I re-ran the evidence with my OWN probe (real SoundProvider + jsdom + instrumented fake AudioContext with an advancing clock, activeHostilesCount:3, 1.0s wall time): `nodes created in 1.0s: {"gain":11,"osc":10,"biquad":10}` = 31 nodes; `gain linearRamp targets: [0, 0.24]`. The 0.24 is the per-note envelope (:352), but all notes route osc->filter->noteGain->arp.masterGain (:360-362) and that masterGain is pinned at 0.75*volume*0 = 0 => output identically zero. Claim's "9 osc/sec, 28 nodes/sec" is honest (BPM 130 at 3 hostiles per musicTheory.js -> 8.67 16th-notes/sec x 3 nodes). (4) NOT already fixed: `git log frontend/src/SoundManager.jsx` shows a371187 "fix(audio): combat-scaling arp respects the PROC_MUSIC_GAIN mute lock" — that commit CREATED this state by adding the *PROC_MUSIC_GAIN factor to the :404 combat ramp, closing the last audible path; HEAD still runs the scheduler. (5) It dies on impact magnitude: 26-31 nodes/sec + 40 timer ticks/sec = 0.33-0.72 ms CPU per SECOND at 5-20us/node = 0.03-0.07% of one core = ~0.005-0.012 ms of a 16.7 ms frame. ~3 orders of magnitude below perceptibility in a voxel renderer that allocates more than 31 objects per FRAME. No second-order re-render cost either: the zustand selector returns a number, so the 250ms setState bails out unless the count changes. Probe file deleted after the run (repo hygiene rule).
verdict.real_player_impact: None. The claim's own player_impact field concedes "Nothing is heard (correct — the music is intentionally muted)", so the entire alleged harm is CPU/GC — and that measures ~0.008 ms out of a 16.7 ms frame (0.03-0.07% of one core). A player hears no difference and can measure no frame-time difference. The code is real, runs during all combat, and is genuine dead weight worth deleting in a cleanup pass (preserving the activeHostilesCount subscription, which spatial audio depends on) — but it is a code-hygiene/INFO item, not a player-facing bug. Severity MEDIUM is inflated; honest severity is LOW/INFO. "Pure-waste allocator running in the most frame-critical moments" is rhetorically true and numerically irrelevant.

verdicts_joined.title: `slam` is 20.5 dB louder than `footstep` (peak 0.98 vs 0.092) — it will slam the limiter and duck the whole mix
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/audio/synthVoices.js:147 (makeSlamSound); measured against all 36 voices
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The master limiter (audio/masterBus.js) has threshold -3 dBFS, ratio 20, attack 3ms. `slam` peaks at 0.98 = -0.2 dBFS, i.e. ~3 dB INTO the limiter on every single use, with a 250ms release. The existing test (synthVoices.test.js) only asserts `peak <= 1.0`, so a voice at -0.2 dBFS passes cleanly. The voice bank is otherwise genuinely healthy — I measured every one.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Ran all 36 VOICES factories through a fake ctx and measured peak / dBFS / RMS / DC offset / clipped-sample count:
  footstep  0.05s peak=0.092 (-20.7 dBFS)
  slam      0.28s peak=0.980  (-0.2 dBFS)
  PEAK SPREAD: 0.092 -> 0.98 = 20.5 dB between quietest and loudest voice
  QUIET (<0.15 peak): footstep(0.092)
  HOT (>=0.98): slam(0.98)
  DC OFFSET (|dc|>0.01): none
  LONG (>1.5s): none
  clipped samples: 0 across ALL 36 voices
So: no clipping, no DC offset, no silent voice, no runaway buffer — the bank is solid. Only the slam-vs-footstep spread stands out.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Every Voidhand slam audibly pumps/ducks the rest of the mix for ~250ms (limiter release). Arguably intentional for the game's heaviest verb, and the limiter exists precisely to catch it — so this is a mix-taste call, not a defect. Flagging it because it is the only level anomaly in the bank and no test would ever catch it.
verdicts_joined.domain: Audio (synth voices, master bus, music, spatial, biome beds)

verdict.title: `slam` is 20.5 dB louder than `footstep` (peak 0.98 vs 0.092) — it will slam the limiter and duck the whole mix
verdict.reason:
The MEASUREMENTS reproduce; the MECHANISM and IMPACT do not.

1) Evidence re-run (vitest probe over all 36 VOICES, 100 RNG seeds each): slam peak 0.953-0.980 (-0.2 dBFS), footstep 0.083-0.099 (-20.1 dBFS), spread ~19.9 dB, 0 clipped samples, no DC offset. So the raw-buffer numbers are accurate and not fabricated. Next-loudest voice is zap at 0.61.

2) The claim's causal chain is arithmetically wrong because it compares the RAW BUFFER PEAK (0.98) directly to the limiter threshold (-3 dBFS), ignoring the voice gain stage in between. src/SoundManager.jsx:31 `const [volume, setVolume] = useState(0.5)` — and `setVolume` is exported but NEVER CALLED anywhere in src (grepped), so `volume` is pinned at 0.5 for every player. Both playback paths apply it: playSound (SoundManager.jsx:522 `gainNode.gain.value = volume`) and the spatial path (SpatialAudioController.jsx:144 `sound.setVolume(volume)`, with per-frame gain = initialVolume * occlusionFactor where occlusion only ATTENUATES, line 267). Panner gain is 1.0 at d < refDistance(30). Master-bus input gain = audioGain(sfxVolume=1, muted=false) = 1.0.
   => level actually reaching the limiter = 0.98 * 0.5 = 0.49 = -6.2 dBFS, i.e. 3.2 dB BELOW the -3 dBFS threshold — not "3 dB INTO the limiter".

3) Proved it in a REAL WebAudio engine (Chromium via Playwright, OfflineAudioContext, exact makeSlamSound + exact createMasterBus params threshold -3 / knee 0 / ratio 20 / attack 3ms / release 250ms):
   - slam at real voice gain 0.5: peak into limiter -6.196 dBFS; measured gain reduction = -0.14 dB (inaudible).
   - DUCKING TEST (the claim's actual player impact): rendered a steady mix bed alone vs bed+slam through the same limiter, RMS measured in the 0.45-0.95s window (inside the 250ms release tail). bed_rms_alone = 0.09470467223766135, bed_rms_with_slam = 0.09470467223766135 — BIT-IDENTICAL. Ducking = 0.000 dB. The mix is not pumped, ducked, or touched.
   - Even granting the claim's implicit assumption of unity voice gain, real reduction is only -0.52 dB, not the ~2.6 dB its arithmetic implies.

4) file:line is real (synthVoices.js:147 = `export const makeSlamSound`), but the claim omits that the 0.98 peak is a DELIBERATE CEILING, not an anomaly: synthVoices.js:163-165 already contains a headroom guard (`if (peak > 0.98) ... d[i] *= 0.98 / peak`) that normalizes the rare hot seed down. The voice is capped at 0.98 on purpose.

5) The claim self-concedes it is not a defect: "Arguably intentional for the game's heaviest verb, and the limiter exists precisely to catch it — so this is a mix-taste call, not a defect." A heavy AoE slam being ~20 dB above a constantly-repeating footstep is ordinary, intentional game-audio mix design.

Not already-fixed / not stale (HEAD 1386b5e, no relevant audio commits) — it simply never reproduced.
verdict.real_player_impact: None. The stated impact — "every Voidhand slam audibly pumps/ducks the rest of the mix for ~250ms" — is measurably false: with the real 0.5 voice gain the slam arrives at the limiter 3.2 dB BELOW threshold and produces 0.14 dB of gain reduction, and a direct A/B render shows the rest of the mix is bit-for-bit identical with and without the slam (0.000 dB duck). The player hears a loud slam, which is the intended design for the game's heaviest verb, and hears zero pumping of music or other SFX. No clipping (0 clipped samples across all 36 voices), and the buffer is already peak-guarded to 0.98 by an existing headroom normalizer.

verdicts_joined.title: An imbue-armed cast that is REFUSED burns 30 Resonance AND leaks a free element zone onto a later, unpaid cast
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/Components.jsx:477 (castFiredRef set unconditionally) + :785-788 (consume/spend); src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:175 (mana guard returns) vs :214 (consumeImbueCast)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: `castFiredRef.current = true` is set on the SAME line as `triggerSpellCast()`, outside any success check. But triggerSpellCast() early-returns on the 333ms CAST_COOLDOWN (Components.jsx:318), and castSpell() early-returns on `!useMana(manaCost)` (EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:175). Either way NO projectile is built -> `consumeImbueCast()` (which lives at :214, AFTER the mana guard) never runs. The latch still sees castFired=true, fires 'consume', spends ZONE_COST, and calls armImbueCast(kind) — leaving _castArm permanently set. The next projectile built — an ordinary, un-imbued, unpaid cast — picks that kind up.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: PROBE 12/13, importing the REAL elemancer.js + elemancerChannel.js + resonance.js and re-enacting the apply-site: `ARMED (ring on). Resonance still 100` -> `CONSUME -> spent 30 Resonance (now 70); _castArm := burning` -> `RESULT: Resonance = 70 (was 100) | zones spawned = 0 | imbue ring = OFF`. Then: `EnhancedMagicSystem:214 builds the projectile with imbueKind: consumeImbueCast() -> burning` on a cast that was never imbued.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: You arm the imbue (white-gold ring), right-click while out of mana or inside the 333ms cast cooldown: the ring goes out, 30 Resonance — a third of your bank, ~15 placed blocks or 30 mined blocks of day labour — silently vanishes, and no zone appears. Then a later ordinary spell you never imbued spawns a FREE zone, of whatever element was loaded at the failed cast (so possibly the wrong one), which then joins the chemistry and can annihilate a real zone you did pay for. Out-of-mana during a night siege is the single most common moment a player reaches for a big imbued play.
verdicts_joined.domain: The four Aspects (Wildheart / Voidhand / Soulbind / Elemancer)

verdict.title: Imbue latch is off-by-one: armImbueCast() always post-dates the projectile, so a REFUSED cast (no-mana / 333ms cooldown) still burns 30 Resonance and hands its element to a later, unaimed cast
verdict.reason:
All cited sites are real and unmodified at HEAD (1386b5e, working tree clean for these files). Components.jsx:477 `else { triggerSpellCast(); castFiredRef.current = true; }` — set unconditionally, outside any success check. Components.jsx:785-788 = the latch's 'consume': setImbueArmed(false); accrueResonance(-ZONE_COST); armImbueCast(KIND_BY_SPELL[...]). EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:176-179 = the mana guard `if (useMana && !useMana(manaCost)) { notifyDenied('no-mana'); return; }` (claim said :175, off by one, immaterial), which returns BEFORE :214 `imbueKind: consumeImbueCast()`. triggerSpellCast early-returns on CAST_COOLDOWN=333ms (Components.jsx:318). ZONE_COST=30 (resonance.js:9).

I RE-RAN the evidence with my own probe importing the REAL elemancer.js + elemancerChannel.js + resonance.js and re-enacting the apply-site ordering. Results: (B) armed + out of mana -> castSpell returns at the mana guard, 0 projectiles built -> next-frame latch fires 'consume' -> Resonance 100->70, ring off, zones=0; a LATER ordinary never-armed cast is then built with imbueKind="burning" and spawns a zone at no extra Resonance cost. (C) armed + right-click inside the 333ms cooldown -> same: Resonance 100->70, zones=0.

MATERIAL CORRECTION to the claim: the "leaks a free zone onto a later unpaid cast" half is NOT refusal-specific and is NOT an extra zone. My probe case (A), the HAPPY path (mana OK, cooldown OK), does exactly the same: projectile.imbueKind = null on the paying cast, and the zone lands on the NEXT cast. Reason: the window 'mousedown' listener (Components.jsx:503) is synchronous and builds the projectile (calling consumeImbueCast() at EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:214), while armImbueCast() (Components.jsx:788) runs later in useFrame/rAF — a DOM event handler can never execute inside a rAF callback, so the arm ALWAYS post-dates the projectile. The imbue never lands on the cast that paid for it. The refusal case is one facet of a universal off-by-one. Net ledger is therefore 30 spent -> 1 zone delivered (same as the also-broken success path), so the claim's "a third of your bank silently vanishes" / "FREE zone" is inflated: the value is deferred and misdirected, not destroyed or duplicated. Severity is honest as a real broken feature but the framing overstates the economic loss; MEDIUM-HIGH rather than HIGH-as-written (no crash, no save corruption, no duplicated resource).

Reachability verified, not theoretical: talent `elemancer_imbue` exists and is unlockable (talentTree.js:50, limit 1, prereq elemancer_focus); Z is bound to the imbue intent (Components.jsx:372); right-click routes to 'cast' per the repo's own verbRouter.test.js:47. _castArm (elemancerChannel.js:24-26) is a module singleton with NO reset on death/respawn/new-game — only the next projectile build clears it. Also note KeyF casts (Components.jsx:381) but never stamps castFiredRef, so an F-cast can silently collect the leaked arm.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, a player hits this on the KB+mouse path. Unlock Elemental Imbue, press Z with >=30 Resonance (white-gold ring on), then right-click while out of mana or inside the 333ms cast cooldown: the ring goes out, 30 Resonance (a third of the bank; Resonance is earned by mining/placing at 1-2 per block) is consumed, and NOTHING is cast — out of mana there is literally zero projectile. Out-of-mana right-clicking during a night siege is a common moment.

The zone is not destroyed but it is misdirected: the element kind is latched from activeSpell at latch time and stored in a module-level slot with no reset across death/respawn, so it erupts later at wherever the next ordinary projectile happens to hit — not where the player aimed the imbued play — and possibly as the WRONG element if they swapped spells in between. That zone then joins the chemistry and can react with a zone the player did place deliberately.

The deeper player-facing consequence I proved beyond the claim: because armImbueCast() always runs after the projectile is built, the imbue NEVER applies to the cast that paid for it, even on a perfect cast. Every imbued play lands one cast late. The Elemancer imbue feature does not work as designed for any player.

verdicts_joined.title: "Base-as-anvil" 3x fires on the natural GROUND — the Voidhand's marquee build-reward is free, and building is pointless
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/hurl.js:80 (resolveAnvil) + src/world/Terrain.jsx:878-889 (castWorldRay)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: resolveAnvil returns ANVIL_MULT for ANY ray hit within ANVIL_RANGE — it performs ZERO filtering on what was hit. castWorldRay filters only the player's own rigid body; terrain chunk colliders pass straight through the predicate. Because the hurl arcs downward under gravity, the flight dir at impact already points into the ground.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: PROBE 10, using the REAL makeHurl/stepHurlChunked/resolveAnvil to compute impact geometry on a flat field with ZERO player-built blocks: aim -20deg / mob 6m -> impact y=-0.01, flight dir.y=-0.334 -> anvil 3x -> 90 damage. aim -30deg / mob 4m -> dir.y=-0.461 -> 3x -> 90 damage. (Flat aims correctly give 1x/30.) HONESTY: I modelled the terrain collider as a ground plane; I did not drive the live Rapier world. What IS executed-proven from real code: resolveAnvil cannot distinguish a wall from the ground, and the impact dir.y values above come from the real flight integrator.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Aim down ~20 degrees — the natural aim at any mob within ~6m — and every hurl deals 3x damage (30 -> 90) with the gold "WALL HIT!" text and the anvil ping, on open grass, having placed zero blocks. The Aspect's entire stated payoff (aspectGuide.js:27 "Your base is ammunition: build by day, throw it by night"; hurl.js:76 "rewards day-building directly") is obtainable without building. Conversely the player who DOES build a wall gets nothing distinguishable for it.
verdicts_joined.domain: The four Aspects (Wildheart / Voidhand / Soulbind / Elemancer)

verdict.title: "Base-as-anvil" 3x fires on the natural GROUND — the Voidhand's build-reward is free (frequency overstated by the claim)
verdict.reason:
Re-ran with the REAL shipped module, not the claim's numbers. Probe imported /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/hurl.js and drove makeHurl -> stepHurlChunked -> resolveAnvil at 60fps using geometry read out of the shipping code (NOT assumed): eye = ground+2.1 (Components.jsx:1311 CapsuleCollider [0.5,0.4] => center ground+0.9; Components.jsx:798 camera = translation.y+1.2), muzzle = eye + 1.2*forward (Components.jsx:645), mob center = ground+0.5 (SpawnerSystem.jsx:57 `new THREE.Vector3(x, y + 0.5, z)`, re-grounded to gy+0.5 at SquadAISystem.jsx:39).

(1) REPRODUCES. The claim's own two cited cases both fire on bare flat ground, zero blocks placed: mob 6m / aim -20deg -> impact y=0.51, dir.y=-0.328 -> 3x, 90 dmg. Mob 4m / aim -30deg -> y=0.71, dir.y=-0.456 -> 3x, 90 dmg. Full sweep (aim -40..+10, dist 2..15): 573 connecting shots, 185 (32.3%) award the free 3x on bare ground.

(3) file:line REAL and says what is claimed. hurl.js:80-83 resolveAnvil = `const r = castRay(hit.pos, hit.dir, ANVIL_RANGE); return r && r.toi <= ANVIL_RANGE ? ANVIL_MULT : 1;` — zero filtering on WHAT was hit. Terrain.jsx:878-889 castWorldRay's filterPredicate excludes only the player rigid body; Terrain.jsx:218-219 is a TrimeshCollider on a type="fixed" body, so natural ground is a legal ray hit identical to a built wall.

(2) NOT already fixed. HEAD = 1386b5e; sed of hurl.js:80-83 on HEAD still unfiltered. Cited stale fixes (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) are unrelated.

(4) PLAYER-REACHABLE, not dead code. voidhand.js:59 — in HELD state ctx.attack (left-click) returns action 'hurl'; Components.jsx:645 requestHurl fires from real camera pose; HurlSystem.jsx:93-97 applies `HURL_DAMAGE * anvil` plus gold "WALL HIT!" text (spawnAnvilText) and the anvilHit ping.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG (does not save it, but severity/frequency is inflated): (a) its "impact y=-0.01" is an artifact of modeling the mob at ground level y=0; real impact y=0.51 — right verdict from a wrong model. (b) "aim down ~20deg, the natural aim at any mob within ~6m -> EVERY hurl deals 3x" is FALSE: with the crosshair actually ON the mob, 4m/6m/8m/12m all give 1x/30; only point-blank 3m and long 15m natural aims trigger. True rate is ~32% of connecting shots, not "every".

Root cause of the miss is visible in hurl.test.js:97 — the anvil test pins hit.dir={x:1,y:0,z:0} (a perfectly LEVEL flight, which gravity guarantees never occurs at impact) and stubs open-air as `() => null`, so the suite never casts a descending ray at real terrain. Green tests, live bug.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real. On open grass with zero blocks ever placed, ~32% of connecting Voidhand hurls — including the natural point-blank aim at a mob ~3m away — deal 3x damage (30 -> 90) and pop the gold "WALL HIT!" text plus the anvil ping. Because mob centers sit 1.6m below eye level, the player is aiming downward at essentially every mob, so the descending flight dir at impact reliably finds the ground within ANVIL_RANGE=3.

Two distinct harms: (a) BALANCE — a free 3x damage triple on roughly a third of shots, no cost, no setup; (b) DESIGN NULLIFICATION — resolveAnvil literally cannot tell a player-built wall from natural terrain (both are the same chunk TrimeshCollider), so the Aspect's entire stated payoff (aspectGuide.js:27 "Your base is ammunition: build by day, throw it by night"; hurl.js:76 "rewards day-building directly") is obtainable without building, and the player who DOES build a wall receives nothing distinguishable for it. The marquee build-reward loop does not actually reward building.

Severity: HIGH is defensible on the design-nullification axis, though the claim's "every hurl" framing overstates the trigger frequency (real: ~1/3 of connecting shots, and NOT at the crosshair-on-mob aim for 4-12m).

verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/voidhand.js:26-36 (PHANTOM_BLOCK_COLORS, covers ids 1-9 only) vs src/world/blockIds.js (id space now runs to 15); consumed at src/Components.jsx:637 and passed to requestHurl at :645

verdict.title: Voidhand phantom + hurled projectile render featureless BEIGE for cobblestone, diamond and glass (PHANTOM_BLOCK_COLORS covers ids 1-9; id space now runs to 15)
verdict.reason: Reproduced with my own probe importing the real modules (voidhand.js, blockIds.js, Blocks.js), cross-joining HOTBAR_BLOCKS through idForBlock() (exactly what Terrain.place writes) into PHANTOM_BLOCK_COLORS (exactly what Components.jsx:637 reads): glass id=15, diamond id=13, cobblestone id=14 all yield phantom=undefined -> APPLIED=#A9966E; 3 of 9 hotbar blocks. PHANTOM keys are 1..9; BLOCK_ID runs to 15. NOTE: my first heredoc probe silently hit an existing probe.mjs under zsh noclobber and emitted an unrelated probe's output — I detected this and re-ran from a fresh file, so the numbers above are mine, not the claim's. Cited lines are real and verbatim: voidhand.js:26-36 = PHANTOM_BLOCK_COLORS{1..9}; Components.jsx:637 = `stv.setHeldPhantom({ color: PHANTOM_BLOCK_COLORS[known] || '#A9966E' })`; :645 forwards that color to requestHurl. Data path closed: Terrain.jsx:851 `newBlocks.set(`${tx}_${ty}_${tz}`, numericType)` (numeric id) vs Components.jsx:635 read via castBuildRay's identical `${x}_${y}_${z}` targetCoords (Terrain.jsx:767) — keys match, so `known` really is 13/14/15. NOT fixed on HEAD: `git status --short` on voidhand.js/Components.jsx/blockIds.js is empty (tree == HEAD), and `git log --follow` shows voidhand.js last touched by e9aeb4c9 "content(voidhand-m8): full worker-type tint enumeration (9 distinct)" — authored when the id space stopped at 9, i.e. before R4a grew it to 15. Unmentioned by the claim: voidhand.test.js:69-71 LOCKS the stale table (`expect(keys).toEqual([1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9])`), which is why the drift survived R4a green.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, reachable, cosmetic. Reachability is closed: voidhand_grasp is a genuine unlockable talent (talentTree.js:18, prereq voidhand_force, bound to V in keyMap.js:22) gated only on banked Kinetic. Cobblestone, glass and diamond are obtainable ONLY by player placement, and the grab tint resolves ONLY player-edited (worldBlocks) voxels — so these are precisely the blocks the feature was built to identify, and precisely the ones it fails. A player builds a cobblestone base, grabs a piece of their own wall, and orbits/hurls a featureless beige cube instead of grey stone; same for diamond and glass. PhantomBlockSystem.jsx states the tint exists so block identity survives night-siege lighting — that identity is lost for the 3 most build-invested blocks. No crash, no data loss, no inventory loss. Severity MEDIUM is defensible but sits at the top of its range; LOW-MEDIUM would also be fair. Two refinements: (a) the claim's secondary cactus/id-8 point is real (phantom[8]=#7A5A38 trunk-brown vs BLOCK_ID.cactus=8) but effectively UNREACHABLE — cactus is not in HOTBAR_BLOCKS, cannot be placed, so it never enters worldBlocks; it is a stale mislabel, not player-visible. (b) Any fix must also update voidhand.test.js:69-71, which asserts the stale 1-9 key set. Correct fix: derive the tint table from BLOCK_ID/BLOCK_TYPES rather than maintain a second hand-written id->colour literal — the exact drift class blockIds.js's own header was written to eliminate.

verdicts_joined.title: Element zones are infinite vertical cylinders — they burn, slow and annihilate through solid floors
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/elementZones.js:25 (`const d2 = (a,b) => (a.x-b.x)**2 + (a.z-b.z)**2` — Y dropped) and :103-126 (applyZoneEffects uses the same x/z-only test)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: Every zone predicate — annihilation, dedupe, amplification, burn DoT, frozen slow, shock, resonant lure — tests horizontal distance only. In a voxel game built on verticality this makes every zone an unbounded column.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: PROBE 4 (real applyZoneEffects): a burning zone at y=0 emits damage events for mobs at y=+30 and y=-25 — `[{"id":"ground"...},{"id":"onRoof"...},{"id":"inCellar"...}]`. PROBE 5: a frozen zone at y=0 sets zoneSlowMult=0.4 on a mob at y=+50. PROBE 2 (real spawnZone): a fire cast 80 blocks ABOVE a basement ice zone returns `null` and leaves `zones: 0` — both annihilated through the floor. Compounding (read from real code): ElementZoneSystem.jsx:51 guards the SFX on `if (z && ...)`, so an annihilation is silent — and `grep -ri steam src/` finds no steam VFX anywhere (the code comment at ElementZoneSystem.jsx:49 concedes "an annihilation stays silent steam in v1").
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Exploit: cast one burning zone at the foot of your tower and everything climbing or standing anywhere above it burns, through stone, for free. Frustration: the fire zone you paid 30 Resonance for on the roof silently vanishes because you laid an ice zone in the mine below — no sound, no particle, no zone, no refund. The player has no way to understand what happened.
verdicts_joined.domain: The four Aspects (Wildheart / Voidhand / Soulbind / Elemancer)

verdict.title: Element zones ignore Y — real defect, but the claim's evidence uses impossible mob states and its exploit narrative is refuted (LOW, not MEDIUM)
verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED (mechanism) — but evidence FABRICATED and severity INFLATED; true severity LOW
verdict.reason:
CODE IS REAL + UNFIXED: elementZones.js:25 is verbatim `const d2 = (a, b) => (a.x - b.x) ** 2 + (a.z - b.z) ** 2` (Y dropped); applyZoneEffects:105-126 uses only `dx = e.position.x - z.pos.x, dz = e.position.z - z.pos.z`. git log -3 = docs-only commits (1386b5e, 45778e7, a8c7b71); not fixed.

I REPRODUCED IT with my own vitest probe against the real module (4/4 pass, probe file deleted): burning zone at y=0 emitted damage to mobs at y=+30 and y=-25 (`[{"id":"ground","dmg":4},{"id":"onRoof","dmg":4},{"id":"inCellar","dmg":4}]`); frozen zone set zoneSlowMult=0.4 on a mob at y=+50; fire cast 80 above an ice zone returned null and left zones:0; dedupe at y=+100 refreshed the zone at y=0 (same object). Feature is live player content: talentTree.js:50 `elemancer_imbue`, keyMap.js:24 bound to `Z`.

BUT THE CLAIM'S EVIDENCE IS FABRICATED AT THE GAME LEVEL. The `onRoof`/`inCellar` mobs cannot exist. AIWorkerSystem.jsx:96-100 hard-clamps every AI tick: `entity.position.y = groundY + 0.5`, where getMobGroundLevel (Terrain.jsx:618-630) is a raycast from `{x, y:255, z}` straight DOWN returning the TOPMOST surface. Mob Y is a pure function of (x,z) — no mob is ever under a roof or in a cellar (caves at terrain.worker.js:455-458 are unreachable to mobs for the same reason). The probe fed the pure function states the engine never produces.

THE EXPLOIT IS REFUTED. The whole mob combat model is ALSO 2D: ai.worker.js:166-270 gates aggro/melee/leap/archery on `distToPlayer2D` (x/z only), and AIWorkerSystem.jsx:53-54 applies `store.damagePlayer(attack.damage,...)` with no Y check. A player on a tower is meleed through 30 blocks by those same mobs — there is no safe perch, so the zone confers no asymmetric advantage. The "30 Resonance" cost is also unverified (no such cost in elemancer.js).

Corroborating that the axis was simply never modeled (design gap, not regression): EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:344 comment concedes "zone effects are 2D x/z", and elementZones.test.js pins EVERY zone and mob at a constant `y: 50`. Silent-annihilation sub-claim holds (ElementZoneSystem.jsx:51 guards SFX on `if (z && ...)`; grep -ri steam src/ finds zero VFX, only comments + aspectGuide.js prose promising the player "fire onto ice = steam") — but that is a self-documented v1 gap ("stays silent steam in v1"), not a discovery.
verdict.real_player_impact:
REAL BUT MUCH SMALLER THAN CLAIMED. Since zone Y ≈ topmost-surface(zone column) and mob Y ≡ topmost-surface(mob column)+0.5, the only reachable Y-delta is the height difference between two columns within the small horizontal radius (2.5 burning / 3 frozen; 3.75/4.5 amplified) — i.e. a player-built roof or pillar, or a steep terrain cliff.

Reachable in ordinary play: player builds a base, stands on the roof (y=5), casts an imbued fireball at their feet near the edge → zone painted on the roof column. A zombie outside against the wall (horizontal 1.5, y=0.5) is inside the 2.5 radius by the x/z test, though its true 3D distance is 5.2 — so it burns through the roof and wall at ~13 dps. Same for an ice zone on a cliff-top slowing mobs at the cliff base for no visible reason. Observable and wrong.

NOT reachable: mobs burning "on the roof" or "in the cellar" (impossible states), and anything "climbing your tower" (mobs have zero vertical navigation). The headline exploit — free risk-free damage from an elevated perch — does not exist, because mob melee is 2D and hits the player through the floor anyway.

Severity: LOW, not MEDIUM. Worth fixing (add a Y band to d2 and to applyZoneEffects, e.g. |dy| <= ~2), but it is a cosmetic/consistency defect inside an engine whose entire mob-combat model is already 2D — a principled fix means giving mobs a vertical model too, which is a larger design decision, not a one-line patch.

verdict.title: Bonehide Bulwark (cow+skeleton) is unreachable dead content — the snare, the only player path to an ally, skips passive mobs and cows are passive
verdict.reason:
Reproduced with my own probe (temporarily at frontend/src/game/__probe_reach.test.js, since removed) importing the REAL modules; 2/2 tests green. Output: `SNAREABLE: zombie, skeleton, spider, skitterling, duskhound, moss_brute, emberhusk` / `NEVER snareable: pig, cow, villager` / `assemblable pairs: 28 | FUSE: 3 | do NOTHING: 25` / `*** DEAD ** bonehide_bulwark role=bruiser hp=240`. Caveat worth flagging: my first heredoc was silently blocked by zsh noclobber and a STALE probe from an earlier session ran green — I rewrote the file via Write and confirmed its contents before trusting output.

Chain verified at HEAD (git status clean for all three files):
- /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/hybrids.js:35 — `'cow+skeleton': 'bonehide_bulwark'` (claim cites :36; that is off by one, line 36 is 'skeleton+spider'. Immaterial.)
- /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/mobTypes.js:8 — `cow: { ... passive: true }` (exact)
- /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/Components.jsx:684 — `if (!e || e.passive || e.health > 0.3 * e.maxHealth || e.health <= 0) continue;` (exact, and UNCONDITIONAL — no talent flag bypasses it; grep found no soulbind talent unlocking passives)
- /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/systems/SpawnerSystem.jsx:62 — `passive: mobConfig.passive` proves the flag is live on the runtime ENTITY, not just the registry (this was the strongest refutation route and it failed).

Snare is the ONLY player path to an ally: `captureMob` (CombatSystem.jsx:150) has exactly two call sites — the snare (Components.jsx:703, which filters passive) and a DEV-only `soulbindShowcase` test hook (App.jsx:594, tree-shaken from prod) that literally fuses ['cow','skeleton'] for a showcase card. My CONTROL test shows `convertMobToAlly` (allegiance.js:13) would happily bind a cow — it blocklists only 'villager' — isolating the snare filter as the sole gate.

NOT already fixed: last commits touching hybrids.js are 64fc55c2 / 52a009c3 / a6d61f4d (mob-variety pass + invisible-hybrid fixes), none address reachability. Unrelated to the R1/R4 fixes (926751e, 15fcc96).
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real but narrower than the title claims. CONFIRMED player impact: Bonehide Bulwark — 240 HP, the roster's ONLY bruiser/tank — cannot be obtained by any player action, ever. That is 1 of 4 hybrids (25% of the fusion roster) and the entire tank archetype, dead. FUSE is a real advertised 50-Soul capstone: aspectGuide.js:37 tells the player "Stand TWO bound creatures together and hold X to FUSE them into a hybrid (50 Soul)", and aspectGuide feeds the player-facing SpellUpgradePanel.jsx.

SEVERITY IS PARTLY INFLATED. The headline "25 of the 28 squads cannot fuse at all" is arithmetically true but is NOT a defect: hybrids.js's own header declares the design — "the CURATED fusion roster (the spec-locked v1 stance: lookup, never procedural splicing)". A 4-entry curated table necessarily leaves most of the 28 pairs without a recipe. Presenting intended curation as breakage inflates the finding. Also, no bestiary/codex shows Bonehide Bulwark to players, so nobody sees a visibly "missing" entry — the harm is denied designed content, not a broken-looking UI.

UNDER-SOLD but real: the zero-feedback path checks out at Components.jsx:736 — canStartFuse requires lookupHybrid(...) truthy, so with no recipe decideFuse never opens a channel: no tether, no denial, no sound. With only 3 recipes and no discovery affordance, holding X on a non-recipe pair yields silence. Legit UX gap, but a separate finding from the dead-content bug.

Net: MEDIUM is defensible for the core defect (unobtainable tank hybrid); the title's framing overstates it. Fix is one line — either make cow snareable (an exception to the passive gate) or re-key bonehide_bulwark onto a snareable pair (e.g. moss_brute+skeleton, which fits the bruiser role).

verdict.title: Squad allies are immortal — Soulbind grants a permanent, risk-free 16 DPS buff
verdict.reason:
Re-ran the evidence with my OWN vitest probe (deleted after) driving the real src/ecs/world.js + src/game/allegiance.js + src/game/squadAI.js, not the claim's asserted output. Result: pre-bind `mobsQuery.entities.find(e => e.id === 4242)` resolves; after `convertMobToAlly(ecs, e)` the same lookup prints `undefined`, the entity is in alliesQuery, and health is restored to 100. That `undefined` is precisely what CombatSystem.jsx:23 computes, so line 24 `if (!entity) return null;` makes every damage call on an ally a no-op.

Cited lines are real and accurate: /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx:23 is `const entity = mobsQuery.entities.find(e => e.id === id);`; /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/allegiance.js:15-16 is the removeComponent('isMob')/addComponent('isAlly') swap; /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/ecs/world.js:7,10 defines the two disjoint archetypes.

I closed the exhaustive-search leg the claim asserted but did not prove. Grepping every health mutation and every entity removal in src/: the ONLY health-reduction site in the whole codebase is CombatSystem.jsx:83 (`entity.health -= damage`), which sits behind the mobsQuery gate. No mob/worker AI targets allies; BossEntity.jsx only ever calls damagePlayer. Every `ecs.remove` sweep (App.jsx x6, SpawnerSystem.jsx:186/193) iterates mobsQuery.entities. The sole ally removal is hybrids.js:63-64 (FUSE), which consumes two allies into a hybrid that is itself `isAlly: true` and therefore also immortal. LEASH_DIST overflow is a teleport (squadAI.js:30), never a death. There is no ally death path whatsoever.

Not already fixed: HEAD is 1386b5e; it and the four commits before it are docs-only. The 926751e/15fcc96 fixes were quest-claim and block-ids, unrelated.

Reachability verified at Components.jsx:697-703: bind requires the `soulbind_snare` talent + SNARE_COST=35 (soul.js:11) + `alliesQuery.length < squadCap` where squadCap = 2 + (soulbind_pack ? 1 : 0). DPS recomputed independently: ALLY_DPS_HIT=12 (squadAI.js:16) / ATTACK_COOLDOWN_SEC=1.5 (squadAI.js:14) = 8 DPS/ally, 16 DPS for two.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real and live on HEAD. A player who unlocks the soulbind_snare talent and spends 35 Soul owns two (three with the pack talent) permanently invulnerable allies that auto-engage any hostile within ENGAGE_RADIUS=18m of the player and deal 16 DPS combined, forever. They cannot be damaged (no code path reduces ally health), cannot die, cannot be culled, and cannot be lost — leash overflow teleports them back. Attrition does not exist, so the night siege is substantially defused and the Aspect's stated tension has no stakes. nametagData.js:19 corroborates: allies hardcode `hpFrac: 1, showBar: false`, i.e. the HP field is already decorative.

Important disposition nuance, which the claimant honestly volunteered and which I confirmed: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-crafty-s2b3-soulbind-design.md §5 ("What v1 explicitly CUTS") names "hostiles-target-allies, mob-vs-mob, ally HP/retreat" as the v2 milestone. So this is a DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATE v1 scope cut, not an accidental defect — the immortality is emergent from a seam the design intentionally built ("five hostile surfaces exited by construction"). That makes it a v2 design/balance ticket rather than an emergency bugfix, but it does not make the player-facing consequence any less real or less present today. Severity MEDIUM is honest, not inflated; the claim disclosed the deferral rather than hiding it and did not fabricate its evidence.

verdict.title: aspectGuide's "Hold X" instruction is false — the snare channel is edge-triggered, and following the guide leaves the verb dead after any aim-break
verdict.reason:
Reproduced against the REAL shipped module (node ESM probe importing frontend/src/game/soulbind.js, replicating the apply-site edge logic verbatim from Components.jsx:672-699; probe scripts deleted same turn).

PROBE A (the claim): t=0.0 press X -> startChannel; key RELEASED every frame thereafter; t=1.1 -> bind. Key-release is unobservable to the SM. PROBE C: holding X but losing aim -> channelBreak, no bind. So the real gate is AIM, not the key. Claim's core mechanic assertion reproduces exactly.

CITATION REAL (minor off-by-one): the text is aspectGuide.js:36 ('Hold X while aiming at it'), not :37 — but :37 ALSO says 'hold X to FUSE', so the drift is in BOTH steps. soulbind.js:19-46 decideSoulbind ctx = { snareEdge, active, alive, now, canSnare, targetId } — no held-key field, confirmed by Read. Traced the apply-site: Components.jsx:672 reads the held key as `snareIn` but consumes it ONLY to derive `snareEdge` (line 673); `ctx.active` is the POINTER-LOCK gate (input/inputState.js:18-21, setActive from pointerlockchange), NOT the key. decideFuse has the same shape (fuseEdge: snareEdge, Components.jsx:739).

NOT ALREADY FIXED: `git status --porcelain` clean for both files; `git log -1 -- frontend/src/game/aspectGuide.js` = 84c7fe26 (the original feature commit), NOT today's 926751e/15fcc96. `git show HEAD:...` still contains 'Hold X while aiming at it'.

SEVERITY HONEST (understated, not inflated): grep for 'hold x' across src/ returns ONLY aspectGuide.js:36-37 — it is the sole teaching surface, confirming the claim's premise.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real, and WORSE than the claim stated — the claim called it "arguably in the player's favour," which my probe refutes.

PROBE D: a player doing exactly what the guide says (hold X, keep aiming) suffers an aim slip — which the design explicitly EXPECTS ("the mob keeps moving, so holding aim IS the skill", soulbind.js:5). The channel breaks free and silently (no cooldown, no message; the tether VFX just vanishes via clearSnareState, Components.jsx:718-719). The player re-centers their aim while STILL HOLDING X as instructed — and the channel NEVER restarts. Held X for 3 full seconds with perfect aim on a jade-weakened mob: zero actions after the break. Because startChannel needs a RISING EDGE (snareIn && !prev), the only way to retry is to RELEASE X and press again — which the guide never tells them to do, since it says to hold.

PROBE E (control): same aim slip, but release at t=0.5 and re-press at t=0.8 -> startChannel, bind at t=1.9.

So the guide's instruction actively produces a dead-input state on the design's own expected-common path. Not theoretical, not dead code: soulbind_snare is a shipped, unlockable talent (talentTree.js:39) wired to KeyX (keyMap.js:23) with live HUD (HUD.jsx:158) and a bind ceremony.

Mitigation keeping this LOW rather than higher: self-recoverable by experimentation (the vanished tether is a visible "nothing is happening" cue), and the break costs nothing — no Soul spent, no cooldown armed. LOW is the honest severity.
