verdict.title: A held Voidhand phantom survives a menu open (the HELD branch never checks ctx.active)
verdict.reason:
The mechanism reproduces, but the claim's load-bearing premise is factually false about the codebase.

(1) File:line is REAL. /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/voidhand.js:56-64 — HELD guards `!ctx.alive` (:58), not `!ctx.active`; CHARGING (:68) guards `!ctx.alive || !ctx.active`. Not fixed on HEAD (git log -3 = 1386b5e/45778e7/a8c7b71; zero voidhand commits).

(2) I re-ran the evidence with my OWN probe importing the real module (scratchpad/voidhand_probe_v2.mjs). CAUTION FLAG: the scratchpad already contained a different agent's `probe.mjs` and zsh noclobber silently blocked my heredoc, so my first run printed a STALE anvil probe. Re-ran on a fresh path. Real output: `t=0.40 -> grab | held=true`; `t=0.50 MENU OPEN (active=false) -> none | held=true`; `t=8.41 -> drop`. Call site Components.jsx:619 confirms ctx wiring (`active: vin.active`, `now: state.clock.getElapsedTime()`), useFrame@515 has no !active early-return, GRAB_COST=25 (kinetic.js:11), and InputManager.jsx:161 exits pointer-lock on menu open. So the mechanism is real.

(3) BUT the claim's central assertion — "Every other cancel path in the domain treats `active` as the modal proxy. Voidhand's held state is the one place that ignores it" — is REFUTED by its own cited twin. beastTransform.js:45-50, the ACTIVE (persistent-state) branch: `if (ctx.isBeast) { if (ctx.now >= sm.activeUntil) -> 'exitTimer'; if (ctx.roarEdge) -> 'exitManual'; return 'none' }` — it checks NEITHER ctx.active NOR ctx.alive, and its 14s form-duration clock burns through a menu exactly like Voidhand's 8s. The claim compared HELD to beastTransform's CHARGE branch (:54) while ignoring its persistent-state branch. Voidhand's HELD is actually STRICTER than its twin (it at least checks alive). The pattern is domain-wide and deliberate: transient charge cancels on input-loss; persistent state persists and runs its own timer.

(4) It is documented intent, not an oversight. voidhand.js:55 enumerates release conditions as "release via a verb, death, or the max-hold timer" (menu-open deliberately excluded); :66 says "menu-open / death cancels" for CHARGING only. The code does exactly what its spec comment says.

(5) Severity is internally incoherent: labeled LOW/"Cosmetic" while describing a 25-Kinetic resource loss.
verdict.real_player_impact: No defect. A player CAN observe the phantom persisting across a menu open and the 8s max-hold clock continuing to run — but that is intended, spec-documented, and consistent with the twin state machine (beast form's 14s duration clock behaves identically). Keeping a carried block while the player checks their inventory is correct design; force-dropping it on menu-open would be the worse behavior. The only residual grain of truth — that menu time counts toward the max-hold clock — is a game-wide "menus do not pause the sim" property shared with beast form, i.e. a global design question about pausing, not a Voidhand-specific bug at voidhand.js:56-64, and not the claimed asymmetry (which does not exist).

verdicts_joined.title: Resuming a save made at NIGHT silently adds a night to the siege -- and it RATCHETS across every reload (persisted)
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/world/survivalSystem.js:17-25 (the day->night branch) + src/App.jsx:176 (useSurvivalMode mounted UNCONDITIONALLY at App top level) + src/store/useGameStore.jsx:858 (loadWorldData derives isDay from gameTime)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: useSurvivalMode is mounted at App top level with `prevIsDay = useRef(true)`, before any world is loaded. loadWorldData sets `isDay = isDayAtUnit(gameTime)` -> for a save recorded at night that is FALSE. The hook's effect sees prevIsDay=true, isDay=false, and treats the LOAD as a nightfall EDGE: it fires incrementNight(). nightCount is persisted (saveSchema.js:41), so the inflation is written straight back to disk and compounds. The autosave (App.jsx:232-249) schedules on inventory/worldBlocks/ferocityBanked changes -- exactly what happens while you fight a siege -- so a night save is the NORMAL state for anyone who plays into the night.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
PROBE (real store + real hook, jsdom, subscribing to every nightCount write):
  save on disk: gameTime=700, isDayAtUnit=false, nightCount=3, lastRewardedNight=2
  nightCount write log: ["0->3","3->4"]      <- the load writes 3; the HOOK then writes 4
  final nightCount    : 4
Control (DAY save, gameTime=200): `DAY-save load -> nightCount = 3 (save said 3)` -- no increment. So it is specifically the night phase.
RATCHET PROBE (5 successive reloads of the same night save):
  reload #1 -> nightCount 4   siege={hostileChance:0.90, maxMobs:32}
  reload #2 -> nightCount 7   siege={hostileChance:0.95, maxMobs:40}   <- CAPS SATURATED
  reload #3 -> 10 | #4 -> 13 | #5 -> 16   siege={0.95, 40}
And the reward inflates with it: after loading a night-3 save and surviving to dawn, `dawnReward` paid for night 5: {night:5, xp:250, coins:50, lootRarity:"legendary", lootItem:"Diamond"} (coins went 0 -> 50).
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Quit/refresh during a night siege and hit Load. The game immediately blasts the siege horn (DayNightAudio fires on the same true->false edge), banners "Night N+1 -- the siege intensifies. Hold until dawn!" for a night you already started, permanently raises the spawn cap and hostile bias, and bumps the next dawn reward a whole rarity tier. Two reloads is enough to saturate the siege at 40 concurrent mobs / 95% hostile -- the entire difficulty curve the siege was built to deliver is destroyed, permanently, by a normal save/resume. It never self-corrects because nightCount is persisted.

verdict.title: Resuming a save made at NIGHT adds a night to the siege on every load — persisted, compounding
verdict.reason:
Reproduced with my own probe (real store + real hook, jsdom, @testing-library/react, mirroring App.jsx:176 — a component reading useGameStore(s=>s.isDay) and passing it to useSurvivalMode). Night save (game_state.gameTime=700, isDayAtUnit(700)===false, progression.nightCount=3) -> loadWorldData -> in-game nightCount=4. DAY control (gameTime=200, same nightCount=3) -> stays 3, so it is specifically the night phase. Clean ratchet with a real disk round-trip via buildSaveData (one mount per reload, explicit cleanup()): 4,5,6,7,8 — +1 per reload, persisted, never self-correcting. Dawn reward after loading a night-3 save paid for night 4 (lastRewardedNight=4, coins=40 instead of 30).

CITED LINES ARE REAL AND SAY WHAT THE CLAIM SAYS: frontend/src/world/survivalSystem.js:15 `const prevIsDay = useRef(true);` + :18 `if (prevIsDay.current && !isDay)` -> `useGameStore.getState().incrementNight()` (no load guard anywhere in the file); frontend/src/App.jsx:176 `const survivalMode = useSurvivalMode(gameState.isDay);` unconditional at App top level; frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx:858 `const isDay = isDayAtUnit(gameTime);` and :876 `const nightCount = prog?.nightCount ?? state.nightCount;`; frontend/src/game/saveSchema.js:41 `nightCount: state.nightCount` (persisted, so the inflation is written back to disk).

NOT ALREADY FIXED: HEAD=45778e7; last commit touching survivalSystem.js is 10087e45 (siege ladder); current source has no guard. The existing tests/gates/siege-gates.test.js is a VACUOUS source-regex gate (expect(/useGameStore\(\(s\)\s*=>\s*s\.nightCount\)/.test(src)).toBe(true)) — it asserts source text, not behavior, so it was structurally incapable of catching this.

WHERE THE CLAIM OVERSTATES: its ratchet probe reported 4,7,10,13,16 (+3/reload, "caps saturated in 2 reloads") and a night-5 legendary/coins-50 dawn reward. That is a test-harness artifact — leaked un-cleaned mounts, each with its own useSurvivalMode firing incrementNight(). With proper cleanup the real rate is +1/reload; caps (hostileChance 0.95, maxMobs 40) still saturate, just after ~3-5 reloads instead of 2. Mechanism and direction correct; numbers inflated ~3x.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, a real player hits this on an ordinary action. MenuSystem is rendered INSIDE App (App.jsx:774) and renders WorldManager with onWorldLoad={gameState.loadWorldData} (MenuSystem.jsx:170), so App — and useSurvivalMode with prevIsDay=true — is mounted the entire time the title/menu is up, before any world is loaded. The autosave (App.jsx:220-250) schedules on inventory/worldBlocks/ferocityBanked changes, exactly what happens while fighting a siege, so a night-phase save is the NORMAL state for anyone who plays past dusk. Quit or refresh during a night siege, hit Load: the game immediately treats the load as a nightfall edge, banners the next night's siege warning for a night you already started, permanently raises the persisted nightCount, which drives siegeParams (spawn cap + hostile bias) and the dawn-reward scaling. Because nightCount is persisted (saveSchema.js:41) the inflation is written straight back to disk and compounds on every subsequent reload (verified 4,5,6,7,8), eventually saturating the siege at maxMobs=40 / hostileChance=0.95 and inflating dawn loot a rarity tier. It never self-corrects.

SEVERITY: HIGH, not CRITICAL. It is genuine persisted, compounding progression corruption from a normal save/resume and it does flatten the siege difficulty curve — but it does not destroy player data or block play, and the per-reload rate is 1/3 of what the claim asserted.

FIX SHAPE: useSurvivalMode must not treat a LOAD as a nightfall EDGE — seed prevIsDay from the store's current isDay on mount, and have loadWorldData bump a load-epoch the hook consumes to resync prevIsDay.current = isDay without firing either branch.

verdict.title: Stars and a moon disc render in the sky at MIDDAY during every storm (~half of all daytime)
verdict.reason:
Reproduced independently, did not take the claim on faith.

(1) CITED LINES ARE REAL AND ACCURATE. nightSky.js:12-16 = `Math.max(0, 1 - Math.abs(m - 1))`, and its own header (lines 3-5) states the star/moon layer must read "never on the bright-blue day sky (mood 0)". weatherGate.js:11 = `export const STORM_MOOD_BOOST = 0.85`. mood.js:91-94 = `moodTarget` returns `clamp(Math.max(night, dangerLevel, weatherBoost), 0, 2)`. Atmosphere.jsx:182 = `u.uStar.value = starIntensity(moodRef.current)`. Atmosphere.jsx:110 = `if (uStar > 0.001) {` opening the star-field block; :129 = `col = mix(col, vec3(0.88,0.92,1.0), disc * uStar)` (moon disc).

(2) MY OWN PROBE (vitest, real modules: starIntensity + moodTarget + sampleMood + stormMoodBoost) reproduces the claimed table exactly:
  clear DAY      mood=0.00 uStar=0.000 skyTop=#1a5ad0 fog=0.0025
  STORM midday   mood=0.85 uStar=0.850 skyTop=#172b65 fog=0.0106  <-- stars+moon drawn
  clear NIGHT    mood=1.00 uStar=1.000 skyTop=#161b3a fog=0.0120
  BOSS day       mood=2.00 uStar=0.000 skyTop=#0a0c14 fog=0.0200
uStar=0.850 > 0.001 => the shader branch executes; moon disc mixed at 85% opacity.

(3) FULLY WIRED, NOT DEAD CODE. WeatherSystem.jsx:68 `store.setWeatherMoodBoost(stormMoodBoost(nextWeather))` -> Atmosphere.jsx:157 `moodTarget({ isDay: st.isDay, dangerLevel: st.dangerLevel, weatherBoost: cap ? 0 : st.weatherMoodBoost })` -> :182 -> shader. I read the full shader block (lines 110-131): there is NO day re-gate on uStar.

(4) NOT ALREADY FIXED. `git status --short` on all 5 cited files returns EMPTY => working tree identical to HEAD (HEAD=45778e7). `git log` on those paths shows commit 20c23fc "W4-T8 storm sky-darken: weatherMoodBoost MAXed into moodTarget" as the commit that INTRODUCED the drift — it added weatherBoost to moodTarget without re-checking starIntensity's isDay/dangerLevel-only assumption. Unrelated to the stale R1(926751e)/R4(15fcc96) fixes.

(5) CLAIM UNDERSTATED ITS OWN STRENGTH: Atmosphere.jsx:157 forces `weatherBoost: cap ? 0` in capture mode, so the pinned visual baselines are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to this bug — that is why it survived. The claim's failure to screenshot is not a weakness; the harness cannot photograph it.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real and pervasive, on the game's most-seen surface.

REACHABILITY: WeatherSystem.jsx:99 toggles clear<->storm on a 90s setInterval with NO isDay gate (verified: `const states = ['clear','storm']` ... `}, 90000)`). A day half is ~150s (dayPhase.js:18 "a ~150s day half"). Storm is therefore active ~50% of the time and uncorrelated with day phase, so roughly half of all daytime is a storm. During each one: mood 0.85 -> uStar 0.85 -> an 85%-intensity star field plus a bright white-blue moon disc (85% opacity mix) painted on a sky (#172b65) that is 85% of the way to the actual night sky (#161b3a). Meanwhile <Sun> at GameScene.jsx:257 is rendered UNCONDITIONALLY (no isDay/weather gate — verified), so the sun billboard hangs in that same starry, moonlit sky. Sun + moon + stars at noon reads as a rendering glitch, not weather.

SEVERITY: HIGH is defensible but sits at the TOP of the honest range. It is purely cosmetic — no crash, no save corruption, no progression block — so it is not in the same class as the R4 block-id data-destruction bug. What earns HIGH is pervasiveness (half of all daytime, on the sky, the second-most-visible surface after the ground) and that it presents as a broken renderer.

IMPORTANT NUANCE the claim glossed: the sky DARKENING during a storm is INTENDED (weatherGate.js:9-10 explicitly wants "overcast/moody, not full night"). The bug is strictly that the stars + moon layer rides along, because `mood` is overloaded as both "time of night" AND "storm darkness", and starIntensity still assumes mood is driven only by isDay/dangerLevel. Fix should decouple the star/moon gate from mood (e.g. gate on !isDay directly, or pass a separate nightness scalar) — NOT by lowering STORM_MOOD_BOOST, which would sacrifice the intended overcast look.

verdict.title: Loading a save while the live phase is NIGHT wipes the loaded save's ferocity / kinetic / soul / resonance banks to zero
verdict.reason:
Reproduced independently against clean HEAD (1386b5e; the 2 commits newer than the audit are docs-only, and `git status` shows survivalSystem.js + useGameStore.jsx unmodified, so my probe exercised HEAD's exact code).

CITED LINES ARE REAL: `git show HEAD:frontend/src/world/survivalSystem.js` lines 27-36 = the `if (!prevIsDay.current && isDay)` dawn branch calling setFerocityBanked(0)/setKineticBanked(0)/setSoulBanked(0)/setResonanceBanked(0). Exactly as cited.

MECHANISM VERIFIED IN SOURCE: useGameStore.jsx:858 `const isDay = isDayAtUnit(gameTime)` derives phase from the SAVE's gameTime, and commits `isDay` at line 920 in the SAME set() as the four banks (lines 935-938). The useEffect([isDay]) in useSurvivalMode (wired at App.jsx:176) then fires post-commit and stomps the freshly-restored values.

MY OWN PROBE (temp vitest + jsdom, real store + real hook, wired as App.jsx does; assertions written to expect banks PRESERVED so a FAILING test = bug present):
- PROBE D (live phase NIGHT, load DAY save w/ banks 90/80/70/60) -> {"ferocityBanked":0,"kineticBanked":0,"soulBanked":0,"resonanceBanked":0}  [FAILED => bug reproduces]
- PROBE E (CONTROL, identical save, live phase already DAY) -> {"ferocityBanked":90,"kineticBanked":80,"soulBanked":70,"resonanceBanked":60}  [PASSED]
The control isolates the cause: the wipe tracks the load-induced phase transition, not the load itself. (First run errored `document is not defined` — env misconfig, not evidence; fixed to jsdom before concluding.) Probe file deleted after.

Banks are genuinely persisted: saveSchema.js:42-45 serializes all four in `progression`.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real, reachable, not dead code. In-game path fully traced: ESC = "Settings / pause" (game/keyMap.js:34) plus a HUD Settings button (ui/GameHud.jsx:68) -> SettingsPanel.onOpenWorldManager (MenuSystem.jsx:155-157) -> WorldManager, whose load calls onWorldLoad(worldData) = loadWorldData DIRECTLY (WorldManager.jsx:119-120). There is NO window.location.reload in that path, so App stays mounted and the `prevIsDay` ref survives as false — which is exactly what arms the dawn branch.

So: player is mid-night in world A, opens World Manager, loads world B (a day save) -> B's four hard-earned banked resources are silently zeroed. No message, no undo. All four gate the Aspect roars, so the player can lose a fully-charged roar banked over a whole day.

Two honest nuances (neither fatal): (1) Recoverable in principle — the save on disk still holds 90/80/70/60, and re-loading the same world now that the phase is DAY restores them (the PROBE E path). But there is no message, so the player would never know to try, and autosave (game/autosave.js) will write the zeroed banks back over the save, making the loss permanent. (2) The same branch also calls grantDawnReward(), so a save with lastRewardedNight < nightCount would additionally fire a spurious dawn reward (correctly no-op'd in my probe, so I do not assert it as part of the finding).

SEVERITY: MEDIUM is honest, arguably conservative. Silently destroys four persisted progression resources with no message/undo, but does not corrupt world/inventory/XP/coins, and the banks do regrow through play.

verdict.title: The dawn branch can pay out a FREE dawn reward merely for LOADING a save
verdict.reason: Cited lines are real and unmodified on HEAD (git status clean; no fix commit) — but the claim's reachability is fabricated. Decisive code: useGameStore.jsx:858 `const isDay = isDayAtUnit(gameTime)` — the loaded phase is DERIVED from the save's gameTime, never read from a stored isDay flag. The dawn branch (survivalSystem.js:27) requires a night->day flip, so the loaded save must be a DAY save. I probed with the real store + real useSurvivalMode hook (mounted as App.jsx:176 does) + the real clock (setGameTime): (1) PLAYER-REACHABLE case — live phase NIGHT, load a real day save that actual play wrote via buildSaveData: the dawn branch DID fire but the guard returned null: coins 60->60, totalXP 300->300, Diamond 0. NO PAYOUT. (2) 8-cycle sweep including BOTH abuse orderings (load day-save-at-night AND Finding #1's load night-save-at-day): zero DAY-saves-with-gap, zero payouts on any load, zero clock desyncs. (3) The claim's stated bridge — "Finding #1 manufactures exactly that state" — is FALSE: Finding #1's inflated saves are always NIGHT saves (measured gameTime:1800 -> isDayOnLoad:false; gameTime:4200 -> isDayOnLoad:false). A night save loaded at night = no flip = no dawn branch; loaded at day = the NIGHT branch, not dawn. The two findings cannot chain. Root invariant: buildSaveData (saveSchema.js:41-42) writes nightCount + lastRewardedNight atomically from one snapshot, and the dawn handler closes the gap (lastRewardedNight = nightCount) at EVERY night->day flip, so gap==0 at every DAY moment, hence in every DAY save. I reproduced the claim's exact numbers (coins 100->160, totalXP 300, Diamond 1) ONLY from the same hand-authored save {gameTime:300 DAY, nightCount:6, lastRewardedNight:2} that no gameplay writes — the claimant fed the store an unreachable input and reported it as a player state. Self-check: my own first sweep reported violations that turned out to be my harness force-setting isDay and gameTime independently (a desync real code paths never produce); re-running on the real clock zeroed them.
verdict.real_player_impact: None via the claimed path. No sequence of real play + real save/load can produce the required precondition (a DAY-phase save with lastRewardedNight < nightCount), so no player can trigger a free dawn reward by loading. The "exploit" framing is void even granting the crafted input: saves are plain localStorage (game/worldSaves.js, "local-first") holding progression.coins, totalXP and inventory in cleartext — anyone able to hand-author that save can simply set coins:999999 instead, which is strictly easier than manufacturing a night-count gap to farm one Diamond. SEPARATE REAL BUG found while refuting (NOT this claim, different trigger/file, no save-load involved): the in-game "Time" toggle at frontend/src/ui/GamePanels.jsx:779 calls setIsDay(!isDay) directly; clicking it at night fires the dawn branch and pays out. Spamming it ratchets — 7 clicks measured: coins 0->100, totalXP 0->500, 4 loot items, nightCount 0->4, with zero gameplay. That one is genuinely player-reachable and worth filing on its own merits.

(1) `src/store/useGameStore.jsx:693` is `const isDay = frac >= 0.25 && frac < 0.75;` (grep on HEAD); `src/game/dayNight.js:48-50` is `Math.floor(t / HALF_CYCLE_UNITS) % 2 === 0` with HALF_CYCLE_UNITS=600. Rows match the claim's table exactly. (NOTE: my first probe run hit zsh noclobber and returned STALE output from an unrelated ocean-cave probe — I caught it and re-ran with a fresh filename; the numbers above are from the clean run.) (3) NOT already fixed: today's fix commits (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) did not touch this; `git log -3 -- src/store/useGameStore.jsx src/game/dayNight.js` shows 114e5a6/fc26af1/af7ccc1, none related, and the line is live on HEAD. (4) DECISIVE: setTimeOfDay is player-UNREACHABLE. Three independent static `import.meta.env.DEV` gates (Vite dead-code-eliminates all in prod): `src/App.jsx:266` `if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return;` guards the registerTestHook block containing the setTimeOfDay hook at :287; `src/devtest/testBridge.js:16` `if (!import.meta.env || !import.meta.env.DEV) return; // dev-only` means window.__craftyTest is never installed in prod; `src/App.jsx:738` `{import.meta.env.DEV && <PerfProbeRunner />}` gates the ONLY src/ caller. A repo-wide grep shows every other caller is in scripts/visual/*.mjs (Playwright dev probes). The shipping clock moves gameTime only via setGameTime (crossedHalfCycle) and loadWorldData (isDayAtUnit) — both bucket-convention and mutually consistent.
verdict.real_player_impact: ZERO. No player-reachable code path invokes setTimeOfDay — it is triple-gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV` and stripped from production builds. The claim concedes this itself ("player_impact: NONE directly") and then relabels the impact as "validation integrity" while retaining a MEDIUM severity — that is the inflation. verdict.reason:
The code asymmetry is REAL and I reproduced it; the player-facing premise is REFUTED.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED (executed): WeatherSystem.jsx:101 is verbatim `return () => { clearInterval(interval); if (stormBedRef.current) stormBedRef.current.stop(); };` — no setWeatherMoodBoost(0). `grep -rn setWeatherMoodBoost src/` shows the interval (WeatherSystem.jsx:68) is the field's ONLY writer; useGameStore.jsx:88-89 defines it, Atmosphere.jsx:157 reads it. I wrote and ran a vitest probe replicating the effect body against the real store singleton: after 90s boost = 0.85 (stormMoodBoost('storm') -> STORM_MOOD_BOOST, weatherGate.js:34-38), and it remains 0.85 after the cleanup runs. Probe deleted after the run (repo hygiene rule).

PLAYER PATH REFUTED: the claim concedes "HYPOTHESIS on the unmount path — I verified the missing reset, not the remount." That hypothesis is false. There is NO reachable unmount that leaves the store alive:
- <WeatherSystem /> (GameScene.jsx:220) is rendered unconditionally and sits OUTSIDE the <Suspense> boundary (GameScene.jsx:233-298), so a suspending asset cannot tear it down.
- <GameScene> (App.jsx:728) is unconditional — no key= prop, no ternary/&& guard, no router. The "GENERATING WORLD" screen (App.jsx:741) is an overlay on top, not a swap.
- "Exit to menu" does not unmount: <MenuSystem> (App.jsx:774) is a SIBLING overlay of <GameScene>, not a replacement.

- No <StrictMode>: index.jsx:103-107 is root.render(<ErrorBoundary><App /></ErrorBoundary>) — no dev double-mount either.
- The ErrorBoundary's only recovery button is window.location.reload() (index.jsx:~88) — a full page teardown that destroys the zustand module singleton, resetting weatherMoodBoost to 0.

The only unmount of WeatherSystem is page teardown, which also destroys the store that would hold the stale 0.85. NOT already fixed (git log -3: 45778e7/a8c7b71/0391ec6; no commits touch WeatherSystem.jsx) — the code is unchanged; it is simply unreachable.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None. No player can reach this state. Triggering it requires WeatherSystem to unmount while the zustand store survives, and no such path exists in the shipped app: GameScene/WeatherSystem are unconditionally rendered with no key, no StrictMode, no router, and no conditional guard; the menu is an overlay sibling rather than a route swap; and the sole unmount (page reload, incl. the ErrorBoundary's location.reload button) destroys the module-singleton store along with it, resetting the field to 0.

Severity is overstated even at LOW — the correct classification is latent/dead, not a player-facing cosmetic bug. It is worth a one-line defensive fix (add setWeatherMoodBoost(0) to the cleanup for symmetry with the stormBed.stop() call) because it would become a genuine bug the moment anyone adds a real world-switch or GameScene remount, but shipping it today costs no player anything.

verdicts_joined.title: The crystal/wand economy is a BLACK HOLE: the Crystals->Wand trade is mathematically unreachable, ore->crystal trades destroy ore for nothing, and a bought wand gives 0% mana discount. Two green gates lock the bug in place.
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/ui/TradingInterface.jsx:24-75 (executeBlockTrade/executeCrystalTrade) + :93-97 (trades table) + :144,148,151 (readouts); src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:175; src/store/useGameStore.jsx:589,595
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: `inventory` has two buckets: `blocks` (rendered/usable) and `magic` (currency). The M5 #15 'flat-bucket' fix routed EVERY purchased item into `blocks` -- including the two things that are CURRENCY read from `magic`. Result: (a) executeBlockTrade writes blocks.crystals, but the panel's Crystals readout AND the wand trade's affordability check both read magic.crystals; (b) executeCrystalTrade writes blocks.wand, but the panel readout AND applyWandFocus (the only consumer, EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:175) both read magic.wand. Nothing anywhere in src/ ever INCREMENTS magic.crystals (grep -rn 'crystals' src/ : the only write is a decrement in TradingInterface). It starts at 8. The wand costs 15. Whole ore->crystal->wand->cheaper-spells loop -- the documented B7 feature, `wandFocus.js` header: 'This closes the loop' -- is dead. The two gates that 'cover' this are BOTH readFileSync+regex and they CONTRADICT each other: tests/gates/inventory-flat-bucket-gates.test.js:26 asserts the wand goes into `blocks`, tests/gates/wand-economy-gates.test.js:20 asserts the mana math reads `magic`. Both green. And tests/integration/trading-interface.test.jsx:57 is a REAL behavioral test that asserts the bug as correct -- it seeds `magic: { crystals: 20 }`, a state the game can never produce.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
PROBE 1 (vite-node, real store): FRESH GAME magic.crystals=8, blocks.crystals=undefined. After the real executeBlockTrade body for 'Stone to Crystal': blocks.stone 16->0, blocks.crystals=1, magic.crystals STILL 8. Wand-trade row: 'Have' reads 8, need 15 -> canTrade=false. After the real executeCrystalTrade body: blocks.wand=1, magic.wand still 1 -> applyWandFocus(15, magic.wand=1)=14 (the purchased wand contributed NOTHING; with it counted it would be 13). Panel prints '-6% spell mana' -- the starting wand's discount, unchanged by the purchase.
PROBE 2 (grind simulation): seeded 1000 gold, ran the Gold->Crystal trade 500x + crafted the 'Magic Crystal' recipe 50x -> blocks.crystals = 700, magic.crystals = 8. 'Crystals to Wand' row: Have=8, Cost=15, button enabled? FALSE. PROVEN UNREACHABLE.
PROBE 3: `npx vitest run tests/integration tests/gates/wand-economy-gates.test.js tests/gates/inventory-flat-bucket-gates.test.js ...` -> 11 files / 37 tests, ALL PASSED. The bug ships green.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: A player who mines 16 stone and trades it for a crystal watches 16 stone vanish and the Crystals counter stay at 0. They can do this forever. The Crystals->Wand trade button is permanently greyed out no matter what they do. The entire merchant magic economy and the 'Magic Crystal' recipe (4x crystals) are a pure resource sink with zero output. Rated CRITICAL because it is a full advertised progression loop that cannot be completed, and the player is actively punished (ore destroyed) for engaging with it.

verdict.title: CONFIRMED: crystal/wand economy is a black hole — purchases route to inventory.blocks while the currency + consumer read inventory.magic, making Crystals→Wand mathematically unreachable and a bought wand a 0% no-op
verdict.reason: I reproduced it with my OWN probe (real TradingInterface + real Zustand store + real fresh-game loadout, rendered in jsdom via RTL; file since deleted), not the claim's. Results matched the claim exactly. (1) Fresh game: magic={wand:1,crystals:8}, blocks.crystals=undefined (useGameStore.jsx:589). (2) Clicking the real "Stone to Crystal" Trade button: blocks.stone 16->0, blocks.crystals=1, magic.crystals STILL 8; the panel's Crystals readout (TradingInterface.jsx:144, reads magic.crystals) went 8->8. (3) Grind probe: 500x Gold->Crystal + 50x "Magic Crystal" craft -> blocks.crystals=700, magic.crystals=8; the wand row still renders "Cost: 15 crystals (Have: 8)" and its Trade button is disabled===true (disabled={!canTrade}, TradingInterface.jsx:206; canTrade reads magic[t.costItem]). UNREACHABLE. (4) Forcing the purchase by seeding an impossible magic.crystals=20: blocks.wand=1 but magic.wand stays 1; applyWandFocus(15, magic.wand)=14 vs 13 if it counted (EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:175); discount readout frozen at "-6% spell mana". Cited lines are all real and say what the claim says. Exhaustive `grep -rn crystals src/`: the ONLY writes to magic.crystals are the init at useGameStore.jsx:589 and a DECREMENT at TradingInterface.jsx:62 — nothing increments it (crafting goes through addToInventory -> blocks, useGameStore.jsx:595; CraftingTable.jsx:96). NOT already fixed: worktree clean for these files, `git show HEAD:` returns identical code, and the last commits touching TradingInterface.jsx (8a65b8d, 53c7478) are the ones that CREATED this state — today's fixes 926751e/15fcc96 touch unrelated files. Two findings that STRENGTHEN the claim: `crystals`/`wand` are not registered in src/data/items.js at all, and `grep -rn 'blocks\.crystals|blocks\.wand' src/` returns ZERO consumers — so the goods are inert in the destination bucket too, and `crystals` is an input to no recipe (the "Magic Crystal" recipe burns diamond+gold for 4 permanently-useless items). Gates: I ran the 3 cited files -> 10/10 GREEN while the economy is broken; inventory-flat-bucket-gates.test.js:26 (writer->blocks) and wand-economy-gates.test.js:20 (reader->magic) are both readFileSync+regex and do contradict; trading-interface.test.jsx:57 is behavioral but seeds magic:{crystals:20}, a state the game cannot produce, certifying the bug as correct.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and on the ordinary play path — not theoretical. npcSpawn.js:11 spawns "Bram the Trader" (role:'merchant'); the G-interact opens the panel (InputManager.jsx:206 -> MenuSystem.jsx:189). A player who mines 16 stone and trades it watches the stone vanish and the merchant's Crystals counter refuse to move (it sits at the starting 8 — note the claim's prose says "stays at 0", which is wrong; the crystals DO land in the Inventory grid via blocks, GamePanels.jsx:376 — but nothing in src/ ever consumes them). They can repeat this forever across all four ore->crystal trades (16 stone / 8 coal / 4 iron / 2 gold each). The Crystals->Wand button is permanently greyed out no matter how much they grind — proven by simulating 500 trades + 50 crafts. If they somehow had a wand, it would grant 0% mana reduction. The entire B7 ore->crystal->wand->cheaper-spells loop (wandFocus.js header: "This closes the loop") is uncompletable, and the "Magic Crystal" recipe destroys diamond+gold for nothing. Severity: CRITICAL is defensible but at the top of its band — there is no crash, no save corruption, and the core mine/build/craft/fight loop is unaffected; what earns top-tier triage is a fully advertised progression loop that is 100% unreachable, irreversible resource destruction as the punishment for engaging with it, and three green tests actively defending the bug (an instance of the repo's own open backlog item #5, VACUOUS-GATE AUDIT).

verdict.title: CraftingTable destroys every material staged in the 3x3 grid when the panel is closed (X / ESC / backdrop) — no unmount refund
verdict.reason:
CITED CODE IS REAL AND ACCURATE. CraftingTable.jsx:22 `const [grid, setGrid] = React.useState(Array(9).fill(null))` — staged grid is React-local only. :79-90 handleGridClick calls `gameState.removeFromInventory(selectedBlock, 1)` on place (and addToInventory on take-back-out). MenuSystem.jsx:122-130 `{gameState.showCrafting && <CraftingTable onClose={() => { gameState.setShowCrafting(false); enterPlay(); }} />}` — close unmounts. Modal.jsx:47 `onClick={dismissOnBackdrop ? onClose : undefined}` with `dismissOnBackdrop = true` default, and CraftingTable does NOT opt out. grep of CraftingTable for `useEffect|return () =>|unmount`: exactly ONE useEffect (line 68, the recipe matcher) with NO cleanup return. There is no refund-on-unmount anywhere.

MY OWN PROBE (jsdom vitest, real CraftingTable + real useGameStore, not the claim's): start {diamond:3, wood:3}; staged Diamond Sword (cells 1,4,7) -> {diamond:1, wood:2}. Then closed via each path and unmounted (exactly as MenuSystem's conditional mount does): header X button -> {diamond:1, wood:2}; backdrop click on [role=dialog] -> {diamond:1, wood:2}; ESC/store-driven unmount -> {diamond:1, wood:2}. NEVER refunded on any of the three.

PROBE SOUNDNESS PROVEN (this matters — my FIRST run was itself broken): run 1 failed all 5 tests including its own baseline, because a bare zustand setState outside act() left a stale selectedBlock and placed 3 diamonds. I fixed it with act() and re-ran rather than reporting off a broken harness. Corrected run: BASELINE PASSES (staging consumes exactly 2 diamond + 1 wood) and CONTROL PASSES (re-clicking a filled cell refunds, diamond 1->2) — so the probe CAN see a refund when one occurs. It sees none on close. Only the 3 close-path tests fail.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: `git log -5 -- frontend/src/ui/panels/CraftingTable.jsx` -> newest is 43ecf840 "perf(ui): useShallow selectors" — a perf refactor, no refund logic. Repo HEAD is 1386b5e (docs). I read the file at HEAD directly; the destroying code is live. Unrelated to the R1/926751e quest-claim and R4/15fcc96 block-id fixes.

TEST GAP CONFIRMED: grep of tests/integration/crafting-table.test.jsx for onClose|unmount|Escape|backdrop returns 3 hits, ALL of them `onClose={() => {}}` no-op props at lines 38/53/65. The suite never closes the panel. Nothing guards this path.

Claim's own evidence transcript also checks out: recipes.js:125-127 Magic Crystal = pattern [['diamond','gold']] -> output {crystals: 4}, i.e. cells 0+1 really do show "4x Magic Crystal". The claim did not fabricate.
verdict.real_player_impact:
REAL, and reachable in one keystroke/click by three separate routes, all live on HEAD: (1) the header X Button onClick={onClose}; (2) the Modal backdrop, dismiss-on-backdrop defaults ON and CraftingTable never disables it, so any stray click outside the panel while selecting materials wipes the grid; (3) ESC — InputManager.jsx:65-71, with any panel open ESC calls state.setShowCrafting(false), the single most reflexive "close this" key in the game. Materials are removed from inventory the instant they are placed and are never given back on close: no toast, no undo, no confirmation. The loss is silent and unrecoverable.

Severity HIGH is HONEST, not inflated. It destroys diamond — mined ore, the most expensive material — and it is the same class of defect as R4 (block-id collapse destroys materials), which was treated as a genuine ship-blocker and fixed today.

AMPLIFIER I FOUND WHILE PROBING (separate latent bug, makes this one considerably worse): in my run the staged Diamond Sword showed "Empty" in the result slot — it never matched. normalizeGrid trims to the bounding box, so a null-bordered pattern like Diamond Sword [[null,'diamond',null],[null,'diamond',null],[null,'wood',null]] normalizes to a 1-wide column and can never equal its own 3-wide recipe. The existing test file's own comment concedes this ("unlike the null-bordered swords"). So the realistic player story is: stage a Diamond Sword, watch the result slot stay stubbornly Empty, give up and hit ESC — and the diamonds are gone. The broken recipe actively drives the player into the destroying action. Worth filing separately.

file:line is real: SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:40 is verbatim `absolute inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center p-4 overflow-y-auto bg-ink/75`; ChestInventoryPanel.jsx:29 carries the identical string (its content is shorter — whether it actually overflows is UNPROVEN; treat that half as unverified).

verdict.real_player_impact:
A player presses U and the panel opens with ZERO scroll offset already showing the broken state — no title, no talent-point counter, no player level, and a close X that document.elementFromPoint proves is unclickable. The entire budget readout that drives the spend decision is invisible, so the player cannot see how many points they have while deciding which talent to buy. ESC/U still close the panel, so they are not trapped (the claim disclosed this honestly rather than hiding it).

Severity HIGH is honest, and the SCOPE was actually UNDERSTATED. My viewport sweep (title visible / close X clickable): 1280x800 no/no; 1440x900 no/no; 1920x1080 no/no; 1024x1366 iPad no/no; 1280x2000 yes/yes. The claim said "every laptop and every tablet" — in fact a 1080p DESKTOP is broken too. Only a viewport taller than the 1952px panel escapes, i.e. essentially no real display short of 4K.

verdict.real_player_impact:

The player levels up, opens the Inventory to spend them, and column 1 renders 492px of content into a 400px clipped column — the entire Core Attributes panel (the "{n} points to spend" banner AND all three allocate buttons) sits below the fold at scrollTop 0, with no badge, no banner, no count, and no visible scrollbar. verdict.reason:
Re-ran my own probe (did NOT trust the claimed output). Wrote a throwaway vitest that imports the REAL modules — `src/data/recipes.js` RECIPES, `src/game/equipment.js` getItemSlot, `src/game/consumables.js` isConsumable, `src/world/blockIds.js` idForBlock — and cross-checked every output against equip/consume/place/ingredient. Result (26 recipes, 4 dead), exactly matching the claim:
  Bow -> 5x Arrow, Torch -> 4x torch, Planks -> 4x planks, Magic Crystal -> 4x crystals — all equip=null, consume=false, placeable=false, ingredient=false. file:line is REAL and says what the claim says — /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/data/recipes.js:104-127 verified with numbered output: 105-107 Bow -> {'Arrow':5}, 110-112 Torch -> {torch:4}, 120-122 Planks -> {planks:4}, 125-127 Magic Crystal -> {crystals:4}.

Mechanism traced end-to-end:
- CraftingTable.jsx:83-88 `handleGridClick` calls `removeFromInventory` for each placed ingredient -> ingredients ARE consumed.
- CraftingTable.jsx:93-97 `doCraft` -> `addToInventory(item, count)`.
- useGameStore.jsx:595 `addToInventory` writes ONLY to `inventory.blocks[item]`.
- Nothing reads those 4 keys from `inventory.blocks`. Confirmed by repo-wide grep: `crystals` is read only from `state.magic.crystals` (TradingInterface.jsx:48/62/97, wandFocus.js) — a DIFFERENT bucket than `inventory.blocks.crystals`, so the claim's "fixing the crystals bucket also fixes this" is accurate. `planks` and `torch` appear NOWHERE outside recipes.js. `Arrow` appears only in items.js:22 (registry), lootTables.js:28 (a mob drop — so Arrow is dead as loot too), and AIWorkerSystem.jsx:37 (ENEMY archer projectile, unrelated to player inventory).
- blockIds.js:93 `idForBlock` returns null for all four -> Terrain.jsx:826-827 `if (numericType === null) return;` -> place is a silent no-op.

Gate confirmed vacuous as claimed: tests/gates/recipes-gates.test.js asserts only non-empty pattern/output, cooking/potion existence, and pattern uniqueness. It never checks an output is USABLE.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — a real player hits this, and the cheapest/most obvious first craft in the game is one of the four.

Reachable: crafting panel is mounted at MenuSystem.jsx:122-129 (`showCrafting`). Planks = one `wood` in the grid; wood is a minable voxel (BLOCK_ID.wood=6). Torch = coal + wood, both minable. Magic Crystal = diamond + gold, both minable. So all four WILL be crafted.

What the player experiences:
1. Spends ingredients (removeFromInventory fires on grid placement), gets a "Crafted Planks!" success toast + 10 XP, and 4 `planks` appear in the item bag with a quantity badge — so the game affirmatively tells them it worked.
2. The 4 planks cannot be placed, worn, eaten, or used in any other recipe. Pure sink.
3. Worse — an active trap: GamePanels.jsx:386-392, clicking a non-equippable bag item runs `setSelectedBlock(type); onClose();`. So clicking your new planks sets your build cursor to `planks` and closes the inventory. Every subsequent build click is now a silent no-op (Terrain.jsx:827 refuses the null id) until the player figures out they must re-select from the hotbar. Same for torch/crystals/Arrow.
4. Magic Crystal is the expensive one: it burns a `diamond` (which is itself a 50-XP consumable per consumables.js) plus a `gold` to produce 4 inert `crystals` that do NOT feed the wand economy (that reads `magic.crystals`). Strictly value-destroying.

Severity MEDIUM is HONEST, not inflated. No crash, no save corruption, no data loss beyond the consumed ingredients — but it is a real, reachable, resource-destroying content defect on the game's most obvious first craft, plus a dead build-cursor trap. Not theoretical, not dead code.

verdict.real_player_impact: Real and reachable on turn 1 with zero prerequisites. The starting loadout ships 2 Health Potions and 1 Mana Potion inside inventory.blocks, so they render as clickable tiles in the item grid. The "Use" affordance is a tiny hover-only overlay button in the tile corner, so clicking the tile body — the natural "use this" gesture — instead falls into the else-branch: it sets selectedBlock='Health Potion' and closes the panel. The player is dropped back into the world with a dead build verb: right-click places nothing, forever, with no error, no toast, and no highlighted hotbar slot (GameHud only highlights names in HOTBAR_BLOCKS, which contains none of these). A confirmed extra confusion vector: idForBlock('Diamond') (the capital-D loot gem) === null while idForBlock('diamond') (the lowercase hotbar block) === 13, so the player can hold two things that look like diamonds where one bricks the build verb and one doesn't. Nothing is destroyed and no save is corrupted, and the player CAN recover by clicking any hotbar slot (GameHud.jsx:32) or cycling with the hotbar key (InputManager.jsx:42) — but nothing tells them that, so the game reads as broken. MEDIUM severity is honest, not inflated: very high reachability and a core voxel-builder verb dies silently, offset by full recoverability and no data loss.

Severe and central, not theoretical. Crafty is a voxel game with a night-siege loop (SpawnerSystem ramps hostile spawns with nightCount) and a block-place verb — "build to survive the night" is the core fantasy, and every vertical defense against it is a no-op.

  tick@66    player 500u -> isAggro=false windupUntil=100380   <-- de-aggroed, windup STILL ARMED

  >>> INSTANT HIT, ZERO TELEGRAPH.

verdict.title: Stale windupUntil survives de-aggro — but it is consumed harmlessly at the aggro edge; no zero-telegraph hit is reachable
verdict.reason:
The cited code is REAL and the state leak is REAL, but the player-facing consequence is fabricated by an impossible probe input.

VERIFIED TRUE (premise): /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/workers/ai.worker.js:280-287 (the windup gate) sits inside `if (isAggro)` (line 177); the de-aggro/wander `else` branch (line ~319) never clears `windupUntil`. The value round-trips and persists: worker:357 -> AIWorkerSystem.jsx:92 (`entity.windupUntil = update.windupUntil`) -> AIWorkerSystem.jsx:194 (sent back next tick). Still present on HEAD (1386b5e); `git log -- frontend/src/workers/ai.worker.js` shows no recent fix. My probe reproduced the stale carry: `respawn d=100 isAggro=false windupUntil=100380`.

REFUTED (consequence): I loaded the REAL worker with a fake `self` and drove real 15Hz TICKs (/private/tmp/.../windup-refute-probe2.mjs). Constants: AGGRO_RANGE=20, MELEE_RANGE=2.5, de-aggro at >30 (ai.worker.js:125-129). The stale windup is CONSUMED HARMLESSLY on the first re-aggro tick, because re-aggro fires at 20u — 17.5u OUTSIDE melee range — so `pendingAttack` is null and the gate simply does `windupUntil = 0` and pushes no attack:
  re-aggro  d=19.2 -> windupUntil AFTER tick = 0, attacks=0
Running the claim's OWN cited path (die -> respawn teleport -> walk back -> stand and fight) the player gets a FULL 400ms telegraph (>= WINDUP_MS 380):
  melee-in d=2.21 windupUntil=0 attacks THIS tick=0
  HIT      d=1.07 at +400ms after melee entry

The claim's "executed evidence" only fires because it teleports the player 500u -> 2u in ONE tick, landing INSIDE melee range. A sweep (Scenario C) shows the instant hit fires ONLY when the single-tick jump lands at d<2.5; at d=5/10/19.9/25 it does not. Required jump: >=17.5u in one 66ms tick. Max player travel = BASE_MOVE_SPEED 14 (locomotion.js:3) / 15Hz = 0.93u/tick — 19x short.

No mechanic produces such a jump. The ONLY player teleport is the respawn coordinator the claim itself cites (Components.jsx:216 `setTranslation({x:0,y:120,z:0})`, :222 `camera.position.set(0,121.2,0)`) — it moves the player TO spawn, AWAY from mobs, never into one. Components.jsx:524 is capture-mode camera pinning, and capture mode disables AI ticks entirely (AIWorkerSystem.jsx:137). SquadAISystem.jsx:31-36 `teleports` move ALLIES (alliesQuery), not the player. Knockback moves mobs away, ~1u/frame.

No cosmetic impact either: MobModel.jsx:164/181 gate the charge pose on `performance.now() < entity.windupUntil`, so a stale (past) windup renders nothing.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None. The claimed scenario — "respawn, walk back, first hit from every mob lands instantly with no tell" — is exactly what I simulated on the real worker, and the player receives the full 400ms telegraph. The stale windup self-disarms at the 20u aggro boundary, 17.5u before the mob can ever reach melee range, so the walk-back itself defuses it. Triggering the instant hit requires teleporting the player >=17.5u directly into melee in a single 66ms tick; no such mechanic exists (every teleport in the codebase goes to spawn coordinates x=0,z=0, i.e. away from mobs).

Residual (not the claimed bug): a genuine state-hygiene wart — the de-aggro branch should set `windupUntil = 0`. Worth a one-line cleanup for robustness (it would matter if a future teleport/blink/portal mechanic ever displaced the player into melee range), but on current HEAD it has zero gameplay and zero visual effect. Severity is inflated: HIGH -> LOW/cleanup.

verdicts_joined.title: SpawnerSystem's spawn loop can spin forever on the main thread — `attempts++` sits INSIDE the distance guard, so rejected samples never count against maxAttempts.
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/systems/SpawnerSystem.jsx:163-178 (`while (spawnedThisTick < spawnCount && attempts < maxAttempts)`; `attempts++` is on line 172, inside `if (dist >= 28 && dist <= 85)`)

If the loaded-chunk set contains no chunk overlapping the [28,85]u annulus around the player, the loop never exits — inside a `useFrame`, on the main thread.   A. healthy 5x5 chunk box, player at origin: {"spawned":3,"attempts":3,"iters":7} — terminates fine.

     chunk center (8,8) is 11.3u away -> fails the [20,90] pre-filter -> candidateChunks EMPTY
     -> fallback re-admits ['0_0'] -> every sampled point is <= 22.6u -> `dist >= 28` NEVER true

Terrain.jsx:677-678 requests chunks corner-first (nx=-renderDistance upward, 2 per tick), so the FAR chunks land before the near ones and candidateChunks is non-empty at startup. This is a proven-non-terminating loop whose trigger state I have not proven reachable.

verdict.title: Cover-seeking LOS passes unclamped player coords into a 9x9 grid index that silently wraps rows — wounded mobs "hide" in fully exposed cells (and skeletons are affected 100% of the time)
verdict.reason: Tried to refute; could not. (1) CITATION EXACT: frontend/src/workers/ai.worker.js:185-186 computes relPlayerX/relPlayerZ with no clamp, :202 passes them straight into hasLineOfSight, while :302-303 in the sibling A* branch DOES clamp with Math.max(0,Math.min(8,...)). `git show HEAD:...| sed -n '185,202p' | grep -c "Math.max(0, Math.min(8"` => 0. (2) NOT FIXED: tree clean, ai.worker.js absent from `git status`, HEAD=1386b5e; last touch to the file was c01e244 (unrelated melee-id fix). (3) REPRODUCED WITH REAL CODE: loaded ai.worker.js into a Node `vm` sandbox and drove it via self.onmessage (no reimplementation of the logic under test). Probe 1 wrapped heightGrid in a Proxy tracing every index read: hasLineOfSight(grid,0,4,14,4) reads idx 50 (=cell (5,5), exactly as claimed) plus idx 45,46,47,48,49 — all in row z=5, though a +X ray from z=4 must never leave row 4. Row-wrap confirmed. (4) MECHANISM PROVEN: wounded zombie at (0,0), wall at world x=-3 (BEHIND it), player 10u away at +X. HEAD picks cell (4,3) = world (0,-1) as "cover" — fully exposed, wall on the opposite side. The false "blocked" verdict arises because px climbs past 8 and idx=px+pz*9 wraps into row z=5, reading grid(1,5) h=10 — the wall column, from a row the ray never crosses. Same real LOS fn with only the clamp added picks [0,4] (world x=-4, genuinely behind the wall) at every tested distance. (5) REACHABLE: AIWorkerSystem.jsx:167-181 genuinely builds the 81-cell grid for every aggroed non-passive mob, so the heightGrid.length===81 gate is satisfied in normal play. Probe scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kz-Code/c7297111-afb7-46c9-83b3-6edc09ed7f41/scratchpad/los-wrap-probe-kz.mjs and los-mechanism-kz.mjs.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, and the claim UNDERSTATES it in two ways. Trigger is just "a mob you wounded below 25% while it's aggroed"; relPlayer goes out of grid range whenever the player is more than ~4 units away — i.e. most of the 20-unit aggro range. It is self-inflicted: cover-seeking's own retreat (with its 1.2x coverBoost) is what pushes the player out of range, so the feature corrupts itself the moment it starts working. (a) The claim says the wrap only corrupts WHICH cell is chosen, "not whether cover-seeking fires at all" — false: at playerX=6, isCoverSeeking comes back FALSE and the wounded mob falls through to the melee branch and CHARGES the player (targetX=1.0) instead of retreating. (b) SKELETONS ARE AFFECTED 100% OF THE TIME — their archery logic deliberately holds 8-12 units, and relPlayerX is out of range at every distance in that band (12..16), so the one class that most obviously wants cover never once computes a valid LOS. Player-visible result: wounded mobs duck into open ground they believe is cover, ignore real cover right next to them, or abandon the retreat and charge. Reads as flaky/dumb AI, which is why it survived. Severity MEDIUM is HONEST — no crash/exploit/progress-loss (JS OOB reads yield undefined, which the `>` comparison silently swallows as "not blocking"), but a shipped feature is functionally wrong across the majority of its operating range. Fix mirrors line 302-303: clamp relPlayerX/relPlayerZ to [0,8]; ideally also bounds-check idx inside hasLineOfSight, which is the function that indexes without a guard.

verdict.reason:

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kz-Code/c7297111-afb7-46c9-83b3-6edc09ed7f41/scratchpad/leap-refute-kz.mjs

CAVEAT ON MY OWN FIRST RUN: my initial probe showed 0 leaps and nearly refuted the claim, but that was MY artifact — I started `now` near 0, whereas the real game passes performance.now() (large) against a freshly-spawned mob's lastAttackTime=0. With the realistic baseline (now=50000), the claim's table reproduces BIT-FOR-BIT: zombie 110, skeleton 0(bridge-immediate), spider 80 {leap:1, melee:10}, skitterling 55, duskhound 132, moss_brute 275, emberhusk 143. Spider DPS 4.00 < zombie 5.50.

(1) Cited lines are real and exact. AIWorkerSystem.jsx:41 `} else if (attack.type === 'leap') {` sets entity.knockback and falls out; `store.damagePlayer(attack.damage, ...)` sits at :54, reachable ONLY via the final `else` — so leap damage is silently dropped. ai.worker.js:261 stages `pendingAttack = { id, type:'leap', damage: 8, ... }` and :283 stamps `lastAttackTime = now` when it fires, burning ATTACK_COOLDOWN (1500ms, ai.worker.js:130).
(2) Dead vertical impulse CONFIRMED: knockback loop at AIWorkerSystem.jsx:145-146 reads ONLY knockback[0] and knockback[2]; the `8` at index [1] (author-commented `// Vertical boost`) is never read.
(3) 1-unit nudge CONFIRMED by measurement, not arithmetic: probe's maxLeapStep = 1.00 units at 60fps (15 * 1/60 * 4). Frame-rate dependent — only 0.5u on a 120Hz ProMotion iPad.
(4) NOT a downstream-damage false alarm: exhaustive grep finds only 4 `leap` refs repo-wide (hurl.js comment, ai.worker.js:261, AIWorkerSystem.jsx:41/51). No leap-damage system exists anywhere.
(5) NOT fixed on HEAD (1386b5e). `git status --short` on both files is clean = matches HEAD. Last commits touching them: f1f7f4d (refactor extraction) and c01e244 (unrelated melee-payload fix).

TWO FLAWS IN THE CLAIM'S EVIDENCE (neither undermines the finding): (a) its `skeleton = 0 DPS` row is a methodology artifact — skeleton arrows DO deal 15 damage downstream at EnemyProjectileSystem.jsx:42. The claim's wording "melee is the only attack type the bridge converts into damagePlayer" is literally true OF THE BRIDGE, but the table implies the skeleton is harmless, which is false. The leap is different precisely because it has NO downstream path. (b) "fastest hostile (speed 3.0)" understates the base table (skitterling 3.8, duskhound 3.2), but the spider's 2.0x aggro multiplier (ai.worker.js:342, vs 1.5x for all others) makes the chasing spider 6.0 u/s — genuinely fastest, so the framing holds.
verdict.real_player_impact: Yes — and more reachable than the claim argues. Because a freshly-spawned mob has lastAttackTime = 0, the leap gate (`now - lastAttackTime > ATTACK_COOLDOWN + 1000`) is ALWAYS open on first contact, so EVERY spider engagement opens with a 0-damage pounce: the player sees the telegraphed windup (380ms), the spider lunges ~1 unit horizontally with no vertical arc, deals nothing, and then cannot melee for another 1500ms+windup. Leaps also recur whenever the player kites in the 2.5-6.0u band (MELEE_RANGE 2.5 < dist < LEAP_RANGE 6), where melee cannot fire and the cooldown builds past the leap threshold — my sprint-kite scenario (player at 5.5 u/s) produced 2 leaps = 16 damage discarded in 20s. Net effect: the mob billed as the fast aggressive leaper lands 4.00 DPS vs the slow zombie's 5.50, and its signature move is a visual no-op. Severity MEDIUM is honest — a balance/feel bug, not a crash or data-loss, and the claim did not inflate it.

   DAY tier0     -> HOSTILE SHARE 70.2%  (maxMobs 16)
   NIGHT 0 tier0 -> 91.0%                (hostileChance 0.70, maxMobs 16)
   NIGHT 6 tier0 -> 98.5%                (hostileChance 0.95, maxMobs 40)
   Analytic: hostileW=6.15 (zombie/skeleton/spider 1.0 ea, skitterling 1.2, duskhound 0.9, emberhusk 0.8, moss_brute 0.25) vs passiveW=2.60 (pig 1, cow 1, villager 0.6) -> 6.15/8.75 = 70.29%. Constants verified: dayNight.js:75 DAY_MAX_MOBS=16, :78 DAY_HOSTILE_CHANCE=0.7, SIEGE_HOSTILE_CAP=0.95, 16+24=40. The claimant's numbers are accurate.

(3) NOT FIXED ON HEAD. git log for the file: last touch is 11b5637 "refactor(de-monolith): extract SpawnerSystem" (behavior-preserving). The else branch is live. Unrelated to the R1/quest-claim (926751e) and R4/block-id (15fcc96) fixes.

(4) NOT A DESIGN CHOICE — IT IS DRIFT (evidence the claimant missed). At 64fc55c2~1 (pre mob-variety-pass) the day roll was a UNIFORM pick — `type = mobTypeKeys[Math.floor(Math.random()*mobTypeKeys.length)]` — over 6 types, 3 passive (pig/cow/villager) + 3 hostile (zombie/skeleton/spider) = EXACTLY 50.0% hostile. That is the balance the "calm day baseline" comment was written against. Two content passes then added 4 HOSTILE types and 0 passive types (64fc55c2 variety trio 2026-06-11; 136bfbd emberhusk 2026-06-14). Because the neutral day roll spans the whole registry with NO passive floor, day hostility silently drifted 50.0% -> 70.3% (+20.3 pts). Nobody picked 70%, and it keeps drifting with every future hostile mob.

(5) BONUS DEFECT (adjacent, not the claim): dayNight.js:90-91 documents the S7 zone-tier as adding "mobs + hostility even by DAY" and SpawnerSystem.jsx:39 repeats it — but the `!store.isDay &&` gate discards the tier hostility bias by day. Probe: DAY tier4 computes hostileChance=0.86 yet hostile share stays 70.4%, identical to tier0. Only maxMobs (16->24) applies. S7's day-hostility is not implemented.

SEVERITY: claimed LOW and self-flagged as design-intent mismatch — honest, arguably conservative. No inflation.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — fully reachable in normal gameplay, and the player fights hostiles all day.

The spawner's useFrame path is gated only on isCaptureMode(), so it runs every 1s in real play, filling to maxMobs=16 concurrent by day. At 70.3% hostile that is ~11 aggro-capable hostiles roaming in broad daylight.

I specifically hunted for a mechanism that would make day calm anyway, and there is none:
- No dawn-burn / no day-despawn: grep for burn|sunlight|despawn across src/systems/ + dayNight.js returns nothing.
- No day-aggro suppression: the ONLY isDay in the mob AI (AIWorkerSystem.jsx:121-125) drives the villager routine (routinePosition), not hostility.
- ai.worker.js:170 aggros on DISTANCE ALONE — `if (!passive && distToPlayer2D < AGGRO_RANGE) isAggro = true` — with no day condition, plus pack-aggro pulling nearby mobs within 12 units (ai.worker.js:137-148).

So daytime never reads as a respite: the player is still fighting ~7 hostiles for every 3 passives, and the ONLY real day/night signal left is the mob CAP (16 -> up to 40), exactly as the claim states. This mutes the day/night contrast the entire siege system exists to sell — the game's core survival tension. The 50%->70.3% drift means the "calm day" the comment promises actually existed once and was lost to unreviewed content additions.

Fix shape (numbers are Kevin's balance call): give the day/neutral roll a passive floor — a separate day weighting table or a passiveChance on the day branch — so future hostile content cannot silently re-balance daytime again.

verdict.title: Ocean plane renders inside inland caves near spawn — real bug, but the claim's evidence and severity are both wrong

CODE: Ocean.jsx:38-60 is real and as cited (ungated useFrame, mesh.position.set(cx, SEA_LEVEL, cz), frustumCulled={false}); GameScene.jsx:212 mounts <Ocean /> unconditionally with no guard (grep: only the import + the bare mount). Worldgen (terrain.worker.js:444-449) proves air at y=28 can ONLY be cave-carved: `y > surfaceY && y <= SEA_LEVEL => block 9 (water)`, so no dry above-ground air at 28.

Live scene inspection shows material side=0 (THREE.FrontSide) => the plane is back-facing and CULLED from below. The claim never mentions culling; its "I can SEE a turquoise plane slicing through a rock cavern" capture at (-19, 26, -30) does not reproduce.

Nearest is 13 blocks from spawn (feet y=32, eye y=34.1) in a 13,858-cell cavern: rendered 22,657 px / 5.45% of frame ocean-attributable turquoise; ocean-OFF control = 0% turquoise.
verdict.real_player_impact:
YES, real but narrower than claimed. A player exploring the large cavern system 13 blocks from spawn, standing on a genuine cave floor (1,124 such standable spots in 169 chunks) and looking down/across, sees a bright animated turquoise sea filling the cave — with zero actual water anywhere in 169 chunks. Verified by rendered A/B from a real player eye position. Immersion/visual-integrity bug: the cave looks flooded and the "water" is fake.

BUT the claim's severity framing is inverted and inflated. The plane is FrontSide, so it is INVISIBLE from below — and the claim's own argument ("the ENTIRE mid/late mining game happens below the phantom sea": gold <=y25, diamond <=y9) describes exactly the region where the artifact CANNOT be seen. The bug only manifests when the eye clears y=28 with cave air below it in view — a band around sea level, not the whole underground. No crash, no data loss, no progression block. verdicts_joined.title: Ocean.jsx burns ~14% of the 60fps frame budget everywhere in the world — including underground and 1.1km from the nearest water
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/render/Ocean.jsx:38-60 (useFrame body; only guard is `if (!mesh) return`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The useFrame sweeps ALL 9,409 plane vertices every frame: gerstnerHeight + gerstnerNormal (4 sin + 4 cos each), a THREE.MathUtils.smoothstep, and 6 BufferAttribute get/set calls per vertex — then flags position + normal + color needsUpdate, re-uploading 331 KB to the GPU per frame. verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: Measured by importing the REAL oceanProfile.js and running the exact per-vertex math for 9,409 vertices x 120 frames in node/V8: 2.37 ms/frame of gerstner math alone = 14.2% of a 16.67 ms frame — and that EXCLUDES the BufferAttribute get/set churn and the 331 KB/frame upload that the real useFrame also pays. Executed transect: the nearest water on +X is 1,144 blocks from spawn, so at spawn this cost buys literally zero visible pixels.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: A flat ~14%+ frame-budget tax at spawn, in every forest, and inside every cave — for a plane that is invisible or buried in rock. iPad/touch is a shipped target (touch-probe gate exists); this is exactly the budget a mobile GPU cannot spare.

verdict.title: Ocean.jsx useFrame does an ungated 9,409-vertex CPU sweep + 331 KB GPU re-upload every frame, everywhere (incl. underground) — but the claim's "14%" and "1.1km from water" numbers are inflated/cherry-picked
verdict.reason:
STRUCTURE (all verified at HEAD): Ocean.jsx:38-60 useFrame's only guard is `if (!mesh) return` — no distance/proximity/camera-height/visibility/quality-tier gate. `<Ocean />` is mounted unconditionally at GameScene.jsx:212, and GameScene.jsx:125 `<Canvas>` has NO `frameloop` prop, so R3F defaults to "always" → the sweep runs every frame. `git status` on Ocean.jsx is clean vs HEAD; last commit touching it is 4d412df (2026-06-20), untouched by today's 926751e/15fcc96. NOT already fixed.

MY OWN MEASUREMENT (node, importing the REAL oceanProfile.js + real THREE.PlaneGeometry, replicating the exact useFrame body incl. all 6 BufferAttribute get/set calls, 600 frames after JIT warmup): vertex count = 9,409 (claim exact), re-upload = 331 KB/frame (claim exact), FULL body = 1.68 ms/frame = ~10.1% of a 16.67 ms frame.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS INFLATED: it asserts "2.37 ms/frame of gerstner math ALONE ... EXCLUDES the BufferAttribute get/set churn". My run of the ENTIRE body including that churn is 1.68 ms — less than what the claim attributes to the math alone. So 14.2% is overstated (~10% real). Its cost model ("4 sin + 4 cos each") also ignores that oceanProfile.js already precomputes _WAVES_D.

WHERE THE CLAIM CHERRY-PICKED: "nearest water 1,144 blocks" only measured the +X transect. Running the real seeded noise (lcg(12345) + createNoise2D + computeHeight + oceanSurfaceY): +X=1144 (reproduces), -X=102, +Z=655, -Z=855; true nearest water = 102 blocks. The plane is 220m (±110m around camera), and 3.2% of its footprint at spawn IS water. So "at spawn this buys literally zero visible pixels" is FALSE — and heightAt.js:31's own comment ("nearest deep water ... 98m") already contradicted the claimant.

The defect survives regardless, since it never depended on the spawn framing.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real but smaller than advertised. Every player pays an ungated ~1.68 ms/frame main-thread CPU sweep (~10% of a 60fps budget on a fast M-series Mac) plus a 331 KB/frame GPU re-upload, in EVERY location — including inside caves where the y=28 plane is fully buried in rock, and deep inland where it is occluded. There is genuinely no visibility, distance, or camera-height gate, so the cost is paid for pixels that are often never drawn. iPad/touch is a shipped target and JS there runs several times slower, so the proportional tax is materially worse on the platform least able to absorb it. However, the claim's dramatic framing ("1.1km from the nearest water", "zero visible pixels at spawn") is wrong: nearest water is 102 blocks and the ocean plane covers real water at spawn. Honest severity is MEDIUM-HIGH, not HIGH — a cheaply-fixable frame-budget tax (add a water-proximity/camera-height early-out), not corruption or a crash.

verdicts_joined.title: Greedy meshing destroys vertex AO — contact shadows vanish, and the ones that survive smear across 64-block quads
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/world/terrain.worker.js:757,760 (merge key = `blockType | (dir << 8)`; AO is NOT in the key) + :890-896 (AO sampled only at the merged quad's 4 corners)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The classic greedy-mesh + AO bug: faces with DIFFERENT true AO get merged into one quad because AO is not part of the mask key, and the merged quad then carries AO only at its 4 corners. The GPU bilinearly interpolates those 4 values across the whole quad, so a 1-block contact shadow becomes an 8x8-block gradient — or disappears entirely if the occluder isn't at a corner.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: Drove the REAL worker (load_modifications + generate) with a synthetic chunk: flat stone plane at y<=40, air above, ONE stone block at (8,41,8). The emitted top (+Y) faces were 4 quads of area 128 / 64 / 56 / 7 blocks. Printed cornerAO: the 128-block quad ADJACENT to the pillar reads [3,3,3,3] — NO shadow at all. The 64-block quad reads [2,3,3,3] — a single AO=2 vertex, so the pillar's contact shadow is smeared across 8x8 blocks of ground. Total vertices with AO<3 on the entire plane: 4. A correct per-face AO would darken ~12 face-corners immediately around the block.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Every tree, cliff edge and player-placed block either casts NO contact shadow or smears a large soft dark gradient across the terrain. The S1 'vertex AO' feature is effectively dead on exactly the large flat surfaces (plains, plateaus, the player's own builds) where it would read most — and where it does fire, it reads as a lighting artifact, not a shadow.
verdicts_joined.domain: World: terrain, biomes, ocean, worldgen

verdict.title: Greedy meshing destroys vertex AO — AO absent from the merge key, then sampled only at merged-quad corners
verdict.reason:
Cited lines are real and accurate. terrain.worker.js:757,760 set `mask[cu + cv * sizeU] = blockA | (1 << 8)` — merge key is blockType|dir<<8, AO genuinely not in it. :890-896 sample AO only at the merged quad's 4 corners, clamped to quad extremes (`nu = gu === cu ? cu : cu + w - 1`).

NOT FIXED on HEAD (a8c7b71): `git diff HEAD` on the mesher is empty (worktree==HEAD), and `git log -- terrain.worker.js vertexAO.js` shows the recent touches were 15fcc96 (R4a block-ids) and a5e763c (debris color) — neither touched the AO/merge-key code. Not stale R1/R4 territory.

I re-ran the evidence with MY OWN probe (scratchpad/ao_probe.mjs), driving the REAL worker file via its real message API (init -> load_modifications overriding every voxel -> generate). Reproduced the claim's numbers EXACTLY: 4 ground quads of area 128/64/56/7; the 128-block quad adjacent to the pillar reads cornerAO=[3,3,3,3] (zero shadow); 4 dark vertices emitted vs 12 correct per-face. Claim was not fabricated.

Real-terrain probe (ao_fidelity2.mjs, 10 generated chunks, no overrides): 59.6% of +Y quads are merged (mean 3.08 blocks, largest 64). On merged quads, 12540/22376 corners (56.0%) carry WRONG AO, mean error 0.47 on the 0..3 scale, max error 3.00 (full-scale). 5,964 corners that should be fully lit render visibly darkened; 162 shadow corners vanish outright.

Probe validated (anti-vacuous control): my occupancy reconstruction, rebuilt from the mesher's own emitted Y-faces, reproduces the mesher's AO with 0 mismatches across 3,552 unmerged 1x1 quad corners. So the merged-quad deltas are real, not harness artifacts.

Live path, not dead code: Terrain.jsx:8 `import TerrainWorker from './terrain.worker.js?worker'`; Terrain.jsx:199 binds meshData.ao to the `aAO` attribute; Terrain.jsx:139 applies it unconditionally (no feature flag) as `diffuseColor.rgb *= mix(0.55, 1.0, clamp(vAO/3.0, 0.0, 1.0))` — up to 45% albedo swing. GameScene.jsx:21 imports MinecraftWorld from world/Terrain.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, a player sees this. The mesher is the only terrain mesher, runs on every chunk, and its AO output feeds an unconditional shader multiply (0.55x..1.0x albedo). On real generated terrain 59.6% of the top faces a player walks on/looks at are merged quads, and 56% of those quads' corners carry wrong AO with errors up to the full 0..3 scale.

Severity is directionally right but the claim's HEADLINE is somewhat inflated. "Contact shadows vanish" is fully true only on FLAT surfaces — plains, plateaus, and player-built platforms (my synthetic flat-plane repro: adjacent quad reads [3,3,3,3], 4 dark vertices vs 12 correct; a 16x16 player platform produced a single 128-block quad). On typical rolling terrain 61.7% of shadow corners are still exactly correct and only 1.9% vanish outright.

The honest dominant real-terrain symptom is the SECOND half of the claim: SMEAR. 5,964 corners that should be fully lit are rendered darkened, because a single dark corner AO bilinearly bleeds across quads up to 64 blocks. That reads as a soft dark lighting artifact drifting across the ground, not as a contact shadow. So: real, pervasive, player-visible degradation of the shipped S1 vertex-AO feature — but cosmetic (no crash, no data loss, no progression block). I'd rate MEDIUM-HIGH rather than HIGH.

Standard fix is well-known: fold the 4 corner AO values into the greedy mask key so faces with differing AO cannot merge.

Housekeeping: prior agents left stray probe files in the repo — frontend/src/world/__probe.mjs, __probe_worker.mjs, __refute_worker.mjs. I ignored them and wrote my own probes in scratchpad; those three should be deleted.

verdict.title: 26-28% of terrain geometry is permanently invisible — chunk-boundary walls emitted against phantom air, buried in the neighbour chunk
verdict.reason: I tried to refute and failed on every angle. (1) REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY: copied terrain.worker.js byte-identically (diff-verified, only an `export {generateChunkData, generateMesh}` line appended), drove the REAL init path at the app's real seed 12345 (Terrain.jsx:31), ran the real generator+mesher, and classified every emitted quad against independently generated neighbour chunks. Chunk (2,2) => 1484 quads / 2968 tris, 386 buried quads (26.0%), 772 wasted tris — EXACTLY matching the claim, derived without reading their probe. Aggregated over the real loaded set (renderDistance high=4 => 9x9=81 chunks): 35,612 / 126,667 quads = 28.1% buried (71,224 of 253,334 tris). Claim is if anything understated. (2) NOT ALREADY FIXED: `git diff HEAD -- frontend/src/world/terrain.worker.js` is empty; last commit touching the file is 15fcc96, which is the R4a block-id fix and never touched the mesher. (3) CITED LINE IS REAL: terrain.worker.js:708-711 is exactly `getBlock`, returning 0 for any out-of-chunk coord; the sweep at line 723 runs `for (let q = -1; q < sizeD; q++)`, so both the x/z=0 and x/z=16 boundary planes emit faces against phantom air. (4) REACHES THE GPU: worker output is uploaded verbatim as BufferAttributes (Terrain.jsx:192-200) with no main-thread filtering, and the mesh is `castShadow receiveShadow` (Terrain.jsx:216), so buried geometry is vertex-processed in BOTH the shadow pass and the main pass every frame; three.js frustum-culls per mesh, not per quad. (5) LAST REFUTATION ANGLE CLOSED: I checked whether buried faces could be visible through non-opaque backing (leaves/glass) — the terrain material is `transparent: false` with no alphaTest (Terrain.jsx:37-41), so every block type renders fully opaque and a face backed by any solid voxel (>0, !=9; water=9 excluded since solid-vs-water faces ARE intentionally visible) is genuinely unviewable. Classification holds for all backing types. Probe files cleaned up; repo left unmodified.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, continuous, and measurable — not theoretical. At renderDistance high (81 loaded chunks), ~71,224 of 253,334 terrain triangles (28.1%) are permanently unviewable yet are uploaded to VRAM and vertex-shaded every single frame, twice (shadow pass + main pass), because the terrain mesh casts and receives shadows and nothing culls per-quad. This is a pure ~28% waste of the vertex/memory/index-buffer cost of the largest geometry in the game, which matters most on the weakest target (iPad). Severity MEDIUM is honest and arguably conservative (measured 28.1% vs claimed 26%): there is no visual corruption, no crash, and nothing the player can SEE going wrong — it is a silent perf tax. IMPORTANT for whoever fixes it: the claim correctly discloses that this redundancy is load-bearing. Those boundary faces are exactly what lets a cross-chunk block edit render correctly without re-meshing the neighbour chunk. The fix must be neighbour-aware meshing (feed the 4 neighbour edge-slices into getBlock and re-mesh neighbours on boundary edits), NOT simply suppressing boundary faces — suppressing them would punch permanent holes in the terrain the moment a player mines a block at a chunk edge.

verdict.title: Caves are systematically pinched at every chunk boundary — the CA treats out-of-chunk neighbours as solid stone
verdict.reason:

I reproduced it with my OWN probe rather than trusting the claim: I copied terrain.worker.js byte-for-byte into two modules whose only difference was the `applyCellularAutomata(blocks)` call at line 477 (confirmed by `diff` showing exactly one changed line), appended an export, and drove the REAL generateChunkData with the app's real seed 12345 (Terrain.jsx:31). No re-implementation, so the generator could not be fabricated.

Results over 121 chunks, y 1..18, restricted to fully-underground columns:
- CA ON (shipped): air% by local x = 18.9 at x0, 18.5 at x15, ~23.5 mid; z0=16.9, z15=17.3. Seam connectivity (A[x=15] air AND B[x=0] air, physically adjacent voxels) = 4362/31680 = 13.8%, vs identical INTERIOR plane (x=7|x=8) = 6408/31680 = 20.2% → caves 1.47x less likely to pass a chunk seam.
- CA OFF (control, raw 3D noise only): x0=26.8, x15=26.3, mid=24.5 — edge bias GONE (ratio 0.92). Seam=23.3% vs interior=21.3% (ratio 0.91, i.e. no penalty).
The control is decisive: the 3D noise is continuous across chunks and the CA is the SOLE cause. My numbers match the claim's almost exactly (claim: 18.9/18.5/16.9/17.3, 1.45x; mine: 18.9/18.5/16.9/17.3, 1.47x) — the evidence was not fabricated.

Mechanism probe (pre-CA air -> post-CA solid): the CA back-fills 29.5% of noise-carved cave air at x=0 and 29.7% at x=15, versus 4.2% mid-chunk — a 7x destruction rate exactly at the seams. Consistent with the arithmetic: at x=0, 9 of the 27 neighbours are out-of-chunk and forced to 3, so solidCount starts at 9, making the `solidCount >= 16 -> fill with stone` rule fire constantly and `solidCount <= 11 -> carve` nearly impossible; corners have 15 of 27 forced solid.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, real and player-facing. The CA's active band (caRangeHeight = 20, loop y=1..18) coincides exactly with the game's dense-cave layer (`caveThreshold = y < 20 ? 0.3 : 0.45`, terrain.worker.js:456) and contains the cobblestone dungeon chambers (`dCenterY = 12`, line 264) plus the depth-banded ores that exist to reward mining. So the defect covers the entire underground content zone that players explore, tunnel through, and loot — not dead code.

Concretely: ~30% of the cave volume the noise carves at every chunk border is back-filled with stone (vs 4.2% mid-chunk), and a cave passage is 1.47x less likely to continue through a chunk seam than through an identical interior plane. Cave systems get systematically chopped and pinched on a regular 16-block grid, producing dead-ends and narrowings aligned to the chunk lattice, degrading exploration and tunnelling.

Severity MEDIUM is honest. One correction to the claim's prose: "a 16-block lattice of stone ribs" overstates the visual — the border planes are still 18.9% air, so they read as denser walls and pinched passages, not literal solid rib walls. The substance (systematic seam pinching, halved cross-seam connectivity) is fully real. This is a worldgen quality/traversal defect, not a crash, data-loss, or progression blocker — MEDIUM, not HIGH.
