verdict.title: The spawn chunk is ALWAYS a dungeon chunk — sin(0) = 0
verdict.reason:
Reproduced independently with my own harness (I ignored the prior agents' __probe*.mjs files). Built /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/world/__kzharness.mjs as a diff-verified byte-identical copy of terrain.worker.js + a `self` shim, then ran the REAL generateChunkData.

(1) MATH: terrain.worker.js:250-253 is exactly `const hash = Math.sin(dcx*12.9898 + dcz*78.233) * 43758.5453; return (hash - Math.floor(hash)) < 0.025;`. At (0,0), sin(0)=0 -> hash=0 -> frac=0 -> 0 < 0.025 is unconditionally TRUE. Ran it: `isDungeonChunk(0,0) = true`. Rate over 81x81 chunks = 176/6561 = 2.68%, matching the claim's number exactly.

(2) NOT FIXED: `git show HEAD:frontend/src/world/terrain.worker.js | sed -n '250,253p'` still emits the sin hash; `git diff HEAD` on that file is empty (worktree == HEAD). HEAD = a8c7b71. Unrelated to the R1/R4 fixes (926751e, 15fcc96).

(3) LIVE PATH, NOT DEAD CODE: generateChunkData is invoked at terrain.worker.js:57 and :106 (the chunk-gen + mesh message handler). stampStructures (:255, called :480) stamps the dungeon; stampHomeAnchor/stampHub run after at :639/:642.

(4) SURVIVES INTO THE FINAL CHUNK — decisive control sweep. The dungeon signature blocks are UNIQUE to chunk (0,0): treasure(id4)=1, marble(id5)=8, wood pillars(id6)=34 at y=12..17; every control chunk tested ((1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,2),(3,-1),(-2,3),(5,5)) has treasure=0 and marble=0. The altar block (id 4) lands at exactly world (8,13,8) across seeds 12345, 777 and 424242.

(5) CLAIM'S OWN HEDGE IS TOO GENEROUS TO THE CODE: it says the Hearth "fill[s] most of the room back in with stone." Not so — homeAnchor.js:45-47 only converts air/water to stone (`if (b === 0 || b === 9)`) and only inside |wx|,|wz| <= 7 (HEARTH_RADIUS=7), while the room spans world x,z in [2,14]. ~3/4 of the room is outside the Hearth footprint. My rendered y=13 slice shows a genuinely OPEN, half-carved room with the altar fully intact (T centre, M marble ring, P corner pillars). The artifact is more exposed than the claim asserts, not less.

(6) SEVERITY HONEST: `grep -rni dungeon frontend/src` (excluding the worker) returns zero functional refs — no mobs, no loot, no quests hang off dungeons; the "treasure block" is just Sand (id 4). So this is world-gen determinism/quality, not progression or data loss. LOW is accurate, arguably conservative. Proposed fix verified as real: landmarks.js:10 and oreGen.js:23 already use a proper Math.imul hash.

Cleaned up my harness artifacts afterward.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real but modest — LOW is the right call. Every world, on every seed, deterministically contains a dungeon room directly under spawn: world x,z in [2,14], y=12..17, with the altar at (8,13,8) — 8 blocks from the origin. The player spawns on the Hearth plinth at HEARTH_Y=51, so the room sits ~35 blocks straight down, reachable by mining down at spawn or by caving (a core voxel verb, and the single most common thing a player does at spawn).

What they find is not a proper dungeon but a half-eaten one: stampHomeAnchor and stampHub (which run after stampStructures and only convert air/water to stone) fill in the quadrant of the room that overlaps the Hearth footprint and the hub-building pads, leaving a partially-carved room with an intact altar, marble ring and wood pillars sitting in a large open cavity. So the player-visible defect is (a) a "rare" 2.5% structure that is in fact guaranteed at the one chunk 100% of players occupy, and (b) that structure is malformed.

No crash, no save corruption, no progression or loot impact — dungeons carry no mobs, loot or quests anywhere in the codebase. This is a world-gen determinism accident plus a cosmetic artifact. The danger is forward-looking, exactly as the claim states: it is load-bearing on the Hearth/hub footprints happening to overlap the room, so any future change to the Hearth radius or hub layout will expose more of the broken room. Fix is cheap — swap the sin hash for the Math.imul hash already used at landmarks.js:10 / oreGen.js:23 (which also fixes the periodicity and large-coordinate precision loss).

FILE:LINE REAL: Atmosphere.jsx:26-28 (FOG_SEA_LEVEL=56.0/FOG_HEIGHT_FALLOFF=34.0/FOG_RESIDUAL=0.55), :208 <ambientLight>, :224 <hemisphereLight> — verbatim at HEAD. NOT ALREADY FIXED: git log on Atmosphere.jsx/mood.js shows newest = a46d545 (dispose leaks); unrelated to 926751e/15fcc96.

REPRODUCED MYSELF (own probe, not the claim's): I replayed terrain.worker.js's own carve rule (:454-459) + heightAt.js/oreGen.js in node to locate a VERIFIED enclosed cavern at world (-4,20,-1), then drove the live app via the enterCapture camera override (applied per-frame at Components.jsx:522), midday/explore mood. Cave mean RGB (12.2, 37.2, 60.6), meanLum 33.6 vs above-ground control (107.2, 155.1, 186.8), meanLum 147.2. Point-blank plain stone underground = RGB (1.3, 24.8, 47.3) — red channel crushed to ~1/255, a featureless navy. Screenshots: A-real-cave.png, ore-stone.png.

CLAIM'S MECHANISM IS WRONG (height fog is NOT the cause), two ways: (1) heightMul = mix(1.0, 0.55, t) — 1.0 is the BASELINE; the height term only THINS fog ABOVE y=56, it never amplifies below it. (2) At explore fogDensity=0.0025 (mood.js MOOD_SCALARS), fogFactor*heightMul at cave-wall distances = 0.006% (3m), 0.016% (5m), 0.062% (10m), 0.25% (20m). Numerically irrelevant. REAL cause = mood.js ROLE.ambient='skyMid' -> ambientLight.color = PALETTE.explore.skyMid = #2E8AE0 (saturated sky-blue, R=46/255=0.18) + hemisphereLight sky=#2E8AE0. Sun occluded underground => that blue ambient is the only light. No torch/block-light system exists (every pointLight in src/ is spell/boss/beast/phantom-block/mascot/hearth-orb).

CLAIM'S EXECUTED EVIDENCE IS INVALID: its cited probe camera (-19,22,-37) is SOLID STONE, not a cave — caveNoise = 0.041 vs the y>=20 threshold 0.45 (terrain.worker.js:455-456). Their "probeB-cave-looking-up" was shot from inside a rock. The conclusion survives only because I found a real cave independently.
verdict.real_player_impact:
REAL BUT OVERSTATED. Players do reach and see this: caves are carved near spawn and are content-bearing — I counted 1738 coal, 1241 iron, and 347 gold ore faces exposed to cave air within |x|,|z|<=60 of origin, and ores are depth-banded for mining payoff (oreGen.js). So the entire underground genuinely renders as a dark blue murk lit only by a sky-blue ambient — a real visual-quality gap, and LOW severity is honest (it is a missing feature, not a defect; nothing breaks).

BUT the claim's sharpest impact line — "you cannot tell coal from stone from diamond by sight" — is REFUTED by my own point-blank captures: stone (1.3, 24.8, 47.3) = flat navy; coal (32.9, 40.8, 54.5) = navy + black flecks; iron (63.9, 66.1, 76.3) = navy + clearly TAN flecks. Pairwise dRGB 36-80, and ore-iron.png visibly reads tan against navy stone. The ORES remain legible; it is the plain STONE that is a featureless blue murk. So the "cannot tell coal from diamond" framing is inflated; the honest finding is "underground stone reads as flat navy because the only light source is a #2E8AE0 sky-blue ambient, and there is no cave/torch lighting system."

verdict.title: Day/night dial is 90° out of phase — draws the SUN at zenith while printing "DUSK", and below the horizon at spawn (HUD.jsx:81,:102 use -180 offset; should be -90)
verdict.reason:
Reproduced independently, not taken on faith.

(1) CITED LINES REAL + UNCHANGED ON HEAD. `git show HEAD:frontend/src/HUD.jsx | sed -n '81p;102p'` returns `rotate(${p.angleDeg - 180}deg)` at both. `git status --short` clean for HUD.jsx + dayPhase.js, so grep == HEAD. NOT already fixed: `git log -5 -- frontend/src/HUD.jsx frontend/src/game/dayPhase.js` top entry is 7b6e7b7 (health bar); the two stale-making commits (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) don't touch this; last 3 repo commits are docs-only.

(2) DOC-VS-CODE DRIFT REAL. dayPhase.js:29-30 documents `cycleFraction 0=midnight, 0.25=dawn, 0.5=noon, 0.75=dusk`. Live clock disagrees: useGameStore.jsx:633/675 init `isDay:true, gameTime:0`; useDayNightClock ticks `t+GAME_UNITS_PER_SECOND` (=4/s); dayNight.js:48 `isDayAtUnit` = floor(t/600)%2===0. So t=0 DAWN, 300 NOON, 600 DUSK, 900 MIDNIGHT — a quarter-cycle off the docstring. `-180` is exactly correct FOR THE DOCSTRING and exactly 90° wrong for the real clock.

(3) MY OWN PROBE (node, importing the REAL src/game/dayPhase.js + dayNight.js, simulating the actual ticker from t=0 with the real crossedHalfCycle flip) reproduced the claimed table:
  t=0   day  SUN  rot -180 -> BOTTOM   label (none)
  t=300 day  SUN  rot  -90 -> LEFT     label (none)
  t=500 day  SUN  rot  -30 -> TOP      label DUSK
  t=596 day  SUN  rot -1.2 -> TOP      label DUSK   <-- last day tick
  t=600 nite MOON rot    0 -> TOP      label NIGHT
Correction to the claim's evidence: gameTime 599 is UNREACHABLE (clock steps by 4); real last day tick is 596, rot -1.2°. Same position, conclusion unaffected.

(4) GEOMETRY OBSERVED, NOT ASSUMED — the load-bearing step. Rendered the exact HUD markup (44px ring, orbit `inset-0`, marker `left-1/2 top-0.5 -translate-x-1/2`, horizon line at `top-1/2`) in real Chromium via Playwright and measured marker-center vs ring-center: rot -180 -> dx=0.0 dy=+13.0 = BOTTOM, and BELOW the widget's own horizon line (sun literally underground at spawn). rot -1.2 -> dy=-13.0 = TOP/zenith while the label reads DUSK. rot 0 -> TOP. Confirms both headline absurdities.

(5) FIX VERIFIED: rot = angleDeg - 90 lands dawn->LEFT, noon->TOP, dusk->RIGHT, midnight->BOTTOM, matching the widget's own stated intent (HUD.jsx:65-66 "noon at top, sunrise left, sunset right, midnight bottom").

(6) NO TEST GUARDS IT: dayPhase.test.js only asserts arithmetic (`angleDeg` closeTo 90 for cf=0.25 — true regardless of semantics); nothing tests the semantic mapping or the HUD's -180 offset. Zero test files reference DayPhaseDial.

SEVERITY TRIMMED HIGH -> MEDIUM (only correction to the claim): the widget is not uniformly lying. The sun/moon ICON is isDay-driven and correct, the "DUSK" LABEL is correct (claim concedes this), and a separate DuskWarning toast fires. The dramatized "commits to a mining trip, siege lands seconds later" requires ignoring two correct cues on the same 44px widget. Real, always-on, immediately visible, one-character fix — but informational, not save-corrupting.

NOTE FOR THE FIXER: useGameStore.jsx:689 `setTimeOfDay` encodes the DOCSTRING convention (`isDay = frac >= 0.25 && frac < 0.75`), directly contradicting isDayAtUnit. It's dev-test-bridge/capture-only (dial returns null in capture mode) so it doesn't rescue the live path, but two coexisting conventions are what let this drift in; the fix should reconcile them.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — every player, every session, continuously. DayPhaseDial mounts at HUD.jsx:545 gated only on `isPointerLocked && gameSystems.isAlive && isWorldBuilt` (the normal playing state); it is suppressed only in capture mode, which is a dev/test path. So this is not theoretical or dead code.

What the player actually sees: at spawn (gameTime 0, broad daylight, sun icon) the sun marker is rendered at the BOTTOM of the ring, below the horizon line the widget itself draws — a sun underground in daylight, visible in the first frame of every new game. Throughout the day the marker runs a quarter-cycle ahead of reality, and in the final ~18% of the day the dial simultaneously prints "DUSK" in warn-orange while parking the sun at the top of the ring (high noon) — a self-contradiction inside one 44px widget, at the exact moment the widget matters most.

Practical severity is bounded by redundancy: the sun/moon icon and the "DUSK" text are both correct, and a DuskWarning toast fires independently, so a player is unlikely to actually die from trusting the marker. The real cost is that the ambient clock whose entire job is "how much daylight is left" is wrong at every instant and visibly incoherent with itself — a credibility defect on a shipped HUD element with a one-character fix (-180 -> -90).

verdict.title: The day-phase dial's live probe is a FALSE PASS — it drives the clock through a DEV-only convention the real game never uses
verdict.reason:
Every technical assertion REPRODUCED — I wrote my own probe (scratchpad/kz-dayphase-refute.mjs) importing the REAL frontend/src/game/dayNight.js + dayPhase.js, and it matched the claimed output byte-for-byte. (Integrity note: my first run silently executed a STALE scratchpad file because zsh noclobber blocked the heredoc write; I caught it, rm -f'd, re-ran from a fresh path, and sha-printed the file. Output below is from the verified-fresh run.)

CITED LINES ARE REAL AND SAY WHAT IS CLAIMED:
- useGameStore.jsx:691-694 (claim said 689-694; off by 2, immaterial): `const isDay = frac >= 0.25 && frac < 0.75; return { gameTime: Math.round(frac * 1200), isDay };`
- dayNight.js:48: `isDayAtUnit(t) => Math.floor(t / HALF_CYCLE_UNITS) % 2 === 0` -> day spans [0,600).
- scripts/visual/dayphase-probe.mjs:69 drives via `window.useGameStore.getState().setTimeOfDay(f)`.
- HUD.jsx:81 (the actual dial, NOT DuskWarning): `rotate(${p.angleDeg - 180}deg)` on a marker anchored top.

MY PROBE OUTPUT:
 PATH A (setTimeOfDay, what the probe does): 0.00->gt=0 isDay=false MOON at BOTTOM=midnight; 0.25->gt=300 isDay=true SUN at LEFT=sunrise; 0.50->gt=600 isDay=true SUN at TOP=noon; 0.75->gt=900 isDay=false MOON at RIGHT=sunset. All four LOOK CORRECT.
 PATH B (real game): gt=0 truth=sunrise -> SUN at BOTTOM=midnight-slot; gt=300 truth=noon -> SUN at LEFT; gt=600 truth=sunset -> MOON at TOP; gt=900 truth=midnight -> MOON at RIGHT. All four 90deg OFF.
 Self-contradiction confirmed: setTimeOfDay(0.5) -> gameTime=600, isDay=true, but isDayAtUnit(600)=false.
 Fidelity check: store initial state is `gameTime: 0` (line 675) + `isDay: true` (line 633), matching isDayAtUnit(0)=true, so PATH B is faithful. Simulating the real crossedHalfCycle ticker at 4 units/s over 2 full cycles gave 0 mismatches vs isDayAtUnit — the real ticker IS the isDayAtUnit convention.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: git log -12 on HUD.jsx/dayPhase.js/useGameStore.jsx shows no touch; `git show HEAD:frontend/src/HUD.jsx | sed -n 81p` still emits `angleDeg - 180`, and HEAD's setTimeOfDay is unchanged. Unrelated to today's 926751e/15fcc96.

WHY IT STILL DOES NOT SURVIVE — the player-impact bar: I grepped ALL setTimeOfDay references across src/ + scripts/ + tests/. There is NO production caller. Every call site is (a) inside the App.jsx useEffect guarded by `if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return;` (line 266, wrapping registerTestHook at 287 and every showcase hook through 577), (b) src/devtest/PerfProbeRunner.jsx:52, or (c) scripts/visual/*.mjs. The defect AS SCOPED is "a dev-only Puppeteer script manufactures false confidence" — players never execute scripts/visual/. The claim concedes this itself: "No direct player impact (setTimeOfDay is DEV-only)."
verdict.real_player_impact:
NONE for this finding as scoped. It is a critique of a DEV-only validation artifact (scripts/visual/dayphase-probe.mjs), not of a code path any player executes. setTimeOfDay has zero production callers — the test bridge that exposes it is statically dead in prod (`import.meta.env.DEV`). The claim's own player_impact field says "No direct player impact." Its "secondary latent risk" is explicitly conditional on a sleep/skip-night feature that does not exist in the codebase.

IMPORTANT CARRY-FORWARD FOR THE PARENT: the UNDERLYING dial bug that this claim merely *explains* IS real, player-facing, and unfixed on HEAD — at gameTime=0 (start of day, every fresh game) the HUD dial renders the SUN at the BOTTOM of the ring, below its own horizon line, and stays 90deg out of phase all cycle (HUD.jsx:81 `angleDeg - 180`, fed by dayPhase.js:32 whose docstring asserts a midnight-at-0 convention that contradicts dayNight.js:48). That belongs to the separate 90deg-off-dial finding. Scoring THIS claim as surviving would double-count that one defect, and the artifact this claim actually indicts (a dev script) is unreachable by players. Severity "MEDIUM" is therefore inflated for the stated scope — as a process/tooling observation it is accurate and genuinely useful (a LIVE probe is not automatically truth), but it is not a player-facing bug.

verdict.real_player_impact:

One factual overstatement in the claim: it calls CombatLog a "strict visual duplicate" of NotificationStack. It is a CONTENT duplicate but not a visual one — the toasts are top-right panelled `Toast` components with framer-motion spring animations, while CombatLog is a quiet unpanelled bottom-left 11px text feed. Same information, different presentation and position. That nuance does not change the substance: the log has no memory, which is the claim's core and it is true.

verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: useSpellUpgrades() is called at App.jsx:181 inside GameApp, which mounts at page boot — BEFORE any world can be loaded (grep confirms there is no boot-time loadWorldData; the ONLY caller is WorldManager, a CHILD of GameApp, via MenuSystem:170). The 'restore-fix' test that claims to lock this regression (tests/store/spellUpgradeRestore.test.js) renderHook()s AFTER seeding the store — an ordering production never produces — so it is green on an unreachable code path.   B store.spellLevels: {"fireball":1,"iceball":2,"lightning":1,"arcane":1}   <-- fireball/lightning were 3
  B NEXT AUTOSAVE persists: {"fireball":1,"iceball":2,"lightning":1,"arcane":1}
CONTROL (fresh mount, i.e. the unreachable order the existing test uses):
  C fresh-mount hook fireball dmg = 120  <-- correct, and never happens in the real app

verdict.title: Spell Mastery is DEAD after loading a save: every spell casts at Level 1 while the panel says MAX RANK — and the first Upgrade click wipes your levels to disk
verdict.reason:
I wrote my OWN probe (tests/store/zzprobe-spellmastery.test.js, since deleted) replicating the real production mount order — renderHook(useSpellUpgrades) with store.spellLevels={} (the boot default at useGameStore.jsx:449), THEN act(() => loadWorldData(save)) with saved levels {fireball:3,iceball:2,lightning:3,arcane:2}. Assertions were written as the CORRECT behavior, so they FAIL iff the bug is real. Output: "A after load: store.spellLevels = {fireball:3,...}" but "store.getSpellStats('fireball').damage = 50" and the real cast seam resolveCastBaseDamage(store.getSpellStats,...) = 50 → expected 120, got 50 (FAIL). Then one upgradeSpell('iceball') → store.spellLevels = {fireball:1,iceball:2,lightning:1,arcane:1} → expected 3, got 1 (FAIL); buildSaveData() of that state persists the wiped map. Control (seed store THEN mount, the order the existing test uses) = 120 PASS.

MECHANISM VERIFIED IN SOURCE (not inferred): spellUpgrades.js:57-65 is a one-shot hydratedRef effect with [] deps that only adopts a NON-EMPTY store map; :104-108 pushes hook-local state into the store. App.jsx:181 calls useSpellUpgrades() inside GameApp, which App()→GameAppWrapper()→GameApp renders UNCONDITIONALLY at page boot. REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (a) grep for a remount key= in App.jsx → none; (b) grep for zustand persist(/createJSONStorage/location.reload or any boot-time auto-load → none, so store.spellLevels is ALWAYS {} at hook mount and the hydration branch NEVER fires; (c) grep for a re-seed tick like useQuestSystem's questLoadedAt (QuestSystem.jsx:143) → spellUpgrades has NO equivalent; (d) the only loadWorldData caller is WorldManager.jsx:119-120 via MenuSystem.jsx:170, a CHILD of GameApp, so load ALWAYS happens after mount.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: git log -1 on the file = 14227cac (Jun 17, "SOTA #51 S3: restore-fix") — that commit IS the broken one-shot hydration. git status --short on spellUpgrades.js / App.jsx / useGameStore.jsx is empty (working tree == HEAD). Today's fixes (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) do not touch this. The existing tests/store/spellUpgradeRestore.test.js is 5/5 GREEN while the bug is live because it seeds the store BEFORE renderHook — the inverse of production order. Panel reads store.spellLevels (SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:28, shows L3) while the cast reads store.getSpellStats (EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:201, stale all-1s closure) — the exact divergence claimed.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and unavoidable for any returning player. The ONLY way to resume a save is World Manager → Load (WorldManager.jsx:110-125), and that path always runs after GameApp has already mounted the hook with an empty store — so the restore is dead 100% of the time, not in an edge case. Impact 1 (needs only a load): every spell casts at Level 1 for the entire session — Fireball III deals 50 instead of 120 (-58%), Lightning III 75 instead of 160 (-53%) — while the panel renders "LEVEL 3/3 / MAX RANK". Spell Mastery, an advertised progression pillar, has never worked across a load. Impact 2 (needs one additional Upgrade click on any spell after loading — normal play, not contrived): the push effect clobbers store.spellLevels back to hook-local all-1s plus the one bump, and the next autosave writes that through buildSaveData → permanent, unrecoverable loss of earned spell levels on disk. Severity CRITICAL is honest: silent damage nerf + lying UI + persisted progression data loss.

verdicts_joined.title: refundUnknownTalents validates the talent ID but never the RANK — an over-limit rank loads unchanged (armor 300 vs legal 18; maxHealth 750 vs legal 195 at level 1)
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/talentTree.js:80-88 (refundUnknownTalents); src/store/useGameStore.jsx:872 (the only load-time talent sanitizer)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: spendTalentPoint (useGameStore.jsx:474-478) rigorously enforces TALENT_LIMITS on the way IN, so the rank<=limit invariant is real and intentional. But the load path's only sanitizer, refundUnknownTalents, checks `if (NODE_BY_ID[id])` — the KEY — and then copies the VALUE through verbatim. This is the classic validate-the-key-trust-the-value hole, and it sits in the exact function whose stated job is forward-compat migration. Any future balance patch that REDUCES a node's limit (e.g. voidhand_ward 3->2) leaves every existing save's rank-3 in place, silently over-cap, forever. Negative ranks also pass through (they fold to 0, so they're a dead point-sink rather than a stat gain).
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Today: a trivial localStorage edit yields armor 300 (75% damage reduction vs the intended 15%) and 750 HP at level 1 — self-inflicted only, since Crafty is single-player local-first. The real bite is forward: the first time you rebalance a talent's limit downward, every existing save keeps its over-cap ranks and those players stay permanently stronger than the new cap allows, with no refund and no way to notice.
verdicts_joined.domain: Progression (XP, levels, attributes, talents, spell mastery)

verdict.title: refundUnknownTalents validates the talent ID but never the RANK — over-limit ranks load unchanged (armor 300 vs legal 18; maxHealth 750 vs legal 195)
verdict.reason:
MECHANISM FULLY REPRODUCED (claim did not fabricate). HEAD=1386b5e; talentTree.js:80-88 is real and verbatim as cited: `if (NODE_BY_ID[id]) kept[id] = unlockedTalents[id]` — key-checked, value copied through. My own vitest probes: refundUnknownTalents({voidhand_ward:50}) -> {voidhand_ward:50}, folded armor=300 (legal max = limit 3 x 6 = 18); through the REAL store.loadWorldData with {voidhand_ward:50, wildheart_vigor:40} -> unlockedTalents kept verbatim, maxHealth=750 (legal 195 at L1). Negative ranks pass through too. Not already fixed — no clamp anywhere in the load path. Corroborating detail the claim missed: useGameStore.jsx:878-881 DOES clamp ferocityBanked/kineticBanked/soulBanked/resonanceBanked on load, so the missing rank clamp is a genuine inconsistency, not a deliberate choice.

BUT THE PLAYER-IMPACT GATE FAILS: (1) No untrusted input surface — src/game/worldSaves.js is a "thin localStorage layer" (JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem)); grep of WorldManager.jsx for FileReader / file input / fetch / upload / import returns NOTHING. No cloud sync, no multiplayer, no leaderboard, no server authority. A save can only originate from the player's own browser. (2) No in-game path can produce an over-cap rank — grep of every writer of `unlockedTalents` shows the ONLY writer is spendTalentPoint (useGameStore.jsx:478, guarded by `currentVal >= limit`); every other reference is a read. Respec is not built (task #10 still pending). (3) The claim's strongest argument — "the first time you rebalance a limit downward" — has NEVER fired: `git log --follow -- frontend/src/game/talentTree.js` shows all 5 commits (233be57d, 68a65b06, ac801cbe, 40a7cfbd, 478cd69d) are purely ADDITIVE (new nodes); no limit has ever been reduced. That harm is contingent on a hypothetical future patch.
verdict.real_player_impact: None today. The only way to reach the 300-armor / 750-HP state is for the player to open devtools and hand-edit their own localStorage in a single-player, local-first game with no import surface, no network sync, and no shared/competitive state. That is a player choosing an outcome, not a bug happening to them — there is no victim and no attacker path. Severity MEDIUM is inflated; this is LOW-priority hardening debt, not a player-facing defect. It IS still worth a cheap ~3-line fix (clamp rank to [0, TALENT_LIMITS[id]] in refundUnknownTalents and refund the excess into talentPoints), because it would (a) match the clamping discipline already applied four lines above at useGameStore.jsx:878-881 and (b) pre-pay for the day a talent limit actually IS reduced — at which point existing saves would silently keep over-cap ranks forever. But that day has not come, so nothing ships broken to a player today.

verdicts_joined.title: Spell Mastery rank pips are INVISIBLE for Fireball/Iceball/Lightning — Tailwind never compiles the dynamically-built bg-spell-* classes
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/ui/SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:208 (`l < lvl ? `bg-spell-${elem}` : 'bg-track'`); tailwind.config.cjs:14-20 (safelist has only text-spell-*, no bg-spell-*)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: Tailwind's JIT scans source text for COMPLETE class strings. `bg-spell-${elem}` is assembled at runtime, so `bg-spell-fire`, `bg-spell-ice` and `bg-spell-lightning` never appear as literals anywhere in src/ and are absent from the safelist (which lists only the text-spell-* variants). Those classes are therefore never emitted, and the 'filled' rank pip renders with no background — visually identical to an empty `bg-track` pip. `bg-spell-arcane` survives ONLY by accident: it happens to appear as a literal in talentTree.js:44 as the Elemancer tree's dot color. The talent-tree pips are all fine for the same reason (bg-stat-atk/spd/def are literals). I found this by LOOKING at tests/visual/baseline/progression-open.png — the Arcane row's first pip is visibly lighter than Fireball/Iceball/Lightning's — then confirmed it deterministically by compiling the real CSS. The visual gate has this exact frame pinned as a baseline and rubber-stamps the broken state; spell-mastery-ui-gates.test.js only regexes the source and never renders.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Compiled the REAL stylesheet: `npx tailwindcss -c tailwind.config.cjs -i src/index.css -o out.css --minify` (Done in 916ms), then grepped the output:
  PRESENT  .text-spell-fire
  PRESENT  .text-spell-ice
  PRESENT  .text-spell-lightning
  PRESENT  .text-spell-arcane
  MISSING  .bg-spell-fire        <-- renders as NO background
  MISSING  .bg-spell-ice         <-- renders as NO background
  MISSING  .bg-spell-lightning   <-- renders as NO background
  PRESENT  .bg-spell-arcane      <-- only because talentTree.js:44 has it as a literal
Control (talent-tree dots, all literals): PRESENT .bg-stat-atk / .bg-stat-spd / .bg-stat-def / .bg-track
Corroborated visually in tests/visual/baseline/progression-open.png: Arcane's leading pip is tinted; Fireball/Iceball/Lightning's are not.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: In the Progression panel, 3 of the 4 spells show three identical grey dots no matter what rank you are — the at-a-glance rank indicator is dead. Arcane's works. The player sees an inconsistent, broken-looking UI and has to read the small 'LEVEL n/3' text to know their rank.
verdicts_joined.domain: Progression (XP, levels, attributes, talents, spell mastery)

verdict.title: Spell Mastery rank pips are invisible for Fireball/Iceball/Lightning — Tailwind never compiles the runtime-built bg-spell-* classes
verdict.reason: Reproduced independently on three channels, none taken on faith. (1) Fresh compile I ran myself: `npx tailwindcss -c tailwind.config.cjs -i src/index.css -o out2.css` (Done in 515ms) → MISSING .bg-spell-fire / .bg-spell-ice / .bg-spell-lightning; PRESENT .bg-spell-arcane; controls PRESENT .bg-track, .bg-stat-atk. (2) The COMMITTED production bundle /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/build/assets/index-DrgU5i8f.css shows the identical set — so this actually shipped, not an artifact of my invocation. (3) Root cause verified by grep, not assumed: `grep -rn "bg-spell" src/` returns exactly 2 hits — the runtime interpolation at /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/ui/SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:208 (`${l < lvl ? `bg-spell-${elem}` : 'bg-track'}`) and /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/talentTree.js:44 (`dot: 'bg-spell-arcane'`), the sole literal that makes arcane survive. No manual .bg-spell-* rule exists in any CSS file (no fallback). SPELL_MASTERY (SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:12-17) confirms elem ∈ {fire,ice,lightning,arcane}. tailwind.config.cjs safelist contains ONLY the five text-spell-* entries — no bg-spell-*. Cited file:line is real and says exactly what the claim says. NOT already fixed: HEAD = 1386b5e (docs-only commit); line 208 and the safelist are both unchanged. Panel is player-reachable: imported/mounted at /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/MenuSystem.jsx:16,81 (Progression menu). Gate blindness confirmed: tests/gates/spell-mastery-ui-gates.test.js is readFileSync + toMatch regex over source text (never renders), so it structurally cannot see a missing compiled class; the visual gate has the broken frame pinned as its own baseline. One wording nit in the claim: the filled pip is transparent-over-bg-slot, not literally bg-track colored — subtly different, both read untinted; defect unaffected.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and universal, and slightly worse than claimed. In tests/visual/baseline/progression-open.png all four spells read LEVEL 1/3, so `l < lvl` is true for l=0 and the first pip should be tinted on ALL FOUR — yet only Arcane's leading pip is visibly lighter. This is therefore not a high-rank edge case: EVERY player hits it at the default rank the first time they open the Progression panel. Fireball, Iceball and Lightning show three identical untinted dots at every rank (1/3, 2/3, 3/3), so the at-a-glance rank indicator is permanently dead for 3 of 4 spells while Arcane's works — an inconsistent, broken-looking UI that forces the player to read the small "LEVEL n/3" text. Severity MEDIUM is honest, not inflated: cosmetic only (no state corruption, no gameplay effect) and the adjacent LEVEL n/3 text carries the same info redundantly, so it is not HIGH; but it is a permanently-dead indicator in a core panel seen by every player, with one spell inconsistently working, so it is more than LOW. Fix is one line: add bg-spell-fire/ice/lightning/arcane/nature to the existing safelist, whose own comment already documents this exact JIT-interpolation hazard for the text-spell-* case (the author fixed half the problem and missed the bg- half).

verdicts_joined.title: A spell upgrade never schedules an autosave, and the tab-close flush is a no-op — upgrade then quit and the upgrade is gone
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/App.jsx:233-248 (autosave transition-key predicate omits spellLevels AND attributes); src/game/autosave.js:8 (`flush() { if (timer !== null) ... }`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The autosave subscriber only calls schedule() when one of level/equipment/chests/talentPoints/gameMode/worldBlocks/inventory/questState/the-4-banks changes by identity. `spellLevels` is not in that list — and neither is `attributes` (so allocateAttribute is in the same boat; talentPoints IS listed, so spendTalentPoint is safe). createAutosave.flush() then only writes if a save is already PENDING, so beforeunload/visibilitychange rescues nothing. Net: upgrading a spell mutates state that nothing watches and nothing flushes.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Drove the REAL upgradeSpell through the REAL App.jsx predicate (copied verbatim) and the REAL createAutosave:
  F spellLevels after upgrade   : {"fireball":2,"iceball":1,"lightning":1,"arcane":1}
  F autosave predicate tripped? : false   <-- NO SAVE IS EVER SCHEDULED
  G flush() with no pending save -> save() called 0 times
  G schedule() then flush()      -> save() called 1 times   (control: the mechanism works when armed)
  H full player story — upgrade Fireball I->II->III, then close the tab:
  H hook says fireball dmg = 120 (L3)
  H saves written to disk  = 0   <-- the upgrade NEVER hit disk
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Open the pause menu, spend your level-gated Fireball upgrades, close the tab -> reopen and you are back at Fireball I. Recoverable (upgrades are free, level-gated, so you just re-click), but it reads as the game eating your progress. In practice an active player usually trips inventory/worldBlocks within 5s and gets saved by luck — which is exactly why this is intermittent and never reproduced.
verdicts_joined.domain: Progression (XP, levels, attributes, talents, spell mastery)

verdict.title: Spell upgrades (and attribute points) never schedule an autosave, and the tab-close flush is a no-op — upgrade then quit and it's gone
verdict.reason:
Reproduced independently rather than trusting the claim's copied predicate. Probe (vitest+jsdom, since deleted) parsed the watched-key list DIRECTLY from App.jsx source at runtime and drove the REAL useSpellUpgrades hook against the REAL useGameStore.

- Keys extracted from App.jsx:233-248 source: [level, equipment, chests, talentPoints, gameMode, worldBlocks, inventory, questState, ferocityBanked, kineticBanked, soulBanked, resonanceBanked]. Contains spellLevels? FALSE. Contains attributes? FALSE.
- Real upgradeSpell('fireball'): spellLevels {fireball:1}->{fireball:2}; watched keys that changed identity = [] -> predicate cannot fire.
- Real createAutosave.flush() with nothing pending -> save() called 0 times (autosave.js:8 = `flush() { if (timer !== null) { clear(); save(); } }`).
- End-to-end: upgrade -> beforeunload flush -> 0 saves written.
- CONTROL (absent from the original claim, added to rule out a vacuous harness): mutate a WATCHED key (worldBlocks) then flush -> 1 save. So "0 saves" is a real negative, not a broken rig.
- Secondary: allocateAttribute('strength') 10->11, watched keys changed = [] — same defect, second instance.

NOT already fixed: cited lines exact at HEAD 1386b5e, `git status` clean for both files. questState IS in the list, i.e. the R1 quest fix edited this very predicate and still omitted spellLevels.

Not dead code / round-trip was intended: saveSchema.js:35 serializes spellLevels, useGameStore.jsx:873+931 restores it, spellUpgrades.js:53-64 hydrates it on mount. Only the TRIGGER was never wired. UI is live (MenuSystem.jsx:81, keybind InputManager.jsx:233). saveActiveWorld has exactly ONE caller app-wide (App.jsx:227, inside the autosave) -> no rescue path.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes. Open the pause menu, spend level-gated Fireball/Iceball/etc. upgrades (and/or allocate attribute points), close the tab -> reopen and you're back at Fireball I with the points unspent. Recoverable, not corrupting: upgrades are free and level-gated, so the player just re-clicks them — but it reads as the game eating progress.

Genuinely intermittent, which is why it survived: the autosave's save() closure reads getState() fresh, so ANY later watched-key change (mine a block -> worldBlocks, pick up an item -> inventory) sweeps the pending spellLevels to disk as a side effect. The bug only bites when the upgrade is the last progression action before quitting — i.e. the very common "open menu at end of session, spend upgrades, quit" flow.

Severity MEDIUM is honest, not inflated: real lost progress, self-healing, no corruption.

Fix: add `s.spellLevels !== prevS.spellLevels || s.attributes !== prevS.attributes` to the App.jsx:233-248 predicate (covers both instances). Do NOT "fix" it by making flush() unconditional — that would write on every tab-hide regardless of dirty state.

verdicts_joined.title: Store-level spendTalentPoint enforces the rank limit but NOT the prereq — the tree's dependency graph is a UI-only convention
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/store/useGameStore.jsx:474-496 (checks talentPoints > 0 and TALENT_LIMITS, never node.prereq)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: ASPECT_TREES encodes a real prereq DAG (voidhand_crush needs voidhand_force; soulbind_pack needs soulbind_snare; wildheart_endurance needs wildheart_roar). SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:101 is the ONLY thing that enforces it. The store — which is the save-authority and the thing every gameplay site reads — will happily grant an orphan node. The existing store test even bakes the hole in: tests/store/progressionXp.test.js spends voidhand_crush 9x with no voidhand_force and asserts it reaches rank 2.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
P4 (talentPoints: 10, unlockedTalents: {}), calling the real store action directly:
  spendTalentPoint('wildheart_endurance')  // prereq wildheart_roar NOT owned
  spendTalentPoint('soulbind_pack')        // prereq soulbind_snare NOT owned
  spendTalentPoint('voidhand_crush')       // prereq voidhand_force NOT owned
  P4 unlockedTalents: {"wildheart_endurance":1,"soulbind_pack":1,"voidhand_crush":1}  tp 7
All three orphan nodes granted; 3 points consumed.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: NONE via normal play today — the panel is the only caller and it gates correctly (verified behaviorally by tests/integration/spell-upgrade-talents.test.jsx). This is a latent authority gap: the moment a second caller appears (a respec button, a quest reward, a touch verb-wheel, the test bridge), the tree's design collapses. Worth closing because the fix is three lines in the place the invariant actually belongs.

verdict.title: Store-level spendTalentPoint enforces the rank limit but NOT the prereq — the tree's dependency graph is a UI-only convention
verdict.reason: Mechanism REPRODUCED independently (own probe, not the claim's). Wrote tests/store/zz-refute-prereq.test.js seeding talentPoints:10 / unlockedTalents:{} and calling the real store action for three orphan nodes; vitest output: unlockedTalents: {"wildheart_endurance":1,"soulbind_pack":1,"voidhand_crush":1}, talentPoints: 7. verdicts_joined.title: allocateAttribute has no attribute whitelist — a bad key writes NaN into attributes, burns the point, and serializes to the save as null
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/store/useGameStore.jsx:256-276 (`[attr]: state.attributes[attr] + 1` with no key check)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: `state.attributes['luck'] + 1` is `undefined + 1` = NaN. The point is still decremented, and the NaN key lands in the persisted `attributes` object (saveSchema.js serializes state.attributes wholesale), where JSON.stringify turns it into `null`. Sibling API addAttributePoints (:278) sanitizes properly (`Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(amount) || 0))`) — allocateAttribute simply doesn't.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
P3 (attributePoints: 3):
  after allocate("armor"):          {"strength":10,...,"armor":1,"attributePoints":2}   (works; armor has no UI '+' button, so this path is unreachable today)
  after allocate("luck"):           {"strength":10,...,"attributePoints":1,"luck":null}  <-- NaN written, point BURNED
  after allocate("attributePoints"): {...,"attributePoints":0}                            <-- net -1, self-cancelling
Also in the same class (same probe file):
  P5 addTalentPoint(undefined) -> talentPoints = NaN
  P5 addTalentPoint(-5)        -> talentPoints = -2      (no clamp; addTalentPoint has zero callers in src/ — dead API)
  P2 grantXP('75')             -> currentXP = "075"      (string concat; no caller passes a string today)
verdicts_joined.player_impact: NONE today — GamePanels.jsx:332-334 only ever passes 'strength'/'agility'/'intellect', and addTalentPoint/addAttributePoints have no callers at all. These are unexercised robustness holes in the store's public API, listed for completeness rather than as live defects. I am explicitly NOT claiming a player can hit them.
verdicts_joined.domain: Progression (XP, levels, attributes, talents, spell mastery)

verdict.title: allocateAttribute has no attribute whitelist — a bad key writes NaN, burns the point, serializes as null
verdict.reason: Every technical assertion reproduces; the finding fails only on reachability. (1) Cited code is real: useGameStore.jsx:256 `allocateAttribute: (attr) => set(...)` does `[attr]: state.attributes[attr] + 1` with no key check; sibling addAttributePoints:278 does sanitize via `Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(amount) || 0))` — the asymmetry is exactly as described. (2) I ran my own vitest probe against the real store (not trusting the claim's output): BEFORE {"strength":10,...,"attributePoints":3} -> after allocateAttribute('luck') -> {"strength":10,...,"attributePoints":2,"luck":null}, with `luck raw: NaN, isNaN: true`. NaN written, point burned, JSON.stringify -> null. Confirmed. (3) NOT already fixed: HEAD is 1386b5e (docs-only commits on top), code is live and unguarded. (4) NO PLAYER PATH: `grep -rn "allocateAttribute(" src/` filtered against the three literal forms returns ZERO dynamic call sites — the only callers are GamePanels.jsx:332-334, all hardcoded 'strength'/'agility'/'intellect'. addTalentPoint and addAttributePoints have zero callers in src/ (dead APIs). Note src/index.jsx:60 exposes `window.useGameStore` unconditionally, but that does not rescue the finding: console access already permits `setState({attributes: garbage})` directly, so the missing whitelist grants zero additional capability — a devtools cheat surface is not a player-experienced defect. Probe file removed after use.
verdict.real_player_impact: None. No player can reach it. The three UI '+' buttons are the only invocation path and they pass hardcoded literals; there is no dynamic key, no save-load path into allocateAttribute, and no in-game surface that supplies an arbitrary attr string. The sibling APIs it flags (addTalentPoint NaN/negative, grantXP string-concat) have no callers whatsoever in src/. Severity is HONEST, not inflated — the claim self-labels LOW and explicitly states "player_impact: NONE today ... I am explicitly NOT claiming a player can hit them." This is a truthful report of an unreachable robustness hole in the store's public API, not a live defect. A one-line guard (`if (!['strength','agility','intellect'].includes(attr)) return {}`) is cheap hardening if someone is already editing that file, but nothing ships broken today.

verdicts_joined.title: Every "Defeat N mobs" quest completes at HALF the advertised cost — each kill counts twice
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/QuestSystem.jsx:199 (the `quest.type === 'kill' && (type === 'kill' || type === 'kill_type')` match arm) + src/QuestSystem.jsx:317-318 (onMobKill fires updateQuestProgress('kill') AND updateQuestProgress('kill_type') for the same kill)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: onMobKill emits TWO progress events per kill. The third match arm makes a `type:'kill'` quest match BOTH of them, so it gains +2 per mob. This governs the entire kill spine (first_blood, hunter, champion) AND the whole endless bounty ladder — the late-game retention feed. The HUD number is visibly false: the tracker and the Achievements panel disagree on the same screen.

(6) UNGUARDED. tests/gates/kill-attribution-gates.test.js passes green — nothing in the suite catches this.

BONUS BUG in the same 4-line block (verified, not claimed): arm 1 (`quest.type === type`) also matches any `kill_type` quest regardless of mobType, making arm 2's mobType check dead. verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — a player experiences this on their very first mob kill, in the default fresh-save state.

first_blood and hunter are both `type:'kill'` and both sit in the fresh-save active set (QuestSystem.jsx:105 takes the first 3 tier-1 quests). champion and the entire endless bounty ladder (makeRepeatableQuest, line 67, `type:'kill'`, target 15+n*5) are also `type:'kill'`, so the whole late-game retention feed pays out at 2x rate. verdict.title: A corrupt/legacy save with a null in questState.quests white-screens the quest HUD — the guard that exists to prevent this does not check elements
verdict.reason:
The DEFECT reproduces — the claim is not fabricated. I re-ran it myself: rendering QuestTracker with quests=[null] (touchDevice mocked false to force the expanded desktop tracker) throws "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'icon')", while a valid-quest control in the same file renders (" QuestsHunterDefeat 5 mobs2/5"), so the map path is genuinely exercised. The cited file:line is real: QuestSystem.jsx:92 `const _arrOr = (v, fb) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v : fb);` with the lines 90-91 comment promising exactly what the claim quotes; crash site QuestSystem.jsx:464 is real. Not already fixed (HEAD 1386b5e is docs-only; nothing touches this).

It dies on REACHABILITY. I traced every ingress into questState.quests:
(1) NO IMPORT CHANNEL. grep for FileReader|importSave|upload|readAsText|input type=file returned zero hits. Saves are strictly self-written localStorage (src/game/worldSaves.js) — no untrusted/shared-save path exists.
(2) NO WRITER CAN EMIT A NULL. All three writers verified: initial seed (QUEST_LIST.filter().map()), updateQuestProgress (QuestSystem.jsx:193 — every branch returns quest or {...quest}), and reduceClaim (questClaim.js:59 `if (next) active.push(next)` — guarded). Probe with pickNext returning undefined gave quests=["b"], no holes. JSON round-trip of a normal quests array: 0 nulls (so the JSON.stringify undefined->null trap is unreachable too).
(3) REAL CORRUPTION DOESN'T PRODUCE A NULL ELEMENT. A truncated blob (quota/partial-write — the corruption that actually occurs) makes JSON.parse throw -> worldSaves.js:26 readWorld returns null -> load skipped. Verified.
(4) LEGACY SAVES ARE HANDLED. No questState key -> useGameStore.jsx:948 `saveData.questState ?? state.questState` -> re-seed effect `if (!qs) return;`. Verified. The claim's own "older-format save" vector is explicitly covered.

Two supporting premises of the claim are additionally FALSE: (a) "white-screen" — an ErrorBoundary at src/index.jsx:63 catches it and shows a styled "Something went wrong / Reload" panel; (b) "reduceClaim guards its elements; the RENDER does not" — the contrast is fabricated: questClaim.js:46 guards (`q &&`) but questClaim.js:55 `quests.filter((q) => q.id !== questId && !q.claimed)` does NOT, so a null would crash the claim path too. The render is not the odd one out.
verdict.real_player_impact: None. The only route to a null element is the player opening devtools and hand-writing one into their own localStorage — and index.jsx:60 already exposes window.useGameStore, so a self-tamperer has far easier ways to break their own game. There is no save import, no sharing, no server, no multiplayer, and no in-app writer that can emit null/undefined; the two realistic corruption modes (truncation, pre-questState legacy format) are both already handled and provably cannot yield a null element. Severity MEDIUM is inflated — this is a defense-in-depth hygiene gap, not a player-facing bug. It is still worth a cheap one-line hardening (`.filter(Boolean)` at the seed in QuestSystem.jsx:99-101, which would also protect the unguarded questClaim.js:55), but as a code-quality nit, not a bug fix.

verdict.title: The Q key and the tracker disagree on the claim predicate — a quest can become permanently unclaimable
verdict.reason:
Cited lines are REAL and NOT fixed on HEAD: InputManager.jsx:137 = `if (quest.progress >= quest.target && !quest.claimed)`; questClaim.js:46 (claim said 47, off-by-one) = `q.completed && !q.claimed`; QuestSystem.jsx:469 = `quest.completed && !quest.claimed`. R1 (926751e) rewrote claimQuest into reduceClaim but never touched InputManager's predicate, so the 3-way divergence stands.

HALF 1 REPRODUCED (I re-ran it, importing the real questClaim.js): seeding {progress:5,target:5,completed:false} printed "InputManager would claim it? true / Tracker shows Claim button? false / reduceClaim -> claimed: null / quest still in feed: ['hunter']". The claimant did not fabricate this.

HALF 2 REFUTES REACHABILITY. Exactly THREE writers of quest progress/completed exist repo-wide, and all three couple them atomically: QuestSystem.jsx:211 `return {...quest, progress: newProgress, completed: nowComplete}` with `nowComplete = newProgress >= quest.target` in the SAME object literal; and :109/110 + :265/266 which both spawn `progress:0, completed:false` where every real target is >=1 (bounties = 15+n*5). I fuzzed 42,500 progress transitions over all 34 real in-game targets with amounts 1/2/3/5/100: "states where (progress>=target && !completed): 0". The invariant progress>=target <=> completed holds absolutely.

The load path (useGameStore.jsx:949 `questState: saveData.questState ?? state.questState`) takes the quests array verbatim, so a hand-tampered localStorage save WOULD round-trip the divergence — but the game can never write one, and the "pre-questState" legacy fallback seeds fresh coupled quests, so there is no legacy vector either.

METHOD NOTE: my first heredoc silently failed on zsh noclobber and ran a PRE-EXISTING unrelated probe whose confident output was about anvil/wall-hit damage. I caught it and re-ran from a clean path — the numbers above are from the real probe.
verdict.real_player_impact: None. No gameplay path can produce progress>=target with completed=false (proven: 42,500 fuzzed transitions, zero violations), so no player ever encounters a Q-key no-op or a dead quest slot. The only route to the divergent state is a hand-edited/corrupt localStorage save — and a player who can tamper their save into this state could equally tamper it to grant the reward outright, so it is self-inflicted, not a bug they experience. The claim's own caveat concedes this ("player_impact: None in clean play"; "Reachability is therefore a HYPOTHESIS"). Severity LOW was honest, not inflated, but the finding does not clear the "a player is affected" bar. Residual value: aligning InputManager.jsx:137 to `quest.completed && !quest.claimed` is a cheap 1-line defensive-hygiene fix worth taking as latent-robustness — not as a bug fix.

verdict.title: Aimed spell hits the WRONG mob: checkMobCollision returns first-in-bucket, not nearest — and there is no friendly-fire guard
verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. All four checks pass.

(3) CITED CODE IS REAL. `frontend/src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx:160-168` at HEAD is verbatim `mobsQuery.entities.find(e => {...; return dist < range; })` — first match wins, no nearest-sort. Sole caller is `frontend/src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:331`: `checkMobCollision(projectile.position, projectile.size + 1.5)`. `game/spells.js` sizes (1.2/1.0/0.8/1.1) give exactly the claimed radii 2.7/2.5/2.3/2.6.

(1) I REPRODUCED IT WITH MY OWN PROBES (the claim's probe file no longer exists; I wrote 3 fresh ones — real EnhancedMagicSystem useFrame + real CombatSystem + real miniplex ECS — then deleted them).
- MECHANISM, isolated RED test: at projectile pos (0,140,-8.5) with zombie at 1.50u and villager at 2.06u, BOTH inside the 2.7 fireball radius, `checkMobCollision` returned "villager" — the FARTHER mob. `expect(hit.type).toBe('zombie')` FAILED. It demonstrably does not return the nearest.
- END-TO-END: camera (0,140,0) looking -Z, zombie dead-centre at (0,140,-10), villager 2u off-axis at (2,140,-9). All four spells hit the VILLAGER; zombie took ZERO. fireball dmg=60, iceball=48, lightning=90, arcane=72 (villager HP 120→60/72/30/48).
- NON-DETERMINISM: bucket order is NOT insertion order — I inserted ids 500,501,502,503 and mobsQuery returned 503,502,501,500 (corroborates the claim's "3,2,1"). The SAME geometry yielded villager-first in one mount and zombie-first in another, i.e. the victim flips run to run.

(2) NOT FIXED ON HEAD. `git log -3` = 1386b5e/45778e7/a8c7b71, all docs-only. `git show HEAD:frontend/src/systems/CombatSystem.jsx` still has the bare `find`. The only "coverage" is `tests/gates/spell-vfx-gates.test.js:111` — `expect(src).toMatch(/checkMobCollision/)`, a source-text regex that can never catch this.

(4) NOT THEORETICAL. There is NO friendly-fire guard anywhere: `damageMob` does `entity.health -= damage` for any mobsQuery entity, with no isNPC/isStatic/passive check. Both victim classes are in mobsQuery.

CLAIM CORRECTIONS (the claim is right but imprecise on two points, and under-states one):
- It conflates two entities. The 120-HP "villager" is the ambient wandering Settler (MOB_TYPES.villager, passive, spawn weight 0.6, mixes into packs) and has NO role/npcName. The hub quest NPCs (world/npcSpawn.js makeNpcEntity) have 200 HP, not 120 — so "two lightning casts" is really three at 90 dmg.
- Its specific numbers (162 direct hit, villager -42/120) did not reproduce in my harness; those depend on its attribute/spell-stat setup. Qualitative outcome identical.
- UNDER-STATED root cause: this is a PAIR of defects. The collision radius (2.3-2.7u) is 2-4x the mob body width (0.6-1.6u). That fat radius is what routinely puts 2+ mobs in range on the same frame (lightning steps 1.0u/frame), which is the precondition that lets the arbitrary tie-break bite. In some geometries the bystander is the ONLY mob in range and eats the shot purely from the fat radius. Fixing only the tie-break (pick nearest) narrows but does NOT eliminate bystander hits — a real fix needs both nearest-selection AND a sane hit radius (and arguably a friendly-fire guard).
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes, real and severe. You aim dead-centre at a monster and your spell kills the settler standing beside it — reproduced on all four spells, with the aimed target taking zero damage. In any pack you cannot focus-fire: which mob eats your shot is decided by ECS bucket order, which is not insertion order and flips between runs, so it is effectively arbitrary.

Worst case is unrecoverable: the 4 static hub quest NPCs (Bram the Trader / Mara the Smith / Old Pike the Warden / Sister Wren) are spawned isMob:true and sit in mobsQuery, so they are spell-targetable with no friendly-fire guard. I called checkMobCollision at the merchant's post and it returned "Bram the Trader"; 3 lightning-tier casts drove him to hp=-70/200 with dying=true. That permanently destroys the trade seam — same for the smith, healer, and guide. Casting a spell at a mob wandering into your settlement can silently delete the merchant/healer and brick those systems for the rest of the run.

Severity CRITICAL is defensible on the permanent-quest-NPC-loss axis (unrecoverable run state, no guard, no warning), though it is a gameplay/state bug rather than a crash. I would accept CRITICAL; HIGH would also be arguable. Not inflated.

Death is PERMANENT: SpawnerSystem.jsx:186 ecs.remove(entity) fires on dyingUntil BEFORE the isStatic guard at :191, whose comment reads "hub NPCs hold their post ... (no respawn path)".

verdict.real_player_impact:

Cast lightning at any hostile within ~8u of a neutral and the chain silently fans into it — the player cannot aim or avoid it, since solveChainTargets picks its own targets by nearest-distance. Cows/pigs/settlers spawn ambiently (villager weight 0.6 in MOB_TYPES), and night sieges drive hostiles into the settlement, so a husk standing among your cattle or settlers is routine, not contrived.

verdict.title: Fireball — the default starting spell — cannot hit anything past ~12.5m due to gravity applied only to fireball/iceball
verdict.reason:
I did NOT take the claimed probe on faith — the cited evidence file (magic3.probe.test.jsx) does not exist in the repo, so I wrote my own probe mounting the REAL EnhancedMagicSystem component with its real useFrame loop, real SPELL_TYPES, and the verbatim checkMobCollision predicate copied from CombatSystem.jsx:160 (dist < size+1.5). Geometry derived from source, not from the claim: terrain=140; CapsuleCollider args=[0.5,0.4] (Components.jsx:1311) -> half-extent 0.9; live camera follow targetY = translation.y + 1.2 (Components.jsx:1268) -> eye = ground+2.1; ground-kill at y <= getMobGroundLevel()+0.5 (EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:311).

MEASURED (max distance at which a mob's health actually dropped; swept 2u..60u @0.5u steps):
  LEVEL shot        — fireball 17u, iceball 14u, lightning 60u+, arcane 60u+
  CROSSHAIR ON MOB  — fireball 12.5u, iceball 11u, lightning 60u+, arcane 60u+
  fireball @40u aimed dead-on -> NO HIT.
(60u was my sweep ceiling; true ceilings = speed x maxAge 3000ms = 180u lightning, 90u arcane.)

Aiming CORRECTLY is worse than a level shot: the mob body-centre sits 1.1u below eye level, so putting the crosshair on it adds downward velocity — 17u -> 12.5u.

(3) file:line REAL and verbatim: EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:295-297 = `if (projectile.type === 'fireball' || projectile.type === 'iceball') { projectile.velocity.y -= 12 * delta; }`. Gravity is applied to NO other spell.

(2) NOT fixed on HEAD: file last touched by d114bf4 (2026-06-30); today's fixes were 926751e (quest-claim) and 15fcc96 (block-ids), unrelated.

Two errors IN THE CLAIM that I caught but that do not rescue it: (a) it cites Components.jsx:798 for camera height — that is the DEAD-player branch; live follow is :1268; (b) it says eye = ground+1.2, actual is ground+2.1. A higher muzzle should give MORE range, yet the bug survives anyway. The claim's "lightning farthest = 90u" is also self-inconsistent (it says the sweep ran 4u..40u — impossible to report 90 from that), and 90u is arcane's ceiling, not lightning's (180u). Its 12u/10u figures land near my AIMED numbers by accident via wrong geometry. Conclusion right; stated evidence not fully executed as described.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real, not theoretical. `activeSpell: 'fireball'` (useGameStore.jsx:554) is the DEFAULT starting spell, and castSpell is the live gameplay path (store-bound, input-driven) — not dead code. Every enemy engagement range sits outside fireball's ~12.5m reach: mobs aggro at AGGRO_RANGE=20 (ai.worker.js:126), archer mobs shoot the player from ARCHERY_RANGE=12 (:128) — exactly at the cliff edge — and the boss aggros at 30 (bossConfig.js:12). The player gets attacked from ranges where their starting spell silently vanishes into the dirt with zero feedback. Lightning strictly dominates fireball on BOTH axes (75 dmg / 180u vs 50 dmg / 12.5u) — no tradeoff exists.

SEVERITY HONESTY: the claim's HIGH is somewhat INFLATED; the honest grade is MEDIUM-HIGH. This is a balance/feel defect, not a crash, save-corruption, or progression blocker. The dominant combat loop masks it — mobs charge to MELEE_RANGE=2.5, so fireball works fine at the distances most fights actually resolve at, and the player can switch spells. But the mechanism, the default-spell exposure, and the silent-failure UX all hold, so it survives.

verdict.reason:
I tried hard to refute this and could not. I reproduced it with my OWN probe (the claim's cited probe file does not exist — see caveat below).

CITED CODE IS REAL (line-verified on HEAD):
- CombatSystem.jsx:160-161 `const checkMobCollision = (pos, range = 3) => { return mobsQuery.entities.find(e => {` — no health filter. Only caller: EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:330-331.
- CombatSystem.jsx:144 `entity.dyingUntil = performance.now() + DEATH_DISSOLVE_MS;`
- deathFx.js:7 `export const DEATH_DISSOLVE_MS = 320;`
- damageMob has NO health guard (CombatSystem.jsx:22-23: only `if (!entity) return null`).
- Contrast point verified: MinimapSyncSystem.jsx:14 DOES filter `health > 0`, and applyChainLightning reads that snapshot — so chain-lightning is corpse-free; the direct projectile is not.

MY OWN PROBE — /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/systems/__refute_corpse_eats_spells.test.jsx (mounts the REAL CombatSystem, replays the EnhancedMagicSystem:331-343 hit branch verbatim, real MOB_TYPES/SPELL_TYPES constants). Output:
  ### CORPSE: startHp=100 health=0 dyingUntil set=true | STILL in mobsQuery=true
  ### CORPSE render scale at dissolve end = 0 (invisible, but still collidable)
  ### FIREBALL hit mob id=1 at z=-5.42 after 13 frames (217ms flight)
  ### damageMob calls = [{"id":1,"dmg":50,"type":"fireball"}]
  ### corpse hp 0 -> -50 | LIVE mob behind hp 100 -> 100
  ### wasKill (drives 0.8 shake + 1.8x sparks) = true
  ### damage numbers spawned this shot = 3
The corpse ate the shot; the live zombie 6u behind took ZERO.

I FOUND THE THING THAT ALMOST REFUTED IT — AND IT MAKES THE BUG WORSE.
CAST_COOLDOWN (Components.jsx:144) = 333ms > DEATH_DISSOLVE_MS = 320ms. If the corpse were removed at `dyingUntil`, the next legal cast would always miss it by 13ms and the claim would collapse. But the removal sweep is NESTED INSIDE SpawnerSystem's 1000ms throttle — I dumped brace depth: SpawnerSystem.jsx:123 `if (now - lastSpawnCheck.current >= 1000) {` opens at depth 1→2, and the sweep at :183-195 (`if (entity.dyingUntil) { if (performance.now() >= entity.dyingUntil) ecs.remove(entity); }`) sits at depth 2, still inside it. It is the ONLY code path that removes a dying mob (grep of all `ecs.remove` sites; the App.jsx ones are world-clear/menu, LootSystem/XPOrbSystem are orbs). So actual ECS residency = 320ms (best) to 999ms (worst), measured by my second probe test. The claimant missed this; it is what makes the bug reachable at all.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: git log -3 = 1386b5e, 45778e7, a8c7b71 — all docs-only commits. The code above is what HEAD says right now.

CAVEAT ON THE CLAIM'S OWN EVIDENCE (the "agents fabricate" warning was warranted): the cited `magic.probe.test.jsx` does not exist anywhere in the repo, and its numbers are impossible against real constants — it reports dmg 60 (fireball is 50), corpse health -4000/-4060, live mob health 1000 (zombie maxHealth is 100). That "executed evidence" is fabricated or from a doctored fixture. The finding survives anyway because the underlying behavior is genuine and I reproduced it from scratch.

HOUSEKEEPING: I left the probe at the path above (matches the repo's tracked `__refute_*.test.jsx` convention; it passes as a characterization test). Separately — NOT mine, I launched no browser — there is a leaked headless Chromium (PID 29541) burning 711% CPU, load average 28.61. That is exactly the pathology CLAUDE.md warns about. I did not kill it in case a sibling subagent is mid-probe; the parent should run `sh frontend/scripts/dev/kill-test-procs.sh`.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real, and felt in the core combat loop. Killing the front mob of a pack and keeping the trigger down is THE most common way players fight. On the kill, an entity whose render scale has collapsed to 0 (dissolvePose(t>=1) => scale 0, clamped to 0.001 at MobModel.jsx:141) stays in mobsQuery as a fully valid, INVISIBLE spell hitbox with a generous 2.7u capture radius (fireball size 1.2 + 1.5).

The very next fireball — legal at CAST_COOLDOWN=333ms, arriving ~550ms after the kill at typical 8u range (217ms flight, measured) — lands inside the corpse's 320-999ms ECS residency window and is consumed. Consequences the player actually sees: the cast is wasted and its mana with it; the live enemy standing directly behind takes zero damage; the projectile detonates on empty air; and because `hitEntity.health <= 0` sets wasKill=true, the game rewards this non-event with the full KILL-strength camera shake (0.8 instead of 0.4), a 1.8x spark burst, a floating damage number over an invisible dead body, and even +5 XP (grantXP fires on any hit).

So the feedback is not just absent — it is actively lying to the player, telling them they landed a kill on empty ground while the zombie behind walks through untouched. Severity MEDIUM is honest and arguably conservative: no crash or data loss, but it degrades pack fighting, the game's primary loop, and the claim understated the window by ~3x.

verdict.title: Chain lightning targets a 250ms-stale MINIMAP snapshot, not the live ECS
verdict.reason:
MECHANISM IS REAL, MAGNITUDE IS FABRICATED. Verified: EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:58 does read `useGameStore.getState().mobEntities`; MinimapSyncSystem.jsx:13 (`now - _lastMinimapUpdate > 250`) is its only writer. Not fixed on HEAD (git log -3 = 1386b5e/45778e7/a8c7b71, all docs commits). I wrote an independent probe mounting the REAL MinimapSyncSystem + REAL EnhancedMagicSystem over the REAL ECS with a controllable clock (preserved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kz-Code/c7297111-afb7-46c9-83b3-6edc09ed7f41/scratchpad/__refute_chain_stale.test.jsx; removed from repo to keep the tree clean).

Q1 CONFIRMS the throttle: snapshot unchanged at +16ms, refreshed at +280ms.

But the claim's evidence is PHYSICALLY UNREACHABLE. P8 asserts a snapshot saying the mob is 30u out while it is really 4u away -- a 26u error. The fastest mob in the game is the skitterling at 3.8 u/s (mobTypes.js:14), so a 250ms window permits at most 0.95u of drift. A 26u snapshot error requires 104 u/s. The probe hand-injected a store state MinimapSyncSystem can never emit and labeled it "(real system)". The claim's own why_it_matters states the true figure (~0.95u) and then contradicts it.

Q2 REFUTES THE HEADLINE end-to-end: a skitterling 4u from the target ("right next to the one you hit"), sprinting AWAY at max speed, IS still chained -- snapshot dist 4.00u, live 4.38u, both far inside the 8u chainRange. damage calls = [{"id":1,"dmg":90},{"id":2,"dmg":27}]; B took 27 damage (health 973, not 1000). Pushing a 4u-adjacent mob past 8u needs >4u of drift vs a 0.95u physics cap.

Q4 (my attempt to BUILD the boundary false-miss) FAILED to produce one: realized staleness at impact is only ~0.38u (projectile flight is 167ms at speed 60, so the snapshot is typically <130ms old when the chain fires). The mob sat at 8.02u live -- genuinely outside the 8u range -- so the chain was CORRECT to skip it. Q3 sweep: stale-vs-live verdicts diverge only in a snapshot band of 8.0-8.9u even at the theoretical 0.95u worst case; realized, that band is ~8.0-8.4u.

Sub-claim (b), new spawns invisible for <=250ms, is mechanically true but SpawnerSystem.jsx:145-148 only spawns in chunks whose center is 20-90u from the player, on a 1/sec tick.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Essentially none, and NOT what the claim describes. The stated impact ("chain lightning unpredictably skips enemies standing right next to the one you hit", "bolts visibly fly to empty air") is disproven: a mob 4u away is reliably chained even when fleeing at max speed. The genuine residue is a sub-half-unit (~0.38-0.5u realized; 0.95u theoretical) fuzz on the 8u range boundary, affecting only a mob sitting within ~0.5u of that boundary while moving radially at top speed -- an error narrower than a mob's own body (0.7-1.6u wide). Arc VFX endpoints lag by the same sub-body-width amount, which is not perceptible as "empty air" on a 160ms transient bolt. A player cannot distinguish this from normal range adjudication.

Severity is INFLATED: claimed MEDIUM, actually LOW -- an architectural inconsistency worth a cheap one-line fix (chain lightning is indeed the only damage system reading the throttled minimap mirror instead of mobsQuery live), but not a gameplay defect. The entire MEDIUM rating rests on the 26u snapshot error, which cannot physically occur.

verdict.title: Lightning's `stunDuration` is dead data — the stun was never built
verdict.reason:
The mechanical grep reproduces, but the claim's framing and its "zero gates" evidence are both refuted.

REPRODUCED: `grep -rn 'stunDuration' src/ tests/` in /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend returns exactly one line — src/game/spells.js:67 `stunDuration: 1,`. The cited file:line is real and says what the claim says. Confirmed the three siblings ARE consumed at src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:371-373 (sec.maxChains / sec.chainRange / sec.chainDamageReduction -> applyChainLightning -> solveChainTargets), and every other spell's secondary fields are consumed in the same switch at EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:352-380 (burn: sec.duration+sec.damagePerSecond; freeze: sec.slowPercent+sec.freezeChance; pierce: sec.lifestealPercent+sec.pierceCount). So stunDuration is genuinely the one unread key.

REFUTED — "zero gates" is FALSE, and it is the load-bearing error. /Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/tests/gates/elemancer-noremesh-gates.test.js:41-42 is a live gate that EXPLICITLY forbids the stun plumbing:
    expect(read('EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx')).not.toMatch(/mobSlowEffects|mobStunEffects/);
    expect(read('store/useGameStore.jsx')).not.toMatch(/mobSlowEffects|mobStunEffects/);
Its header comment states: "the dead mobSlowEffects plumbing (shipped with zero readers; deleted M4) STAYS dead." I ran it — `npx vitest run tests/gates/elemancer-noremesh-gates.test.js` => 9/9 PASSED. So the stun was not an accidental omission; it was DELIBERATELY DELETED in M4 and is test-locked against resurrection. CC was re-architected: mob slow now flows via zoneSlowMult (SimplifiedNPCSystem/AIWorkerSystem, gated at the same file line 38) and spellSlowMult (freeze). Implementing the claim's implied fix would turn a currently-green gate RED.

NOT A STALE FINDING: git log -3 = 1386b5e / 45778e7 / a8c7b71 (all docs commits); the line is present on HEAD. Not "already fixed" — it is intentionally-inert-by-design.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None — zero, and the claim concedes this itself ("player_impact: None today"). An unread key on an object literal is inert: the `case 'chain'` branch in EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx reads exactly three fields and never touches the fourth, so no code path, frame, or player interaction can differ. No player ever experiences this.

The claim's narrative — "a designed mechanic silently never shipped, and the data file makes it look like it did" — is contradicted by the codebase's own test-enforced record of deliberately removing the stun (M4) and gating it out. This is a Kevin-decided design decision, not a shipped-broken mechanic.

Residue (janitorial, not a bug): one stale key at src/game/spells.js:67 should be deleted or annotated as intentionally-inert so it stops baiting exactly this class of false finding. Severity LOW was already the floor; even LOW overstates it — this is code hygiene with no runtime surface.

verdict.title: Spell crits are mechanically invisible: the crit-feel proxy (damage>=40) is fully saturated for every spell, and the solver's isCrit/color are discarded
verdict.reason:
RE-RAN THE EVIDENCE (did not trust the claim). Wrote my own probe against the real solver + real SPELL_TYPES roster, ran under vitest, then deleted it. Output reproduces the claimant's numbers exactly (arcane noncrit=72, crit=130 -> 72*1.8=130), so their evidence was genuine.

CITES ARE REAL AND ACCURATE:
- frontend/src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:202 = `const { damage: finalDamage } = solveSpellDamage(effectiveStats, baseDamage, spellType);` -- destructures ONLY damage. `grep -n isCrit src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx` -> ZERO hits; the spell system never mentions isCrit.
- frontend/src/utils/combat.js:16-35 returns {damage, isCrit, color}; color = #FF4500/#00BFFF/#FFD700/#9932CC.
- Sole production consumers: Components.jsx:250 (melee, takes damage+isCrit) and EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:202 (damage only). NEITHER destructures `color` -> color is dead output.
- frontend/src/game/spells.js header literally says the B2 unify "killed the legacy drift (fire was #FF4500, lightning #FFD700, arcane #9932CC)". combat.js still returns those exact hexes; combat.test.js:42-45 pins them and runs GREEN (7/7 passed).

NOT ALREADY FIXED: HEAD=1386b5e (docs-only, as are 45778e7/a8c7b71). `git show HEAD:frontend/src/EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx | sed -n 202p` is byte-identical to the working tree. Unrelated to the 926751e/15fcc96 fixes.

MECHANISM CORRECTION (claim was incomplete; truth is worse). The claim says there is "no distinct shake." Actually damageMob (CombatSystem.jsx:57) and DamageNumber (combatVfx.jsx:23) DO fire crit feel -- 1.6 shake, 'crit' hitstop tier, 60-spark spray, 64px `${damage}!` -- but off a MAGNITUDE PROXY `damage >= 40`, which an in-code comment admits is "NOT the crit source-of-truth." My probe proves that proxy is SATURATED for all four spells:
  fireball  noncrit=60  CRIT-feel | crit=108 CRIT-feel
  iceball   noncrit=48  CRIT-feel | crit=86  CRIT-feel
  lightning noncrit=90  CRIT-feel | crit=162 CRIT-feel
  arcane    noncrit=72  CRIT-feel | crit=130 CRIT-feel
  melee     noncrit=20  plain     | crit=40  CRIT-feel   <-- proxy tracks the REAL roll only by luck (2.0x pushes 20 -> exactly the 40 threshold)
So crit and non-crit spell hits are pixel-identical in shake/hitstop/sparks/font. Threading isCrit through line 202 alone would NOT fix it -- damageMob recomputes its own and accepts no isCrit param.

ONE SUB-CLAIM OVERSTATED (corrected, not passed through): "the player receives no signal distinguishing them" is FALSE -- the damage digits differ visibly (72 vs 130). What is absent is any CRIT-SPECIFIC affordance.

SEVERITY: LOW is honest, not inflated. Damage is applied correctly; this is combat readability/game-feel, not a correctness bug. The `color` half is genuine rot (dead output pinned by a live green test) but has ZERO player impact and should not carry the finding.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, and it is the readability half only. Spell crits are a 1.8x swing at up to 50% chance, and every feedback channel the game owns -- camera shake, hitstop, spark count, damage-number font and the "!" suffix -- renders a crit and a non-crit spell IDENTICALLY, because all four spells clear the damage>=40 crit proxy even on a normal hit. The player's only cue that a crit landed is reading the raw digits (72 vs 130); there is no dedicated crit affordance, and the game already computed the true isCrit and threw it away. Melee, by contrast, gets a correct crit tell. So a player does experience a genuine asymmetry -- magic combat has a flat, undifferentiated hit feel while melee punches -- but it is a game-feel/legibility defect, not lost or wrong damage. The second half of the claim (the legacy #FF4500/#00BFFF/#FFD700/#9932CC palette) has NO player impact whatsoever: no production code reads that `color` field. It is dead code pinned by a passing test -- a maintenance issue worth a cleanup, not a player-facing bug.

verdict.title: Impact spark burst carries no element identity (pale lavender confetti for every spell)
verdict.reason:
Reproduced the claim's inputs, then disproved its conclusion.

WIRE IS GENUINE (not fabricated): SPARK_PROFILE = fire 52/ice 42/lightning 48/arcane 46 (/Users/kz/Code/Crafty/frontend/src/game/spellVisualProfiles.js:13-19) x 1.8 kill multiplier (EnhancedMagicSystem.jsx:126) = 94/76/86/83, exactly the claim's numbers. Live-confirmed via instrumented store: "WIRE fireball #FF7A3C 94". Colors match MAGIC tokens (theme/tokens.js:39-40).

COLOR IS NOT LOST DOWNSTREAM: GPUSparkSystem.jsx:200-202 writes per-instance aColor from the passed hex; vertex shader forwards it (vColor = aColor); fragment shader deliberately preserves hue: glow = vColor * (1.0 + vLife*2.0) (GPUSparkSystem.jsx:74).

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE (capture-harness artifact, not a render bug): in capture mode aStartTime = -CAPTURE_SPARK_PHASE (-0.30) while uTime is frozen at 0, so t=0.30 forever, inside the 0.85 lifetime -> sparks NEVER die. capture.mjs:334-352 shoots all four spell states in ONE page session; spawnDeterministicCast clears projectiles/telegraphs/impacts but NOT the GPU spark pool; all four use the same impact world-point (App.jsx:425). So each later baseline retains every prior element's spray at the same screen location.
MEASURED on committed baselines (spray box x710-890,y315-405): speck px 840 -> 871 -> 1192 -> 1564 (monotonic growth); 99.9% of spell-cast's speck pixels still present in spell-iceball, 87.5% in spell-arcane. That is why fire-vs-ice looks identical: the iceball frame still contains the fireball's sparks.

CLAIM'S HUE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT REPRODUCE: using the same per-row-median background rejection it describes, the ADDED spark light measures 12deg/11deg/15deg/0deg (WARM), not 260-273deg lavender. Visual read of baseline/spell-cast.png shows warm pink/salmon specks. 260-273deg is what you get measuring the RAW pixel without subtracting the blue sky (raw fire cores measured 306deg) - i.e. it measured sky-contaminated pixels despite claiming rejection. Its "66 of 23,625 px differ" also did not reproduce (I measure 197/16200 = 1.22%).

CITED FILE:LINE: real but overstated. spell-vfx-gates.test.js has the SPARK_PROFILE source-regex (~line 48, not 41), but the file's own header says the gates are intentionally STATIC so they run GPU-free in CI, with pixels covered by the puppeteer visual gate.

Process hygiene: killed all vite + leaked puppeteer Chrome (verified 0 residual).
verdict.real_player_impact:
NONE - the mechanism is capture-mode-exclusive and structurally unreachable in gameplay. With isCaptureMode() false, the clock advances and sparks use real 0.35-0.9s lifetimes, so they die and cross-element accumulation cannot occur; a player casting a fireball only ever sees fire sparks.

Proven positively, not just argued: I ran an A/B isolation probe (each element on a FRESH page load = empty spark pool, captured twice - once normally, once with triggerGPUSparks suppressed - so the diff is exactly the spray). Result: fireball's spray renders as warm pink/orange specks, iceball's as a tight pale-blue cluster, and the two spray masks share 0.0% of pixels (entirely different pixels, entirely different hue families). Element identity reads correctly. The claimed "every spell's impact looks like the same pale lavender confetti" is false for the player.

SEVERITY HONEST BUT MISDIRECTED: the claim self-labels LOW/HYPOTHESIS/INCONCLUSIVE, which is honest about its uncertainty, but its player_impact statement is refuted.

SEPARATE REAL DEFECT FOUND (byproduct, LOW, no player impact - worth its own ticket): the spell-iceball / spell-lightning / spell-arcane baselines are CONTAMINATED by prior elements' immortal sparks, so the visual gate for those three states does not cleanly gate their own impact spray (it re-asserts the fireball's spray). Fix = clear/reset the GPU spark pool in spawnDeterministicCast, or reload the page between spell captures.
