verdict.title: `dodge` is the only intent with no keyup handler — a Shift press while input is inactive LATCHES and fires an uncommanded dodge-roll the instant play resumes
verdict.reason:
SOURCE (Components.jsx, clean vs HEAD — `git status --porcelain src/Components.jsx` empty; last 3 commits 1386b5e/45778e7/a8c7b71 are docs-only, so NOT already fixed): line 347-349 `if (e.code === 'ShiftLeft' || e.code === 'ShiftRight') { setIntent('dodge', true); }` on keydown, ungated by `active`. `handleKeyUp` (387+) clears moveF/B/L/R, Space, KeyR, KeyV, KeyX, KeyZ — there is NO Shift branch (`grep -rn "Shift" src/Components.jsx` returns exactly ONE hit: line 347, the keydown). Whole-app greps: the ONLY `setIntent('dodge', false)` is Components.jsx:883, inside useFrame gated on `isLocked`; the ONLY `resetInput()` caller in app code is Components.jsx:211, on DEATH. `setActive()` (input/inputState.js) only flips the bool + notifies — it clears no intents. So nothing clears dodge while input is inactive.

EXECUTED (my own Playwright probe, not the claim's): I did NOT trust the claimed output. Built a 2-arm differential with an anti-vacuous LIVENESS gate first — a COMMANDED dodge while ACTIVE must burn the cooldown, else a null result is meaningless. Oracle is behavioral, not the intent flag: `abilityCooldowns.dodge` is mirrored from the live `dodgeStateRef` INSIDE useFrame (Components.jsx:934), so it only moves if the roll actually ran.
  LIVENESS (both arms): {"ready":true,"remaining":0} -> {"ready":false,"remaining":0.8} => loop ALIVE (consumer genuinely ticking).
  CONTROL (leave play via a real `pointerlockchange`, press NOTHING, resume): before {"ready":true} -> after {"ready":true} => NO dodge.
  LATCH   (leave play, press AND RELEASE Shift while INACTIVE, resume pressing NOTHING): before {"ready":true,"remaining":0} -> after {"ready":false,"remaining":0.8}, readyAt 112.148 -> 133.746 => UNCOMMANDED DODGE FIRED.
Both arms passed their assertions. The two arms are identical except the single Shift press+release, so the differential isolates the cause.

I PROVED WHAT THE CLAIM COULD NOT: the claim's "HONEST LIMIT" was that its harness never ticked useFrame, so it could only prove the latch, not the roll. Root cause of that: the player useFrame early-returns until `isWorldBuiltRef` (Components.jsx:822), and the spawn chunk is meshed by a web worker (Terrain.jsx:579) that never completes under headless swiftshader. I unblocked it via the app's own in-app flag (`setIsSpawnChunkLoaded(true)`, exactly what DebugOverlay.jsx:106 flips) and confirmed the roll FIRES.

HARNESS HONESTY (2 accommodations, both non-distorting): (a) headless Chromium cannot hold pointer lock (page threw "The root document of this element is not valid for pointer lock"), so I resumed play via the app's own `forcePlay` test hook = `setActive(true)` (App.jsx:283) — the EXACT single line `handlePointerLockChange` executes on lock (Components.jsx:489). I verified the only other thing re-lock does is `markGameStarted`, which just sets a boolean (useGameStore.jsx:712) — so NO intent-clearing step was bypassed. (b) forced isSpawnChunkLoaded to unblock the loop. Neither touches the input/dodge path; the CONTROL arm carried BOTH accommodations and did NOT fire; so they cannot manufacture the result.

Note: the existing e2e suite (gameplay-flow.spec.js) currently fails at boot in this env, and a stale /tmp log contained an unrelated Babel parse error from another agent's transient edit — I confirmed the app itself compiles and serves (HTTP 200) and did not draw any conclusion from those artifacts. All probe files and processes cleaned up.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and reachable, not theoretical. `InputManager.jsx` calls `document.exitPointerLock()` when the player opens the inventory/building tools (:111), achievements (:161), crafting via a smith NPC (:198), trading (:207), spell upgrades (:234), and settings — every one of these sets `active=false` while the window keydown listener stays attached and UNGATED. So a Shift press anywhere the pointer is unlocked (title menu, pause/settings, a shift-click while managing inventory, or Shift held during an alt-tab) latches `dodge=true` permanently, and the moment the player closes the panel and re-locks, the very next frame fires an involuntary dodge-roll with zero input: player displacement (the classic "I closed my inventory and rolled off the ledge"), plus it burns the 0.8s cooldown and the i-frames — so the defensive dodge the player needs for the boss's next swing is unavailable. Notably the death path IS protected (Components.jsx:211 calls resetInput() on death), which shows the codebase already recognises stale-intent carryover as a bug class — the unlock path just never got the same treatment. SEVERITY: MEDIUM is HONEST, not inflated — it is an uncommanded player action with genuine combat/traversal consequence, but no save corruption or crash, and it requires a Shift press while unlocked rather than firing every session. Fix is one line: add a `ShiftLeft/ShiftRight -> setIntent('dodge', false)` branch to handleKeyUp (and/or clear intents on the active->false transition).

verdict.title: Panel-stack trap CONFIRMED via the merchant/trading panel (and achievements/spell-upgrades/world-manager) — but the CHEST headline is REFUTED: the chest UI never renders at all, because App's gameState selector omits showChestInterface
verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED (mechanism + player-reachable trap) — with the headline chest scenario REFUTED
verdict.reason:
CITED LINES ARE REAL AND SAY WHAT THE CLAIM SAYS. InputManager.jsx:96-117 toggleUI closes only 6 setters (Inventory/Crafting/Magic/BuildingTools/Settings/QuestLog) then calls requestPointerLockSafely(state) unconditionally in the !newValue close-branch, reading no other panel flag. panelState.js:12-18 lists 13 PANEL_FLAGS. I REPRODUCED IT (headed Chromium, real key presses, GENUINE browser-granted lock — probe-v3): after chest-open -> E -> E, instrumented counters showed lockCalls 1->2 AND lockGrants 1->2 (an actual grant, not merely a request — the original claim only counted CALLS), with the panel flag still set; a real LMB then mutated the world: worldBlocks 0 -> 1.

HEADLINE REFUTED. The chest UI NEVER RENDERS. App.jsx:72-102 builds `gameState` via useShallow omitting every chest key (`sed -n '72,102p' src/App.jsx | grep -c Chest` => 0), so MenuSystem.jsx:91's `gameState.showChestInterface` is permanently undefined. Runtime proof (probe-v5/v6): with showChestInterface=true in the store, visible [role=dialog] list = [] at every step, while the "Inventory" dialog rendered normally in the same run (so MenuSystem re-renders fine). ChestInventoryPanel has no early-return (it defaults chestData), so the only blocker is the missing selector key. Method note: that final run replayed the browser's own grant signal (pointerLockElement + pointerlockchange) because this machine's window cannot take OS focus and Chrome refuses grants in EVERY mode incl. real Chrome (WrongDocumentError); no app code was stubbed, and a genuine grant of the identical re-lock was directly observed in probe-v3. The panel closing on click in v7 is an emulation artifact — under a real lock, clicks target the locked canvas and cannot reach the overlay, which IS the "panel unusable" failure.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: HEAD=1386b5e, last 3 commits docs-only; `git show HEAD:frontend/src/InputManager.jsx | sed -n '96,117p'` still shows the 6 setters + unconditional requestPointerLockSafely. Unrelated to 926751e/15fcc96. Cleaned up: killed vite + all playwright browsers.

YES, a player is affected — but via the merchant/trading panel, not the chest. Talk to a merchant villager (G) to open the trade panel, press E (muscle memory for inventory), press E again to dismiss it: the trade panel is still on screen, but the pointer is re-locked, so there is no cursor to click trade slots with, and LMB/RMB now mine/place blocks behind the visible panel (mutating the world unintentionally). verdicts_joined.player_impact: Hold E a beat too long (or a sticky/stuck key, or leaning on the keyboard) and the inventory strobes open/closed while the pointer lock is hammered. verdict.title: No `e.repeat` guard: holding a panel key (E/C/B/M/L/Tab/U) strobes the panel and thrashes pointer lock — but it does NOT kill input
verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED (core defect) — but severity INFLATED and the stated causal chain REFUTED
verdict.reason:
REPRODUCED. Wrote a jsdom vitest probe driving the REAL `useInputManager` (src/InputManager.jsx), the REAL `useGameStore`, and the REAL `isAnyPanelOpen` gate, dispatching genuine `KeyboardEvent{repeat:true}`. Pointer lock was modeled GENEROUSLY (every re-lock granted). One physical press of E + 6 OS auto-repeats produced: `press inv=true exit=1 req=1 / repeat#1 inv=false exit=1 req=2 / ... / repeat#6 inv=true exit=4 req=4` -> "PANEL FLIPS from ONE held key: 6", 4 exitPointerLock + 4 requestPointerLock. C/B/M/L each flip true/false/true/false/true (5 lock ops); Tab strobes too (3 exit + 4 req). Root cause is exact: InputManager.jsx:59 re-reads `useGameStore.getState()` fresh per event and zustand `set` is synchronous, so each repeat keydown sees the flipped flag and inverts it again via toggleUI (InputManager.jsx:96-117, which calls document.exitPointerLock() on open / requestPointerLockSafely() on close).

CITED LINES: InputManager.jsx:58 (`const handleKeyDown = (event) => {`) is REAL and has no repeat guard — load-bearing. Components.jsx:498 (`setActive(false)` in handlePointerLockError) is REAL. BUT Components.jsx:337 handleKeyDown is a BOGUS citation — it contains only movement-intent writes (`setIntent('moveF', true)` etc.), which are idempotent and repeat-safe; it has zero panel/pointer-lock logic (grep for setShow|exitPointerLock|requestPointerLock over lines 337-470 returns nothing).

NOT FIXED ON HEAD: `git log -1 -- frontend/src/InputManager.jsx` = ca26383 (2026-06-18); no working-tree modification; grep for e.repeat/event.repeat in src/ returns zero real guards. Recent commits (1386b5e, 45778e7, a8c7b71) are docs-only, unrelated.

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: the headline chain "Chrome rate-limits rapid re-lock and rejects it -> pointerlockerror -> Components.jsx:498 setActive(false) -> input goes dead" does NOT hold here. Per W3C Pointer Lock 2.0 (w3c.github.io/pointerlock, A1): "a requestPointerLock() call immediately after a programmatic lock exit (through an exitPointerLock() call) MUST succeed when transient activation is available" — and the spec's reject condition requires BOTH no-transient-activation AND no-prior-exitPointerLock()-release, so it fails on both conjuncts. Crafty exits PROGRAMMATICALLY via document.exitPointerLock(); the ~1.25s Chrome throttle applies only to the Esc/default-unlock-gesture path. Crafty's own KEVIN-FIX C3 comment (Components.jsx:494) even says "Chrome's ~1-2.5s POST-ESC cooldown" — the claim borrowed that comment and misapplied it to a path it does not govern. The claim's "dead input" outcome only reproduced when I FORCED rejectRelock=true, which the spec says will not happen on this path.

Cleaned up: removed all probe files (tests/zzr-*.test.jsx, tests/e2e/zzr-repeat-refute.spec.js) and killed the stray vite server on :4179, so nothing leaks into CI.
verdict.real_player_impact:
REAL but milder than claimed. Holding a panel key past the OS auto-repeat delay (~500ms macOS default) — trivially easy on E, the most-used panel key in a Minecraft-like, and also on C/B/M/L/Tab/U — makes the panel flicker open/closed at the repeat rate (~30/s) while pointer lock is exited and re-acquired ~15x/s each, so the cursor and mouse-look flicker with it. On key release the panel lands on a coin-flip parity (open or closed depending on how long you held), which is nondeterministic and disorienting. A sticky/stuck key or leaning on the keyboard triggers it too.

What does NOT happen: the player is NOT left with dead input. Because the exits are programmatic, the spec mandates the re-locks succeed, so `pointerlockerror` is not fired and `setActive(false)` (Components.jsx:498) is not reached via this path. The state is always recoverable — worst case the player presses the key again or clicks the canvas.

Honest severity: LOW-MEDIUM (a visible, ugly input/UI glitch on core keys), not MEDIUM-"can kill input entirely". Still worth the one-line fix `if (event.repeat) return;` at the top of InputManager.jsx handleKeyDown — it is cheap, kills the strobe on all 7 keys at once, and is the standard guard for discrete-action keys.

verdicts_joined.title: KEY_MAP anti-drift gate is one-directional — Q (claim quest) and L (quest log) are live but never advertised, hiding the quest reward loop
verdicts_joined.file_line: tests/game/keyMap.test.js:35-42 (checks map->handler only) ; src/game/keyMap.js:8-35 (no L/Q/F3 rows) ; src/InputManager.jsx:123 (KeyL), :133 (KeyQ), :145 (F3)

verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
Imported the real KEY_MAP in the running page:
  KEY_MAP advertises: KeyF, KeyT, KeyR, KeyV, KeyX, KeyZ, KeyE, KeyM, KeyC, KeyB, KeyU, KeyG, KeyH, Tab, Escape  (15 codes)

verdict.title: KEY_MAP anti-drift gate is one-directional — Q (claim quest) and L (quest log) are live but never advertised, hiding the quest reward loop
verdict.reason: The mechanical half reproduces; the load-bearing player-impact half is false. VERIFIED TRUE: src/game/keyMap.js has no L/Q/F3 rows; src/InputManager.jsx:123 (KeyL), :133 (KeyQ), :145 (F3) are live; tests/game/keyMap.test.js:35-42 asserts map->handler only, never the reverse; I ran `npx vitest run tests/game/keyMap.test.js` -> 4/4 PASS while L/Q/F3 sit unadvertised, proving the gate's one-directionality; src/ui/CombatInstructions.jsx is the sole KEY_MAP renderer. REFUTED: the claim asserts "the entire quest reward loop sits behind two keys the game never tells you about" and "[the player] never learns that Q claims a finished quest". Both are false. (1) src/QuestSystem.jsx:207 fires a toast on completion: `Quest Complete: ${quest.title}! Click Q to claim reward.` — NotificationStack is mounted at src/HUD.jsx:596, so the game teaches Q at the exact moment Q becomes relevant. (2) src/QuestSystem.jsx:469-477 — QuestTracker (always-on HUD, mounted src/HUD.jsx:594) renders for every completed-unclaimed quest a primary Button labeled "Press Q" (or "Claim" on touch) with `onClick={() => onClaim(quest.id)}`. The reward loop is NOT keyboard-gated: it is a mouse-clickable button that also names the key. src/QuestSystem.jsx:434 `expanded = userToggled === null ? !touch : userToggled` means the tracker is expanded BY DEFAULT on desktop — the claim's own declared domain. The claim quotes QuestLog.jsx:65 ("Q claims a finished quest FROM THE TRACKER") yet never opened the tracker. Not a stale/already-fixed issue: cited commits 926751e and 15fcc96 exist but do not touch keyMap.js.
verdict.real_player_impact: Essentially none for the claimed defect. The quest reward loop is advertised twice (completion toast naming Q + an always-visible "Press Q" button in the desktop-default-expanded QuestTracker) and is fully completable by mouse click without ever knowing the Q key exists. Residual, much smaller and distinct from what was filed: L (quest log) is taught only at QuestLog.jsx:65, inside the panel you can only open with L — a genuine circular-discoverability nit — and F3 (debug stats) is unlisted. But QuestLog.jsx:7 self-describes as a "Read-only narrative surface — claiming still happens via Q in the QuestTracker": title, description, progress and the claim button are already in the always-visible tracker, so never discovering L costs the player lore/giver flavor text only, not the reward loop. Severity is inflated: the LOW tag is paired with a narrative ("hides the entire quest reward loop", "same class as the 'M - Magic' HUD lie") that the code contradicts — the M bug advertised a key that did nothing, whereas here the feature is reachable and self-advertising without the key. Worth at most a separate cosmetic ticket: add a reverse assertion to the gate plus an explicit `unadvertised: ['F3']` allowlist, and add an L row to KEY_MAP.

verdicts_joined.title: The autosave DESTROYS the player's world on their next visit: nothing auto-resumes the save at boot, but the autosave still targets the SAME world slot
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/App.jsx:220-261 (autosave effect, deps []) + src/store/useGameStore.jsx:967-973 (saveActiveWorld reuses getActiveWorldId()); loadWorldData is called from exactly ONE place: src/MenuSystem.jsx:170 -> the WorldManager 'Load' button
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: `crafty_active_world` survives a page reload, but NOTHING calls loadWorldData at boot — the store comes up at its defaults (level 1, 0 coins, empty worldBlocks). The autosave subscription mounts unconditionally with `[]` deps and no gameStarted/isWorldBuilt guard, and saveActiveWorld does `let id = getActiveWorldId()` — i.e. it writes the EMPTY fresh-boot state straight into the slot holding the player's real world. The save system is a data-destruction machine: it faithfully persists a world it never reads back, then overwrites it. It has gone unnoticed precisely because there is no resume path, so the blob is never read in normal play. Fix needs BOTH halves: (a) auto-load the active world at boot / offer a Continue, and (b) refuse to autosave a world that was never loaded (guard on gameStarted or a `hydratedFromSlot` flag).
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
LIVE, real Chromium + real vite dev + a REAL page reload (playwright, scratchpad live-save.spec.js):
  SESSION 1 - PERSISTED blob: {"level":15,"coins":3150,"blocks":3,"won":true,"inv":{...,"Diamond":12}}
  SESSION 2 @boot - live store: level 1 coins 0 blocks 0 won false   <-- the game did NOT auto-resume
  SESSION 2 @boot - blob on disk still: level 15 coins 3150
  SESSION 2 @boot - active id: local_1783964805615 (UNCHANGED - still points at the real save)
  SESSION 2 - player picks up ONE item, 16s pass. Same slot local_1783964805615 now holds:
     {"level":1,"coins":0,"blocks":0,"won":false}
  >>> SESSION-1 WORLD RECOVERABLE? NO -- DESTROYED BY THE FRESH-BOOT AUTOSAVE
(1 passed). Independently reproduced at unit level against the real store + real worldSaves + a verbatim copy of the App.jsx:220-261 wiring (probe3 P12/P13): 'SESSION 1 saved: level 21 coins 3150 blocks 4 gameWon true' -> reload -> 'AFTER 5 IDLE SECONDS: level 1 coins 0 blocks 0 gameWon false'.
NOTE / honest correction: at unit level the mere App+QuestSystem mount fires the overwrite within 5s of an IDLE title screen; LIVE it does not (React effect ordering — the quest mirror effect at App.jsx:174 writes questState BEFORE the autosave effect at :220 subscribes, so boot itself is not a trigger). The destruction is therefore not instant-on-idle, but it fires on the FIRST inventory/block/level change of the new session. I verified that live.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: A player builds for hours, closes the tab, comes back, is dropped into an empty level-1 world, and the moment they pick up a single item their entire world/character/win is permanently gone. Total, unrecoverable, silent progress loss for every returning player. This is a ship-blocker.
verdicts_joined.domain: Save / load / persistence / migration

verdict.title: Autosave destroys the player's world on their next visit: nothing auto-resumes at boot, but the autosave still targets the SAME world slot
verdict.reason:
I could not refute it; it reproduces two independent ways.

(1) LIVE, real Chromium + real vite + a REAL page.reload() (my own spec, frontend/tests/e2e/zzz-refute-autosave-destroy.spec.js, 1 passed in 53.1s):
  SESSION 1 live: { level: 9, coins: 3150, won: true } | slot: local_1784026908899 | blob has 3150: true
  SESSION 2 @boot live store: { level: 1, coins: 0, won: false, blocks: 0 }
  SESSION 2 @boot slot: local_1784026908899 | blob still has 3150: true
  AUTO-RESUMED? NO — dropped into a fresh level-1 world
  SESSION 2 after ONE pickup + 8s — slot local_1784026908899 still has 3150: false
  SESSION-1 WORLD RECOVERABLE? NO — DESTROYED
(2) Unit level against the REAL store + REAL worldSaves + REAL createAutosave + a verbatim transplant of the App.jsx:220-261 wiring (frontend/tests/zz-refute-autosave-destroys-world.test.js): same slot, blocks 2 -> 0, coins 3150 gone, listWorlds().length === 1 (clobbered, not a new slot).

CITED CODE IS REAL AND ACCURATE:
- src/App.jsx:220-261 — autosave effect, deps [], no gameStarted/hydration guard; the ONLY early-return is `if (st.isCaptureMode) return`.
- src/store/useGameStore.jsx:967-973 — `saveActiveWorld: (position) => { ... let id = getActiveWorldId(); if (!id) { id = 'local_' + Date.now(); setActiveWorldId(id); } writeWorld(id, ...) }`.
- grep of the whole src/ tree: loadWorldData has exactly ONE call site — MenuSystem.jsx:170 `onWorldLoad={gameState.loadWorldData}` -> WorldManager's Load button. No boot-time load, no zustand persist middleware (useGameStore.jsx:48 is a plain `create((set,get) => ...)`).

NOT ALREADY FIXED: git status shows App.jsx / useGameStore.jsx / worldSaves.js clean at HEAD, so what I read IS HEAD. Today's two fixes are unrelated subsystems — 926751e = quest multi-claim (QuestSystem.jsx, game/questClaim.js), 15fcc96 = block-ids (world/Terrain.jsx, world/blockIds.js). Neither touches the autosave or the world-slot layer.

I ACTIVELY TRIED TO REFUTE IT and failed on the strongest candidate: does "Start Adventure" mint a NEW slot (which would preserve the old save)? No — MenuSystem.jsx:60 calls only `markGameStarted()`; it never mints or clears a world id. There is no Continue/Resume control anywhere. So the stale `crafty_active_world` survives the reload and remains the autosave target.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED (bonus): tests/e2e/save-load.spec.js — the gate whose own comment says it exists because "live world LOAD/resume never probed" — HAND-CALLS `g().loadWorldData(blob)` and fakes a fresh session via `setState({gameWon:false, coins:0})`. It never reloads the page. It proves the serializer round-trips while never exercising resume: a vacuous gate (pending task #5's exact class).
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — on the DEFAULT player path, no World Manager interaction required.

Session 1: player boots, clicks "Start Adventure", plays. The autosave mints slot local_X on its first fire and persists level/coins/blocks/inventory/win-state there. Player closes the tab.
Session 2: player returns. There is no Continue/Resume, and nothing calls loadWorldData at boot, so they land on the title menu with the store at defaults (level 1, 0 coins, empty worldBlocks). They click "Start Adventure" — which only sets gameStarted and does NOT re-point the world slot — and are dropped into an empty fresh world. `crafty_active_world` still points at local_X. The moment they pick up ONE item (or place a block, or gain a level), the unguarded autosave subscription fires, and 5s later saveActiveWorld writes the EMPTY fresh-boot state straight into local_X. The real world is gone, silently and unrecoverably.

Severity CRITICAL is HONEST, not inflated: total, silent, unrecoverable progress loss for every returning player, on the default path, triggered by the first action any player takes. Ship-blocker.

One nuance I confirmed (the claim itself disclosed it, to its credit): a pure boot-and-immediately-close does NOT overwrite, because createAutosave.flush() only writes when a debounce timer is already pending. So the destruction is not instant-on-idle — it fires on the first inventory/block/level/quest change of the new session. That narrows the trigger but does not reduce the impact, since that change is the first thing a player does.

Fix needs BOTH halves as the claim states: (a) auto-load the active world at boot / offer a Continue, and (b) refuse to autosave a world that was never hydrated (guard on gameStarted or a hydratedFromSlot flag). Half (b) alone stops the data destruction and is the urgent one.

verdicts_joined.title: Every autosave clobbers the player's chosen world name with `Save_<timestamp>`
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/store/useGameStore.jsx:972 (`writeWorld(id, { name: data.save_name, created_at: new Date().toISOString(), ... }, data)`) + src/game/worldSaves.js:35 (`list.unshift({ id, ...meta })`) + src/game/saveSchema.js:16 (`save_name: 'Save_' + new Date().toLocaleString()`)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: saveActiveWorld passes a GENERATED meta (name = `Save_<toLocaleString>`, created_at = now) into writeWorld, which unshifts it over the existing index entry. So the name the player typed in Create World, and the name WorldManager's Save gives ('Guest's World - <date>'), are both destroyed by the very next autosave (<=5s later). created_at is also rewritten to 'now' on every save, so the World Manager's 'created' column actually shows 'last autosaved'. saveActiveWorld should preserve the existing index entry's name/created_at, not synthesize new ones.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: probe2 P11 (real store + real worldSaves): 'after Create/Save-As: index name = "Marcus's Castle"' -> one saveActiveWorld -> 'after ONE autosave: index name = "Save_7/13/2026, 10:25:06 AM"; blob.name = "Save_7/13/2026, 10:25:06 AM"'. Confirmed LIVE in the browser: after a real play session the world list read `["Save_7/13/2026, 10:46:45 AM"]`.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: The World Manager is unusable as a save picker: every world is named an identical-looking timestamp instead of what the player called it. Combined with the CRITICAL finding, a player trying to recover their world cannot even tell which entry it is.
verdicts_joined.domain: Save / load / persistence / migration

verdict.title: Every autosave clobbers the player's chosen world name with Save_<timestamp> (and silently drops is_public + rewrites created_at)
verdict.reason:
Wrote my own vitest probe (jsdom) importing the REAL src/game/worldSaves.js and the REAL useGameStore.saveActiveWorld — nothing under test mocked. Replayed WorldManager.createWorld()'s exact write (name "Marcus's Castle", created_at 2026-01-01, is_public true) + setActiveWorldId, then invoked the same store action App.jsx:227 calls. Output: index entry went from {"name":"Marcus's Castle","created_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","is_public":true} to {"name":"Save_7/14/2026, 3:58:18 AM","created_at":"2026-07-14T10:58:18.198Z","is_owner":true} with the SAME id — a clobber of the existing slot, not a new one. is_public became undefined (a defect the claim did not mention). Probe deleted after the run; tree clean.

All three cited lines are real and verbatim at HEAD: useGameStore.jsx:972 `writeWorld(id, { name: data.save_name, created_at: new Date().toISOString(), is_owner: true }, data)` (confirmed via `git show HEAD:frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx | sed -n 972p`); worldSaves.js:35 `list.unshift({ id, ...meta })` after `.filter(w => w.id !== id)` — replaces the index entry wholesale; saveSchema.js:16 `save_name: `Save_${new Date().toLocaleString()}``.

NOT already fixed: git log on the two files shows no fix; 4414dc6 touched worldSaves.js but was the quota-safe write-ORDER fix (blob before index), never touching meta. Today's fixes 926751e (quest-claim) and 15fcc96 (block-ids) are unrelated domains. Working tree clean for all 4 files.

Reachability: the autosave useEffect in App.jsx is mounted UNCONDITIONALLY (the `import.meta.env.DEV` gate is on a separate effect below it), isCaptureMode defaults false (useGameStore.jsx:57), and the zustand subscription schedules on `s.worldBlocks !== prevS.worldBlocks` — placing/breaking ONE block — with a 5000ms debounce (createAutosave). createWorld() calls setActiveWorldId(id), guaranteeing the just-named world is the autosave target.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real and guaranteed, but metadata-only — no data loss. Player creates a world named "Marcus's Castle" (or hits WorldManager Save, which names it "Guest's World - <date>"), places a single block, and 5 seconds later the World Manager index entry is renamed to `Save_<toLocaleString>`. The world blob itself is intact and still loads; what is corrupted is the index metadata: name (destroyed), created_at (rewritten to now, so the "created" column actually shows "last autosaved"), and is_public (dropped to undefined, so a Public world silently flips to Private / Globe->Lock icon in the list at WorldManager.jsx:345). Every world the player ACTUALLY PLAYS loses the name they gave it; worlds they never load keep their names.

Severity: claim says HIGH; honest rating is MEDIUM-HIGH. Two overstatements in the claim: (a) the clobbered names are NOT "identical-looking" — each carries its own last-autosave timestamp, so entries remain distinguishable by time, just not by player intent; (b) it is not data destruction — the save still loads fine. The defensible headline is that the World Manager stops being a meaningful save PICKER (you can no longer tell which world is which by the name you chose), plus the created/visibility columns display wrong values.

Fix: saveActiveWorld should read the existing index entry and preserve name/created_at/is_public, synthesizing them only for a brand-new slot. Note the trap that makes the current code look plausible: `data.save_name` (blob field) is a DIFFERENT concept from the index `name`, and conflating them is the bug.

verdicts_joined.title: 'Create New World' does not create a new world — it silently clones the current one
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/WorldManager.jsx:65-108 (createWorld: builds `freshBlob`, calls writeWorld + setActiveWorldId, but never resets the store and never calls loadWorldData)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: createWorld writes a minimal blob and points the active slot at it, but leaves the LIVE store untouched. The next autosave (<=5s, triggered by any worldBlocks/inventory/questState change) overwrites that fresh blob with a full snapshot of the world the player was already in. Separately, the freshBlob literal itself is not a valid fresh world: it has no `version`, no `progression`, no `chests`, no `questState` — and loadWorldData falls back to CURRENT state for every missing key, so even explicitly Loading it keeps the old character.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: probe1 P4 (real store + real worldSaves): after Create + ONE autosave into the new slot -> 'blocks = 2 [["1_2_3",5],["4_5_6",2]]  level = 12  coins = 4321' — i.e. the old world verbatim. probe1 P3 (loading the exact freshBlob literal from WorldManager.jsx:73-88): 'level = 12 (fresh world should be 1) / coins = 4321 (should be 0) / totalXP = 99999 / talentPts = 9 / nightCount = 7 / chests = 1 entries -> [["10_5_10",{inventory:{Diamond:64}}]] (should be 0) / questState = {...old quests...} (should be null)'. Only worldBlocks was actually cleared.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: The player asks for a new world (e.g. to start a fresh run, or to make a second world for a sibling) and gets a copy of their old one — same level, same coins, same chest loot, same quest progress, under a name that is then also overwritten. Multi-world play is fundamentally broken.

verdict.title: 'Create New World' does not create a new world — it silently clones the current one
verdict.reason:
I did not take the claimed output on faith — I wrote my own probe (frontend/src/game/__refute_createworld.test.jsx, since deleted) that renders the REAL <WorldManager/> via @testing-library/react and fires REAL clicks ("Create New World" -> type name -> "Create"), against the REAL zustand store and REAL worldSaves.js localStorage layer. Only framer-motion was mocked. It reproduced exactly.

(3) File:line is real and accurate. frontend/src/WorldManager.jsx:65-108 `createWorld` builds `freshBlob` (lines 73-88), calls `writeWorld(id, meta, freshBlob)` + `setActiveWorldId(id)` (lines 91-94), and never resets the store nor calls loadWorldData/onWorldLoad.

(1) Reproduced. Probe P1, after the real click: LIVE STORE after create -> level = 12 | coins = 4321 | blocks = 2 | chests = 1 | questState = {"completed":["slay_10"],...} (i.e. NOT reset). FRESH BLOB on disk -> blocks = [] | has version? false | has progression? false | has chests? false | has questState? false | inventory = {"Diamond":12,"Wood":30} (the live inventory copied verbatim — WorldManager.jsx:77 `inventory: gameState.inventory`; the claim underplays this). Then ONE real autosave tick (`useGameStore.getState().saveActiveWorld(...)`, exactly what App.jsx:227 calls on any worldBlocks/inventory/questState/level change, 5s debounce per App.jsx:219-249): the new slot now reads blocks = 2 [["1_2_3",5],["4_5_6",2]] | level = 12 | coins = 4321 | chests = [["10_5_10",{"inventory":{"Diamond":64}}]] | questState = old — the old world verbatim.
Probe P2, loading the PRISTINE freshBlob through the real store loader: level = 12 (fresh should be 1), coins = 4321 (should be 0), totalXP = 99999, talentPoints = 9, nightCount = 7, chests = 1 entry (should be 0), questState = old (should be null). Only worldBlocks cleared. Root cause is useGameStore.jsx:843-950 `loadWorldData`, which falls back to CURRENT state for every missing key (`prog?.level ?? state.level`, `saveData.chests ? ... : state.chests`, `saveData.questState ?? state.questState`) — and freshBlob has no version/progression/chests/questState.

(2) NOT already fixed on HEAD. HEAD = 1386b5e. The two commits I was told were fixed TODAY are unrelated to this: 926751e = quest multi-claim (R1), 15fcc96 = hotbar block-ids (R4a). `git log -5 -- frontend/src/WorldManager.jsx` shows the most recent touch is 24d88dd (success-message renders green not red) — cosmetic. `git status --short` on WorldManager.jsx / useGameStore.jsx / App.jsx / game/autosave.js is EMPTY, so I reproduced against committed HEAD code, not a dirty tree.

(4) Player-reachable, not dead code: SettingsPanel renders a "Manage Worlds" button (src/ui/GamePanels.jsx:801-810) -> onOpenWorldManager (MenuSystem.jsx:155) -> setShowWorldManager(true) -> <WorldManager onWorldLoad={gameState.loadWorldData}/> (MenuSystem.jsx:167-171) -> the "Create New World" button (WorldManager.jsx:188-194) -> "Create" (line 311). No existing test covers createWorld's behavior.

(5) Severity HIGH is honest, not inflated. A top-level advertised action completely fails its stated purpose and silently misroutes autosaves. It is not CRITICAL only because the old world's blob survives under its own id — nothing is outright destroyed.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Yes — a real player is affected via a fully reachable UI path (Settings -> Manage Worlds -> Create New World -> Create).

The player asks for a new world (fresh run, or a second world for a sibling) and gets a copy of their old one: same level, coins, totalXP, talent points, chest loot, quest progress, and even the same inventory. Within 5 seconds, the first block placed / item picked up / quest ticked fires the autosave, which overwrites the "fresh" blob with a full snapshot of the world they were already in. Multi-world play is fundamentally broken, and the fresh-start intent is unachievable through the UI.

Additional consequence the claim did not state (found in my probe): because the store is never reset, the player keeps playing the OLD world while the autosave target has already moved to the NEW slot. The old world's slot therefore freezes at its last save, and all subsequent progress silently lands in the "new" world. If the player later Loads their old world to get back to it, they roll back every bit of progress made since they pressed Create.

verdicts_joined.title: flush() on tab-close is a no-op unless a debounce is already pending — and coins / XP / gameWon / nightCount are not autosave triggers, so a grind session dies with the tab
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/autosave.js:8 (`flush() { if (timer !== null) { clear(); save(); } }`) + src/App.jsx:234-249 (the trigger predicate) + :251-252 (visibilitychange/beforeunload -> flush)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The comment says 'flush on tab-hide/close', but flush() only fires a PENDING debounce; with no timer armed it does nothing. And the subscribe predicate only watches level, equipment, chests, talentPoints, gameMode, worldBlocks, inventory, questState + the 4 banked aspects. Everything else buildSaveData persists — coins, currentXP, totalXP, gameWon, nightCount, lastRewardedNight, gameTime, playerStats, achievements, spellLevels, attributes, unlockedTalents, selectedBlock, activeSpell — never arms the timer. So if the player's last actions were 'earn coins / gain XP / win the game', nothing is pending and the tab-close flush writes nothing. Correct fix: flush() should save unconditionally (or App should call saveActiveWorld directly on hide), AND the trigger list should cover the persisted surface.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence:
probe4 P14 (real store, exact App.jsx predicate) printed, for each PERSISTED field: coins(addCoins) >>> NO AUTOSAVE; currentXP(grantXP, no level-up) >>> NO AUTOSAVE; gameWon(markGameWon) >>> NO AUTOSAVE; nightCount >>> NO AUTOSAVE; gameTime >>> NO AUTOSAVE; playerStats >>> NO AUTOSAVE; selectedBlock >>> NO AUTOSAVE; spellLevels >>> NO AUTOSAVE; unlockedTalents >>> NO AUTOSAVE; attributes >>> NO AUTOSAVE; achievements >>> NO AUTOSAVE. Controls (worldBlocks / inventory / level) DID schedule.
probe4 P15 (tab-close simulation): after a block-triggered autosave, the player earns 2000 coins and wins the game, then flush() runs -> 'autosave.flush() called (tab hidden / beforeunload). saves = 1' (unchanged) -> 'PERSISTED blob now: coins = 0  gameWon = false' -> '>>> 2000 coins + the WIN survived the tab close? NO — LOST'. Control P16 (timer pending) flushes correctly: blob coins = 777.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: Kill mobs for 40 minutes without levelling up or picking anything up, close the tab — all the XP and coins are gone. Beat the final boss and close the tab — the win is not recorded. Losses are silent and look like the game 'forgot'.

verdict.title: flush() on tab-close is a no-op unless a debounce is pending — and coins/XP/gameWon are not autosave triggers, so a grind session dies with the tab
verdict.reason:
Cited code is real and unfixed on HEAD (1386b5e): autosave.js:8 is verbatim `flush() { if (timer !== null) { clear(); save(); } }`, and the App.jsx:234-249 predicate really does omit coins/currentXP/gameWon/nightCount/gameTime/playerStats/achievements/spellLevels, all of which buildSaveData (saveSchema.js:13-58) persists. I reproduced the claim's isolated probe (real store + real createAutosave + verbatim predicate): poking coins/XP/gameWon directly -> NO AUTOSAVE, and a subsequent flush() wrote nothing (persisted coins=0, gameWon=false). Controls fired (inventory/level -> AUTOSAVED; armed-timer flush persisted coins=777), so the probe was not vacuous.

BUT the claim only tested store setters in a vacuum and never checked what real gameplay does. Every real action that yields coins/XP/a win CO-MUTATES a watched key, which arms the debounce:
(1) Mob kill: QuestSystem.onMobKill (QuestSystem.jsx:302-314) does setStats(prev => ({...prev, kills: prev.kills+1})); the mirror effect at QuestSystem.jsx:134-141 depends on `stats` and writes a BRAND-NEW object literal via setQuestState -> s.questState !== prevS.questState -> arms. Probe P4: armed=YES, tab-close flush persisted currentXP=25.
(2) Coins have exactly two sources: grantDawnReward (useGameStore.jsx:660-672) calls addToInventory -> new inventory ref -> arms (probe P5: persisted coins=10 == live); quest rewards (QuestSystem.jsx:291-292) mutate questState -> arms.
(3) Boss win: bossSystem.js:92-107 calls addToInventory('Crown of the Dragon King') BEFORE markGameWon() -> arms. Probe P6: persisted gameWon=true.
There is only ONE autosave path (grep confirmed: no interval save, no save-on-death), so this co-mutation is the whole story. Probe files were deleted after the run.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None of the claimed impacts occur. "Kill mobs for 40 min without levelling, close tab, XP gone" is false — every kill arms the autosave via the questState stats mirror. "Beat the boss, close the tab, the win is not recorded" is false — the Crown/Dragon Scale drop arms it and gameWon=true persists. "Earn coins, close tab, coins gone" is false — both coin sources (dawn reward, quest reward) arm it.

The only genuine residual is a bounded debounce tail: state changed after the last watched-key change AND after its 5s debounce already fired (e.g. XP from a bare spell cast with no kill) is lost on close. That is seconds of play — the normal cost of any 5s-debounce autosave, not a lost session. Severity HIGH is inflated; this is LOW.

Worth a cheap hardening ticket, not a bug fix: the save is currently correct only by INCIDENTAL co-mutation. If anyone adds a coin source that doesn't touch inventory/quests, or reorders markGameWon() before the Crown drop, the loss becomes real and no test would catch it. Making flush() save unconditionally would remove that latent fragility.

verdicts_joined.title: Loading a versionless / legacy / fresh blob silently inherits the CURRENT character; SAVE_VERSION is written but never read
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/saveSchema.js:9 (SAVE_VERSION = 2) and :61-68 (migrateSaveData does no version dispatch at all) + src/store/useGameStore.jsx:862-883 (`prog?.level ?? state.level` etc. for every progression key)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: The header calls migrateSaveData 'a version-gated migration seam', but it never inspects saveData.version — it only normalizes inventory keys. A v1 (pre-progression) save, a WorldManager freshBlob, or a FUTURE v3 save all load blindly, and every missing key silently falls back to whatever the live store currently holds. That means 'load an old save' quietly grafts your current level/coins/talents/chests/quests onto it rather than restoring or rejecting. verdicts_joined.player_impact: Loading an older save gives a character that is a hybrid of the save and whatever you were just playing — wrong level, wrong coins, ghost chests from another world, quest progress from another run. Silently wrong rather than visibly broken, so it reads as 'the game is buggy'.

verdict.title: Loading a versionless / legacy / fresh blob silently inherits the CURRENT character; SAVE_VERSION is written but never read
verdict.reason:
Cited lines are real and accurate. frontend/src/game/saveSchema.js:9 = `export const SAVE_VERSION = 2`; migrateSaveData (:61-68) never inspects saveData.version — it only calls normalizeInventoryKeys. Repo-wide grep (`grep -rn "migrateSaveData|SAVE_VERSION" frontend/src` + a grep for `.version` reads) shows `version` is WRITTEN at saveSchema.js:15 and READ nowhere in src/ except saveSchema.test.js asserting it was set. The header comment calling it "a version-gated migration seam" is therefore false. useGameStore.jsx:864-881 (inside the cited 862-883) is the `prog?.level ?? state.level` / `?? state.coins` / etc. chain; :948 does the same for questState (`saveData.questState ?? state.questState`); :884 for chests.

RE-RAN THE EVIDENCE MYSELF: wrote my own vitest probe (frontend/src/game/__probe_saveload.test.js, since DELETED — tree left clean) importing the REAL useGameStore and driving loadWorldData. 4/4 passed. Output: P1 v99 save loaded blindly -> level 3 coins 7 (migrateSaveData(v99).version === 99, no rejection). P2 VERSIONLESS save -> level 12, coins 4321, talentPoints 9, chests 1, questState {completed:[slay_10],active:boss_hunt}, nightCount 9 — all inherited from the LIVE character, none from the save. P3, using the VERBATIM freshBlob object literal from WorldManager.createWorld (WorldManager.jsx:73-87) -> blocks 0, blocksPlaced 0, achievements [] (so "fresh" WAS the intent) YET level 12, coins 4321, talentPoints 9, nightCount 9, GHOST chests 1, questState carried over.

NOT ALREADY FIXED: `git status --porcelain` is empty for saveSchema.js, useGameStore.jsx and WorldManager.jsx (so I read/ran HEAD, not a dirty tree). `git show --stat 926751e 15fcc96` — the two fixes landed today (R1/quest-claim, R4/block-ids) — touch none of these three files.

REACHABILITY: WorldManager.jsx:189/193 "Create New World" button -> modal -> :311 onClick=createWorld -> writeWorld(freshBlob) + setActiveWorldId. World card :352 onClick=onLoad -> loadWorld() -> :120 onWorldLoad(worldData) -> MenuSystem.jsx:170 wires that to gameState.loadWorldData. Plain 2-click player flow, no dev flag, no legacy save required.
verdict.real_player_impact:
Real, and reachable today without any legacy save. The claim's headline (SAVE_VERSION never read) is actually its WEAKER half — largely latent, since no player has a v99 save and a v1 save requires a pre-A3 localStorage entry. The live harm is the WorldManager path: createWorld's freshBlob omits `progression`, `chests`, and `questState`, so it trips the `?? state.X` fallback that was written for legacy migration. Player clicks "Create New World", clicks the new world, and lands in a brand-new empty world still carrying their level 12 / 4321 coins / all talents / spell levels / nightCount 9 (so the new world immediately runs night-10 siege intensity), plus ghost chests sitting at coordinates that contain zero blocks, plus completed quests from the previous run.

This is a bug, not a "persistent character across worlds" design choice: freshBlob deliberately zeroes playerStats and achievements, proving a fresh start was intended, yet level/coins/talents/spells/nightCount/chests/quests all survive. That internal incoherence — and especially ghost chests in a blockless world — is indefensible under any design reading.

Severity MEDIUM is honest, not inflated: it is visibly wrong and trivially reachable, but it corrupts no existing save (the old world's slot is untouched) and is not a crash or data-loss bug. Root cause worth naming for the fix: a fallback intended only for legacy-save migration is being hit by a first-class runtime path, and there is no version dispatch to refuse or repair an unreadable blob.

verdicts_joined.title: Save failure is completely silent — quota exhaustion or Safari Private Mode means the game never saves and never says so
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/store/useGameStore.jsx:972 (ignores writeWorld's boolean return) + src/game/worldSaves.js:11-13 (safeGet/safeSet swallow every throw) + :29-38 (writeWorld returns false on a failed write)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: worldSaves.js deliberately returns false on a blocked/full localStorage — and saveActiveWorld throws that signal away, returning undefined. In Safari Private Browsing (and under iOS storage pressure / a full quota) EVERY setItem throws, so the game silently never persists anything for the entire session and the player gets no warning, no toast, no console error. writeWorld's blob-first-then-index ordering is good defensive design that nothing upstream honours.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: probe2 P10 (real store; Storage.prototype.setItem monkeypatched to throw QuotaExceededError): 'saveActiveWorld under a FULL localStorage: returned no-throw; setItem attempts swallowed = 2; worlds in index = 0; active id = null; -> the save silently did nothing; saveActiveWorld returns undefined'. Same probe measured the real blob size so the quota risk is quantified, not guessed: '20,000 player-edited blocks -> blob = 305737 bytes (0.29 MB); blocks affordable at a ~5MB quota ~= 342,966' — so ordinary building will not hit quota, but private mode / storage pressure will.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: iPad/iPhone players in Private Browsing (or with a full origin quota) play a whole session that is never saved, with zero indication. They close the tab and everything is gone.

verdict.title: Save-failure signal is discarded by every caller — a blocked/full localStorage saves nothing, and the manual Save button reports "saved successfully"
verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED (with a stale premise corrected and severity trimmed to LOW-MEDIUM)
verdict.reason:
REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I wrote my own probe (jsdom, real useGameStore + real worldSaves.js, only Storage.prototype.setItem faulted to throw QuotaExceededError). Result: saveActiveWorld did not throw, returned undefined, 2 setItem attempts swallowed, listWorlds()=0, activeId=null. A control case (healthy storage -> 1 world persisted) proves the fault actually reached the output, so this is not a vacuous pass; my first run failed on a bad import and the control caught it. Probe deleted after the run (repo hygiene).

CITED LINES ARE REAL AND ACCURATE ON HEAD (read directly): worldSaves.js:12 `const safeSet = (k,v) => { try { localStorage.setItem(k,v); return true; } catch { return false; } }`; :33 `if (!ok) return false;`; useGameStore.jsx:972 calls writeWorld(...) and discards the boolean. NOT already fixed — HEAD's last commits (1386b5e, 45778e7, a8c7b71) are docs-only and touch neither file; unrelated to the 926751e/15fcc96 quest-claim and block-id fixes.

grep confirms NO caller anywhere checks the return: useGameStore.jsx:972, WorldManager.jsx:52, WorldManager.jsx:92.

CLAIM'S MECHANISM IS PARTLY STALE (verified live, not from memory): "In Safari Private Browsing EVERY setItem throws" was fixed in Safari 11 / 2017 — WebKit bug 157010 RESOLVED FIXED, r215315, Safari Tech Preview 29 notes. Modern Safari private mode allows writes with a reduced quota and wipes on session end (which honoring the boolean would not fix). The still-live throw paths are origin-quota exhaustion (WebKit storage-policy blog, A1: "If the limit is reached, the storage operation ... will fail, and a QuotaExceededError exception will be thrown", and quota "might change based on factors like existing usage and site visit frequency"), storage blocked by browser setting/enterprise policy, and iOS storage pressure/eviction. The claim's own measurement (~343k blocks to fill 5MB) undercuts its own urgency.

CLAIM UNDERSTATES ONE THING: WorldManager.saveCurrentWorld (:55-62) wraps persistLocal() in try/catch, but writeWorld never throws — so the catch at :59 is DEAD and the player is shown "World saved to LocalStorage successfully!" (:58) on a write that stored nothing. That is an active false success, worse than the silence the claim describes. An addNotification toast system already exists (QuestSystem.jsx:161, used by DuskWarning/InputManager); the save path simply never calls it, so the fix surface is already built and the fix is cheap.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real, but narrower and rarer than the claim asserts. Both failing paths are player-reachable: autosave is fully wired (App.jsx:220-260, transition-subscribe + flush on visibilitychange/beforeunload), and WorldManager is reachable via Settings -> "Open World Manager" -> Save World (MenuSystem.jsx:167, GamePanels.jsx:801). When a write fails, autosave says nothing at all, and the manual Save button affirmatively lies ("World saved to LocalStorage successfully!"). A player whose origin quota is exhausted, whose storage is blocked by policy/settings, or who is under iOS storage pressure plays an entire session that is never persisted, is told it WAS saved if they click Save, closes the tab, and loses everything. What does NOT hold is the claim's dramatic framing that this hits every Safari/iPad Private-Browsing player on every write — that stopped being true in 2017. Ordinary building will not hit quota (~343k blocks needed at 5MB, by the claim's own measurement), though multiple accumulated world blobs shorten that. Honest severity is LOW-MEDIUM, not MEDIUM: the defect is genuine and trivially fixable (the boolean signal and the toast system both already exist), but the trigger rate is much lower than the write-up implies.

verdict.title: loadWorldData has no shape validation: a malformed blob either throws a TypeError or writes garbage straight into the store
verdict.reason:
REPRODUCED the code behavior, REFUTED the player path.

(1) Evidence re-run (my own probe test against the real store, since deleted): every claimed shape matched exactly — THREW: null/undefined -> "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'world_data')"; blocks='notanarray' / [1,2,3] -> "Iterator value n is not an entry object"; chests=5 / {a:1} -> "not iterable". ACCEPTED: inventory=5; level="999" -> maxHP=10130 (claim said 10080 — immaterial base-state diff); level=-5; coins=Infinity; position="hax". The claimant did NOT fabricate.

(2) Not fixed on HEAD (1386b5e). file:line is real — useGameStore.jsx:843 `loadWorldData: (rawSaveData) =>` has zero shape guards, only ??/|| fallbacks; saveSchema.js:61 migrateSaveData is a passthrough (`if (!saveData || typeof saveData !== 'object') return saveData`).

(3) REACHABILITY KILLS IT. Sole production path: WorldManager.jsx:114 `readWorld(worldId)` -> :115 `if (!worldData) throw new Error('Local save not found')` -> :119 onWorldLoad. worldSaves.js:23-27 readWorld wraps JSON.parse in try/catch returning null. So a corrupted byte => invalid JSON => null => the :115 guard throws => caught at :125 => graceful "Failed to load world". The claim's null/undefined TypeError cases are UNREACHABLE — the :115 guard fires first.

(4) The silently-accepted half requires valid-JSON-with-wrong-types. No producer exists: buildSaveData (saveSchema.js:13) always serializes correct shapes from the live store; localStorage.setItem is atomic (no partial writes); grep confirms NO zustand persist/rehydrate (plain `create` at useGameStore.jsx:1), NO FileReader/file-import/save-upload (the `Upload` at Components.jsx:53 is an unused lucide icon), and exactly ONE production caller of readWorld. Only a human hand-editing localStorage in DevTools produces it.

(5) The claim's "no repair path / unrecoverable" is FALSE: WorldManager.jsx:359 renders a delete button -> deleteWorld -> deleteWorldSave, so a corrupt slot is removable and other slots still load.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None reachable. The realistic corruption scenario the claim leads with (a flipped byte in localStorage) already lands on the SAFE, fully-handled path: JSON.parse fails inside readWorld -> null -> WorldManager's `if (!worldData) throw` -> caught -> a "Failed to load world" banner, with the corrupt slot deletable from the same UI (WorldManager.jsx:359) and other slots unaffected. That is graceful degradation, not a bug.

The only way to hit the harmful "garbage accepted into the store" half is to deliberately hand-edit localStorage in DevTools to a valid-JSON-but-wrong-typed blob — nothing the game itself can ever write. In a fully client-authoritative, single-player, no-server, no-leaderboard game, that same person can trivially call `useGameStore.setState({level:999})` in the console instead, so the save layer is not a security or integrity boundary and the "attack" is self-inflicted with a strictly easier alternative.

Severity MEDIUM is INFLATED. The residual truth is a defense-in-depth hardening nit (add _numOr/_objOr coercers + a version check, mirroring QuestSystem.jsx:92-93) worth LOW at most — legitimate cleanup, but no player experiences it.

Reachability chain (no page reload anywhere in it): App.jsx:209 (Esc) -> setShowSettings(true) -> GamePanels.jsx:801-805 "World Manager" button -> MenuSystem.jsx:170 `onWorldLoad={gameState.loadWorldData}` -> WorldManager.loadWorld() calls onWorldLoad(worldData) then onClose(). verdict.real_player_impact: Real, player-visible, but gated behind an in-session world load. A player who loads a world from a cold page load sees nothing (live clock is still 0, so `0 || 0` accidentally yields 0). The bug bites when a world is loaded WITHOUT a reload — Esc -> Settings -> World Manager -> Load, which is exactly how a freshly-created world is entered. Because the clock advances 4 units/s and a half-cycle is 600 units, after only 150s (2.5 min) of play the live clock is >=600, so loading a brand-new WorldManager world (whose blob literally says `gameTime: 0`) keeps the old clock and derives isDay = isDayAtUnit(720) = false — the brand-new world starts at NIGHT instead of dawn, and the time of day never resets with the world. Night is load-bearing in this game (siege/nightCount progression), so this is a genuine gameplay consequence, not cosmetic. Severity LOW is honest, arguably slightly under-stated; it is not inflated. One-character fix: `??`.

It is persisted state with no consumer, plus a dedicated store test (tests/store/gameWon.test.js) and an e2e assertion that make the domain look better-covered than it is. Either wire a victory beat to it or delete it.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: grep (executed): `grep -rn --include='*.jsx' 'gameWon' src/ | grep -v store/useGameStore` -> no output. Confirmed in the live browser: the blob carries `"won":true` after markGameWon (SESSION 1 output) yet nothing renders.
verdicts_joined.player_impact: NONE directly — the player can beat the Blight-Heart and see no victory acknowledgement, but that is a missing feature rather than a regression. Flagged because it inflates the apparent test coverage of this domain.
verdicts_joined.domain: Save / load / persistence / migration

verdict.title: gameWon is serialized, restored and commented as a persisted win-state, but nothing in the app reads it
verdict.reason:
The claim's core assertion ("nothing reads gameWon") is false — it is an artifact of the claim's own grep filter. The claim ran `grep -rn --include='*.jsx' 'gameWon' src/`, which only searches .jsx files. The actual consumer is in a .js file: src/world/bossSystem.js:37 — `if (playerLevel < 5 || bossSpawned.current || bossDefeated || useGameStore.getState().gameWon) return;`. An unfiltered `grep -rn "gameWon" src/` surfaces it immediately.

The read is load-bearing, not vestigial. `bossSpawned` (useRef) and `bossDefeated` (useState) in bossSystem.js:10-19 are TRANSIENT — both reset to false on page reload. The save-restored `gameWon` is the ONLY surviving signal that prevents the slain Blight-Heart from re-awakening at the lair after a reload. Full closed loop verified: written at bossSystem.js:107 (`markGameWon()` on the once-only boss-defeat block) -> serialized at saveSchema.js:55 -> restored at useGameStore.jsx:860,923 -> consumed at bossSystem.js:37. Hook is wired live at App.jsx:180 (`useBossSystem(experienceSystem.playerLevel)`).

EXECUTED PROBE (vitest + @testing-library/react, rendered the real useBossSystem hook at blightHeartSite(), playerLevel=5, varying ONLY gameWon):
  [CONTROL]   gameWon=false -> bossActive = true   (dragon awakens; proves the spawn poll fires)
  [TREATMENT] gameWon=true  -> bossActive = false  (beaten dragon stays dead)
  2 passed. Probe file deleted after the run; tree left clean.

The claim's collateral assertions are also false: "no victory screen" — VictoryOverlay exists (src/GameSystems.jsx:223), is rendered at src/HUD.jsx:664-665 on bossDefeated, and fires a victory audio sting (SoundManager.jsx:615). Not already-fixed/stale: HEAD is 1386b5e and the cited lines are present and current as written.
verdict.real_player_impact:
None — there is no defect. The claim itself concedes player_impact NONE, and the code proves the field is actively consumed.

Inverted risk: the claim's remediation ("either wire a victory beat to it or delete it") would INTRODUCE a real player-facing regression. Deleting gameWon would make the beaten Shadow Dragon auto-respawn at the lair on every reload after the player wins — exactly the failure the S9c comment says the field exists to prevent. The store test (gameWon) and e2e assertion the claim dismisses as "inflating apparent coverage" are in fact guarding live behavior. Acting on this finding is net-negative.

verdicts_joined.title: Deleting the world you are currently playing resurrects it as a duplicate on the next autosave
verdicts_joined.file_line: src/game/worldSaves.js:40-44 (deleteWorld clears the active id) + src/store/useGameStore.jsx:970-971 (saveActiveWorld mints a NEW id when none is active)
verdicts_joined.why_it_matters: deleteWorld correctly removes the blob + index entry and nulls the active id, but the live store still holds the whole world. The next trigger-key change mints `local_<Date.now()>` and writes the same world straight back under a new id. Deleting the active world should either also reset the store or suppress autosaves until a world is loaded/created.
verdicts_joined.executed_evidence: probe1 P5 (real store + real worldSaves): 'saved world id = local_1783963418272  worlds = 1' -> deleteWorld -> 'after deleteWorld: worlds = 0  active = null' -> one more autosave -> 'after the next autosave: worlds = 1 ["local_1783963418272"]'. (The id matched only because Date.now() was identical inside the test tick; in real time it mints a fresh id, i.e. a DUPLICATE entry rather than the same one.)
verdicts_joined.player_impact: The player deletes a world, it reappears in the list seconds later. Confusing but not destructive.
verdicts_joined.domain: Save / load / persistence / migration

verdict.title: Deleting the world you are currently playing resurrects it on the next autosave (new id, player's world name lost)
verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Independent probe (src/game/__verify_delete_active.test.jsx, since removed) drove the REAL store + REAL <WorldManager/> component (real red delete button click, window.confirm mocked true) + REAL worldSaves + REAL createAutosave wired with App.jsx:233-249's verbatim transition-key predicate. Output: STEP 1 (playing) active=local_AAA worlds=["local_AAA"] blocks=[["1,2,3",{"type":"diamond"}]] level=12 -> STEP 2 (after real delete click) active=null worlds=[] blob=null -> STEP 3 (clock advanced 30s, player places one more block) worlds=["local_1784023235000"] active=local_1784023235000 name="Save_7/14/2026, 3:00:35 AM" and the resurrected blob carries the DELETED world's content: blocks=[["1,2,3",{"type":"diamond"}],["4,5,6",{"type":"stone"}]] level=12 coins=900. I improved on the claimant's evidence: their id matched only because Date.now() was frozen in-tick (they flagged this honestly); by advancing the system clock I proved the real-time case mints a genuinely NEW id.

(2) NOT already fixed: git status clean for all three files; `git show HEAD:frontend/src/game/worldSaves.js | sed -n 40,44p` and `git show HEAD:frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx | sed -n 967,973p` return the cited code verbatim. Today's fixes (926751e quest-claim, 15fcc96 block-ids) touch unrelated files.

(3) Cites real + accurate: worldSaves.js:40-44 = deleteWorld, ending `if (getActiveWorldId() === id) setActiveWorldId(null);`. useGameStore.jsx:970-971 = `let id = getActiveWorldId(); if (!id) { id = 'local_' + Date.now(); setActiveWorldId(id); }`. No store reset anywhere in WorldManager.deleteWorld (WorldManager.jsx:130-143 — it only calls deleteWorldSave + setWorlds + setError).

(4) Reachability (my strongest refutation attempt, failed): "Manage Worlds" is a button in SettingsPanel (ui/GamePanels.jsx:801-806); App.jsx:107-115 opens SettingsPanel as the IN-GAME PAUSE MENU on pointer-unlock when `s.isAlive && s.gameStarted`. MenuSystem.jsx:167-176's WorldManager onClose even re-locks the pointer `if (gameState.gameStarted)` — the code explicitly anticipates being open mid-game. The autosave useEffect (App.jsx:220-261) ends `}, []);` so the subscription is live for App's whole lifetime.

(5) Severity LOW is honest, arguably understated: not data-destructive (it fails to delete rather than destroying), but unrecoverable in-session — deleting the resurrected entry just mints another on the next transition key.

CORRECTION to the claim: "duplicate" is imprecise. The original entry IS removed; the world returns as a SINGLE new entry with a fresh id and a machine-generated name, silently discarding the player's chosen world name. One entry, not two. The substance (deleted world reappears) is exactly right.
verdict.real_player_impact: Real and reachable via a normal path. Mid-game the player presses ESC -> pause menu -> "Manage Worlds" -> deletes the world they are currently in. The panel confirms "World deleted successfully." They close it, return to the game, and the next time any progression/world key changes (mine or place a block, pick up an item, gain a level, open a chest), the 5s debounced autosave fires, finds no active id, mints `local_<Date.now()>`, and writes the still-live world straight back. The world reappears in the list seconds later under a NEW id with a machine name like "Save_7/14/2026, 3:00:35 AM" — the player's chosen world name is gone. Deleting again does not help: the next block they place mints yet another entry. Effectively the player cannot delete the world they are playing without first leaving the game, and the list accumulates auto-named ghosts on each attempt. Confusing and defeats an explicit, confirmed player action, but not destructive of data.
